assumptions.notes: 買家年行駛 6,000-8,000 km，遠低於台灣平均 12,000-15,000 km。所有檢查點一律用 7,000 km × 年數（7,000／21,000／35,000／49,000／70,000 km）。此里程下 Audi 的保養間隔由「時間」觸發而非里程（原廠 1 年或 15,000 km 先到者為準），所以每年都要進廠一次，年數才是保養成本的主要驅動因子；輪胎同理，會先老化到期而不是磨到底。低里程車在台灣中古市場明顯高於不看里程的平均行情，故各檢查點都以「同年份低里程件」為報價基準，並在 source 字串註明。稅金與保險依規格排除（僅供參考：本車年燃料稅 4,800 元、牌照稅 7,120 元，經 U-CAR 規格表確認，未計入任何欄位）。非電動車，無充電樁安裝成本。特別注意：本車的 48V 系統是輕油電（MHEV），無法純電行駛，powertrain 歸類為 gasoline 而非 hybrid。

purchase.source: 官方建議售價 1,580,000 元，本次獨立複查後確認無誤、未修改。兩個來源逐字驗證：(1) UDN Autos 2025-11-06「2026 年式 Audi A3 Sportback 升級登場」內文明列『30 TFSI 享馭版 建議售價 142 萬元／35 TFSI advanced 進化版 建議售價 158 萬元／35 TFSI S line 運動版 建議售價 182 萬元』；(2) U-CAR 新車頻道 A3 Sportback 規格表印出『35 TFSI advanced進化版 158（萬）／1,498 c.c.／汽油／直列4汽缸／七速自手排／前輪驅動／150 hp／18.6 km/l／燃4,800 牌7,120』。折扣與領牌代辦為市場行情推估，非官方數字。
purchase.notes: 車型全名 Audi A3 Sportback 35 TFSI advanced 進化版，2026 年式（8Y 世代小改款，2025-03-07 在台發表，2026 年式於 2025-11 導入並全車系標配前方橫向車流警示、Park assist plus 自動停車與 360 度環景）。動力為 1,498 c.c. 直列四缸渦輪汽油引擎，150 hp／25.5 kgm，搭配 S tronic 七速雙離合器自手排、前輪驅動，18 吋輪圈為標配。年式價差經來源確認：2025 年式同車型 155 萬（UDN 2025-03-12 試駕報導逐字列出 139／155／179 萬），2026 年式調為 158 萬，+3 萬換得環景與自動停車。【48V 分類說明】本車全車系搭載 48V 輕油電（mild hybrid）系統，屬皮帶式啟動發電機（BSG）架構，只能做怠速熄火、滑行熄火與起步輔助，無法以純電驅動車輛，因此依表格規範歸類為 gasoline，不是 hybrid。折扣 70,000 元的依據：台灣奧迪 2026 年 2 月與 3 月的購車方案均未公布現金折讓，主打低頭款低月付（A3 Sportback 月付 8,888 元起、130 萬 40 期零利率）與五年原廠保固，屬金融讓利而非牌價讓利；但 A3 是台灣 SUV 主導市場中的低量入門掀背，實際成交仍談得到現金加配件的讓利，取 6-9 萬元區間的中位數 7 萬元，屬保守推估。折扣率 4.4%，與本表其他德系入門車一致（BMW 1 Series 4.3%、Mercedes A180 3.6%）。領牌代辦 52,000 元＝領牌規費與驗車約 5,000 元＋代辦費約 10,000 元＋交車配件（行車記錄器、玻璃鍍膜、避光墊、腳踏墊等）約 37,000 元，隨車價級距調整，與本表 Mercedes A180（1,650,000 車價／55,000）同級。稅金與保險依規格排除。real_cost = 1,580,000 - 70,000 + 52,000 = 1,562,000。

selling_costs.notes: 以自售（私下賣給個人）情境估算，對應 value_checkpoints 的 private_sale_price。豪華品牌自售時整備規格要比國產車高一階才賣得動，故美容整備抓 7,500 元。若改走車商收購（dealer_tradein_price），過戶與整備由車商吸收，此筆可視為 0，但售價要用 dealer_tradein_price 那一欄。

value_checkpoints.source: 推估值，非直接掛牌觀察：SUM 汽車網 2026-08-12 全站 8Y 世代 A3 僅 3 筆在架（2022-2023 年份），無 1 年車可比。做法是以已驗證的新車牌價 1,580,000 為上界、以下方 3 年期的實際掛牌行情為下界內插，並套用德系豪華車在台第一年的陡跌特性，得車商零售開價約 1,264,000（牌價 80%）。再依「車商售價 → 自售價」調降 11%（8-15% 區間中位）得自售價 1,125,000，再依「自售價 → 車商收購價」調降 13%（10-15% 區間中位）得收購價 980,000。自售價為 real_cost 的 72.0%，第一年即認列 28% 損失——這正是德系豪華車與日系（同期約 85%）的分水嶺，且與本表德系同級車一致（BMW 1 Series 72.8%、Mercedes A180 70.5%、CLA180 71.0%）。低里程 7,000 km 已納入加成。

以 SUM 汽車網（https://www.sum.com.tw/carsearch/AUDI/A3?v=4）2026-08-12 實際在架車輛換算，全部為同世代（8Y）同車系，本次已逐筆重新抓取並核對無誤：2023 年式 A3 Sportback 1,500 c.c.（26,000 km）車商開價 998,000＝原牌價 1,550,000 的 64.4%；2023 年式 1,000 c.c. 30 TFSI（47,747 km）車商開價 869,000＝原牌價 1,380,000 的 63.0%；2022 年式 1,500 c.c.（66,459 km）車商開價 928,000＝原牌價 1,690,000 的 54.9%。【本次修正】前一版取「區間上緣 67%」，高於全部三個觀測樣本；本案 21,000 km 與最可比樣本（2023 年式 1.5、26,000 km、64.4%）只差 5,000 km，不足以支撐高於所有觀測值的比率，故改取 65.5%（僅較最可比樣本加 1.1 個百分點的低里程加成）→ 車商零售開價約 1,034,900。【關鍵調整】上述皆為車商售價（零售開價），不是車主拿得到的錢：再降 11% 得自售價 920,000，自售價再降 13% 得車商收購價 800,000。自售價為 real_cost 的 58.9%，3 年跌掉四成，符合德系而非日系的曲線，並落在本表德系同級帶（58.3-61.2%）內。樣本僅 3 筆且其中一筆未載明車型等級（以 35 TFSI advanced 原價認列），故給 medium 不給 high。

外推值。可觀察的最遠同世代樣本是 SUM 上的 2022 年式 1,500 c.c.（4 年、66,459 km）＝原牌價 54.9%；本案 5 年僅 35,000 km，里程約為該樣本的一半，先做低里程加成、再多折舊一年，得車商零售開價約牌價 53%（1,580,000 × 53% ≈ 837,400）。再依 -11% / -13% 兩段換算得自售價 745,000、車商收購價 648,000。自售價為 real_cost 的 47.7%，落在本表德系同級帶（43.8-49.4%）內；3→5 年的年跌幅（-6.25 個百分點／年）小於 1→3 年（-7.25 個百分點／年），維持前重後輕的德系形狀。第 5 年是台灣奧迪促銷「五年原廠保固」到期的節點，中古市場會在此處對修理風險重新定價。無 5 年車實際掛牌可比，故 confidence 為 low。

外推值，採前代（8V 世代）保值率換算，因為現行 8Y 世代 2021 年才在台上市，最老僅 5 年，沒有真實的 7 年資料，不虛構。做法：SUM 2026-08-12 在架 2018 年式 A3 Sportback 1,500 c.c.（8 年、110,000 km）車商開價 458,000；該車當年原廠牌價由 UDN Autos 2017-08-02 小改款上市報導驗證為 A3 Sportback 35 TFSI 1,430,000 元（本次已逐字複查該報導，確認 Sportback 35 TFSI 143 萬、35 TFSI Premium 149.9 萬、40 TFSI Sport 177 萬、Sedan 35 TFSI Premium 156 萬），車身型式與動力等級皆對得上，故 8 年高里程保值率＝32.0%（車商零售）。往前推一年（+約 5 個百分點）並針對本案 49,000 km 相對該樣本 110,000 km 的低里程加成（+約 6 個百分點），得 7 年低里程車商零售保值率約 43%。將此比率套用到本車 real_cost 1,562,000 得車商零售開價約 671,700，再依 -11% / -13% 換算得自售價 598,000、車商收購價 520,000。此時已脫離五年原廠保固，中古市場對水泵、節溫器殼、DQ200 機電單元、48V 啟動發電機等的修理風險折價，尾段持續下跌而非像 Lexus 那樣打平。

外推值，同樣採前代（8V 世代）保值率換算，現行世代無 10 年真實資料。【本次修正了一個對照錯誤】前一版把 SUM 在架的『2016 年式 A3 Sedan 1,800 c.c.（111,770 km）開價 398,000』對到 40 TFSI Sport 原牌價 1,770,000 算出 22.5%，但 UDN 2017-08-02 報導中的 177 萬是 A3 **Sportback** 40 TFSI Sport，該報導唯一的 Sedan 是 35 TFSI Premium 156 萬，且 2016 年式車在 2017 年小改款改名前並非以『40 TFSI』販售——車身型式與年式雙重不匹配，該樣本已剔除不用。改以車身型式與動力等級都對得上的單一樣本認列：2017 年式 A3 Sportback 1,500 c.c.（9 年、180,000 km）車商開價 398,000，對 UDN 驗證的 35 TFSI 原牌價 1,430,000 為 27.8%（超高里程）。本案 10 年僅 70,000 km，遠低於該樣本，取低里程加成後的車商零售保值率約 28.5%，套用到 real_cost 1,562,000 得車商零售開價約 445,000，再依 -11% / -13% 換算得自售價 396,000、車商收購價 344,000。自售價僅剩 real_cost 的 25.4%，十年蒸發約 75%——德系豪華車出保後尾段不打平的典型結果，並落在本表德系同級帶（21.0-29.6%）內。剔除誤配樣本後僅剩單一有效樣本，confidence 維持 low。

maintenance.plan_notes: 【口徑】period_cost 為「距上一個檢查點之間」的花費，非累計：1 年＝0-1 年，3 年＝1-3 年，5 年＝3-5 年，7 年＝5-7 年，10 年＝7-10 年。十年合計約 506,000 元（平均約 50,600 元／年）。【本次上修】前一版十年合計 434,000 元，低於本表所有德系同級入門車（Mercedes A180 502,000、CLA180 509,000、BMW 1 Series 530,000、BMW 2 Series GC 592,000），甚至讓 A3 成為全表最便宜的德系豪華車，與 DQ200 乾式雙離合器的實際維修風險不符——前一版只替 DQ200 編列「保養」，完全沒有替機電單元（mechatronic unit）故障編列期望值，而這是台灣 VAG 車主單價最高的已知風險項之一（原廠更換動輒 6-10 萬元）。本次把 3-5、5-7、7-10 三段各上修約 15%，十年合計拉到 506,000 元，與 A180／CLA180 同水位、略低於 1 Series，符合 A3 是德系入門掀背（1.5 升、18 吋、小碟盤）的定位。【間隔由時間決定】年行駛僅 7,000 km，Audi 原廠「1 年或 15,000 km 先到者」的規則下永遠是時間先到，所以每年固定進廠一次，十年共 10 次定保；輪胎也是先老化（約 5-6 年）而非磨耗到期。【保固的正確口徑】UDN 2026-02-13 與 2026-03-10 兩篇報導的原文都是「Audi A3 Sportback **指定車型**主打低頭款、低月付 8,888 元起，並提供五年原廠保固」——五年保固是**促銷專案且限指定車型**，不是全車系標配（台灣奧迪的標準保固為 3 年）。前一版寫成「現行方案標配」屬過度延伸，本次修正。因此 0-3 年幾乎不含故障維修；3-5 年雖多半仍在促銷保固內，仍保留少量非保固項（耗材、內裝、鈑金小項）的提列；第 5 年後兩個期間完全未補貼。兩篇報導均未提及贈送定期保養套餐，故例行保養一律由車主自付。【車型限定】A3 是前驅緊湊掀背，無氣壓懸吊、汽油車無 DPF，故不列這兩項；但列入 EA211 evo 引擎已知的水泵／節溫器殼、點火線圈，DQ200 七速乾式雙離合器的變速箱油、機電單元保養與故障期望值，以及 48V 輕油電專屬的鋰電池與皮帶式啟動發電機（BSG）——後者出保後單價極高，是台灣車主最容易低估的一項。【誠實聲明】audi.com.tw 官方保養價目表與 Mobile01 車主實單討論串在本次研究中均被伺服器拒絕存取（503／403），無法取得逐項原廠報價，因此下列所有金額皆為依台灣豪華品牌原廠廠訂價慣例、並對齊本表德系同級車建模的推估值，全部標記 confidence: low。唯一取得的實價來源是 HOT 保修大聯盟公布的服務工資表（進口車 5,000 km 定保工資 500 元、10,000 km 600 元、20,000 km／1 年 1,500 元，僅工資不含零件、2,000 c.c. 以下），可作為「非原廠通路工資下限」的錨點，原廠實際收費為其數倍。

assumptions.notes: Buyer drives 6,000-8,000 km/year, far below the Taiwan average of ~12,000-15,000 km/year. All checkpoints use assumed_km = 7000 * years (7,000 / 21,000 / 35,000 / 49,000 / 70,000). At this mileage every service interval is TIME-driven, not mileage-driven: the Audi Taiwan schedule is 10,000 km or 12 months whichever comes first, and at 7,000 km/yr the 12-month clock always fires first, so the car gets ~10 annual services in 10 years while the odometer only reaches 70,000 km. Consequence: oil/oil-filter/cabin-filter costs are paid on the calendar, but genuinely mileage-gated items arrive late and some are reached only once — the 60,000 km ATF service lands a single time (around year 9) and the 120,000 km belt service never happens at all. Tyres are replaced on AGE not tread wear (~every 5-6 years). Tax (牌照稅 NT$11,230/yr + 公路養管費 NT$6,180/yr = NT$17,410/yr, confirmed on 8891's own cost page for this exact trim) and all insurance are EXCLUDED by design and appear nowhere in these figures. Fuel is also excluded. Powertrain is conventional gasoline for this table's purposes; see purchase.notes on the unresolved mild-hybrid question, which does not change the classification either way.

purchase.source: Official 建議售價 independently re-verified in a rendered browser on the live 8891 新車 page (https://c.8891.com.tw/audi/a5-sedan/Summary.html): the 2026年式 lineup reads TFSI 110kW advanced 進化版 227萬, TFSI 110kW S line 運動版 239.7萬, TFSI 150kW S line 運動版 268.5萬, and S5 367.1萬, with a headline range of 227-367.1萬. NT$2,270,000 CONFIRMED — no correction needed. Discounts and on-road fees are reasoned estimates, not quoted figures.
purchase.notes: Price confirmed against the live page, not from memory. LINEAGE: the A5 Sedan is Audi's renamed A4 — under the 2024 naming scheme odd numbers denote combustion cars. 8891's discontinued-model page for the A4 Sedan (https://c.8891.com.tw/audi/a4-sedan/Summary.html) confirms this numerically: the final 2024年式 A4 Sedan lineup was 40 TFSI 享馭版 229萬 / 40 TFSI advanced 進化版 230萬 / 40 TFSI S line 運動版 246萬, so the outgoing advanced 進化版 at 230萬 is replaced almost one-for-one by this A5 at 227萬. That makes B9 A4 used data an unusually clean basis for the whole depreciation curve, and it is what the value_checkpoints below are built on. POWERTRAIN: classified gasoline. 8891 groups the 2.0L A5 trims under 汽油 and the S5 3.0 under 油電混合. NOTE THE CAVEAT: that tagging is NOT a reliable spec source — the same site tags the outgoing B9 A4 40 TFSI, which does carry a mild-hybrid, as 油電混合 2.0L. Audi Taiwan's own spec page returns HTTP 503 and 8891's Spec.html returns HTTP 500, both reproduced on this pass, so whether the Taiwan-spec 110 kW 2.0 TFSI carries 12V or 48V MHEV hardware could NOT be confirmed. This does not affect the field: a 48V mild hybrid cannot move the car on battery alone and is 'gasoline' for this table regardless. No 48V starter-generator replacement is costed in maintenance, which is the one place the open question bites. DISCOUNTS: NT$90,000 (~4% of list) is a realistic negotiated package, not a quote. Audi Taiwan's incentives on this car as shown in the 廠商優惠 block on the 8891 page are financing-led — 低頭款、首年低月付6999元起 or 最高180萬48期0利率(指定車型), plus 5年保固(指定車型) — rather than deep cash cuts, which is the classic profile of a car moved on terms rather than on price. A separate 汰舊換新 再減5萬 scrappage rebate is advertised but requires scrapping a qualifying old car, so it is deliberately NOT included. ON-ROAD FEES: NT$66,000 = 領牌 + 代辦 ~NT$16,000 (statutory portion is trivial — 牌照費 600, 行車執照費 200, per the same 8891 cost page — the rest is dealer agency fee) plus ~NT$50,000 of typical delivery accessories at this class (mats, window film, coating, dashcam). Tax and insurance excluded per spec.

selling_costs.notes: Assumes a private sale (自售), consistent with private_sale_price being the headline figure. A German luxury sedan needs proper pre-sale detailing to reach a private price at all, so prep sits at the higher end. Total is mid-range of the 6,000-15,000 typical for this class. If the owner trades in to a dealer instead, most of these costs disappear but the realised price drops to dealer_tradein_price, which is by far the larger effect.

value_checkpoints.source: CORRECTED DOWN from a prior estimate of 1,740,000. Same-generation listings on 8891 中古車 (https://auto.8891.com.tw/audi/a5-sedan) show nine 2025款 A5 Sedan TFSI 150kW S line cars at 219.8萬 (15,000 km), 223.8萬 x2 (10,100 km), 228.8萬 x4 (6,000-6,584 km) and one 電洽 — all 奧迪原廠認證中古車 (CPO) — i.e. low-mileage cars matching this buyer's profile, asking roughly 85-88% of their model-year list. Those numbers are NOT usable at face value for three compounding reasons: (a) they are CPO dealer RETAIL asking prices, the very top of the price chain, carrying a warranty-backed premium; (b) they are the higher 150kW S line trim, and cheaper trims retain a lower percentage; (c) the A5 only launched in Taiwan in June 2025, so with nine used cars in the entire country the price is inflated by launch scarcity that will have faded by the time this buyer's own car is one year old. The direct predecessor contradicts them decisively: on https://auto.8891.com.tw/audi/a4-sedan a 2024-registered A4 40 TFSI advanced 進化版 with 5,000 km asks 118.8萬 (51.7% of its 230萬 list) and 2024-registered 享馭版 cars ask 129.8-147.0萬 (57-64%) at two years. A year-1 dealer retail of 87% followed by a year-2 of ~60% is not a curve. ADJUSTMENT MADE: dealer retail set at 80% of list (1,816,000), cut 11% to private sale (1,620,000), a further 13% to dealer trade-in (1,400,000). No asking price was copied. Includes a small low-mileage allowance (7,000 km).

CORRECTED DOWN from a prior estimate of 1,230,000, which rested on rejecting the only mileage-matched real data point. Predecessor listings on https://auto.8891.com.tw/audi/a4-sedan for 2023-registered A4 40 TFSI 享馭版 (list 229萬): three separate Taichung dealers ask 108.8萬 at 20,000 km (47.5% of list), one asks 129.8萬 at 18,000 km (56.7%), and one Audi CPO car with just 1,000 km asks 139.8萬 (61.0%). The prior pass discarded the 108.8萬 point as accident-history stock because one dealer's boilerplate reads 瑕疵案件皆可全額貸款 — but that is a financing pitch ('we can arrange full financing even on defect cases'), not a disclosure about that car, and the same 108.8萬 / 20,000 km price recurs across three independent listings. The 139.8萬 car is a 1,000 km delivery-mileage outlier, not comparable to a 21,000 km car. The honest 3-year band for a normally-used example is therefore 47.5-56.7% of list. ADJUSTMENT MADE: dealer retail set at 53% (1,203,000) — mid-band, with a slight uplift because the A4 was a run-out model being displaced by this very A5, which depresses its residual specifically — then cut 11% to private sale (1,070,000) and a further 13% to trade-in (930,000). No separate low-mileage uplift is applied: the comparison cars are already at 18,000-20,000 km against our 21,000 km, so adding one would double-count. Years 1-3 are the steepest part of a German luxury curve and this is deliberately far below Japanese-brand behaviour. 8891's own model for this trim (https://c.8891.com.tw/audi/a5-sedan/cost.html) claims 70.5% at year 3 (160.0萬); rejected — see the year-7 note for the back-test that fails it.

CORRECTED DOWN from a prior estimate of 840,000, which missed a directly age- AND mileage-matched listing. On https://auto.8891.com.tw/audi/a4-sedan a 2021-registered A4 40 TFSI S line 運動版 with 35,000 km asks 91.8萬 — exactly this checkpoint's five years and exactly its 35,000 km — which is ~37.9% of that trim's ~242萬 list. That is a far better anchor than interpolating back from six-year cars, and it lands below the 42% dealer retail used previously. Corroborating six-year points from the same page: 2020-registered 40 TFSI at 73.8萬 (50,000 km) and 78.8萬 (84,000 km), ~33-35% of their ~225萬 list. ADJUSTMENT MADE: dealer retail set at 38.5% of list (874,000) — a touch above the observed 37.9% because the A4 S line was by then a run-out model — then cut 11% to private sale (780,000) and a further 14% to dealer trade-in (670,000). No extra low-mileage uplift: the anchor listing already carries this buyer's mileage. Ratio applied to this car's list price per the predecessor-generation method.

EXTRAPOLATED — no genuine 7-year data exists for this generation, which only launched in Taiwan in June 2025. Method: took real predecessor-generation (B9 A4 Sedan) listings at that age from https://auto.8891.com.tw/audi/a4-sedan, expressed them as a retention ratio of that car's original list, and applied the ratio here. Eight-year points: 2018-registered 40 TFSI Premium Plus at 51.8萬 (130,000 km) and 40TFSI at 52.5萬 (128,000 km), ~23% of their ~225萬 list. Nine-year points: 2017-registered 40 TFSI cars cluster at 48.8-60.8萬 (35,000-170,000 km), ~22-27%. Six-year points sit at ~33-35%. Interpolating to seven years and allowing ~+2 points for genuinely low mileage (49,000 km against a typical ~91,000 km) gives 30% of list as dealer retail (681,000), then a 13% cut to private sale (595,000) and a further 14% to trade-in (510,000). Note 8891's own model (https://c.8891.com.tw/audi/a5-sedan/cost.html) claims 50.5% at year 7; REJECTED, because applied to real 8-year-old A4s it would predict ~105萬 against actual asking prices of ~52萬 — roughly 2x optimistic in the tail. The car is out of warranty here and the used market prices in repair risk, so the curve keeps falling rather than flattening.

EXTRAPOLATED from the predecessor generation — no 10-year data can exist for a car launched in 2025. Real B9/B8.5 A4 Sedan listings at that age on https://auto.8891.com.tw/audi/a4-sedan: 2016-registered 30 TFSI 1.4L at 38.8萬 (150,000 km) and 40.0萬 (130,000 km) and 35 TFSI 1.4L at 36.8萬 (90,000 km) — ~19-22% of their ~180-190萬 original list at ten years; 2015-registered 25 TFSI cars at eleven years are already down to 23.9-27.8萬 (~15%). An independent same-nameplate tail check: the one old A5 on the A5 page, a 2014 A5 45TFSI quattro with 130,000 km, asks 33.8萬 — roughly 12-13% of its original list at twelve years. I expressed the ten-year figures as a retention ratio of original list and applied it here, uplifted for very low mileage (70,000 km against a typical ~130,000 km, a large gap at this age), giving 21% of list as dealer retail (477,000), then a 15% cut to private sale (405,000) and a further 15% to trade-in (345,000). The tail keeps declining rather than flattening the way a Lexus does, because a 10-year out-of-warranty Audi is priced on repair risk.

maintenance.plan_notes: Grounded in Audi Taiwan's OFFICIAL published service-price table at https://service-pricing.audi-service.com.tw (title 保養透明 安心啟航), whose public API I queried directly on this pass: /api/v1.0/pricing for per-interval prices and /api/v1.0/service-matrix for exact service content. The matrix was read line by line and confirms: 原廠引擎機油 + 機油濾清器 + 華司與油封 + 粉塵濾清器 at EVERY 10,000 km service; 煞車油 (brake fluid) and 火星塞 (spark plugs) every 20,000 km; 空氣濾清器 (air filter) every 30,000 km; 自動變速箱油 (ATF) + Sealing Plug at 60,000 and 120,000 km; V型皮帶/綜合皮帶 + 皮帶調整器 only at 120,000 km. Verified reference prices from that table — A4 Sedan 40 TFSI (the direct predecessor engine, 2017/2018/2020 model years, all identical): 8,600 basic / 9,600 at the 20,000 km interval / 10,700 at 30,000 km / 21,500 at the 60,000 km ATF service. A5 Sportback 40 TFSI is materially dearer: 11,200-11,800 basic / 13,600 / 29,700-30,700 at 60,000 km. CAVEAT ON THE BASIS, stated plainly: the table only covers 2017-2022 cars and contains no B10 A5 Sedan at all, so every figure below is an extrapolation across both model and time. I retained the dearer A5 Sportback figures uplifted ~15% to 2026 money (~13,500 basic, ~15,500 when brake fluid and plugs fall due, ~34,000 for the 60,000 km ATF service) rather than the cheaper A4 Sedan ones. That is a deliberately conservative choice justified by the new PPC platform, not by lineage — on lineage alone the A4 Sedan's 8,600 basic would be the closer analogue and the scheduled total would fall roughly NT$35,000 over ten years. Because of this the year-1 and year-3 confidences are 'medium', not 'high': the table is real and official but it does not cover this car. TIMING IS THE KEY POINT: at 7,000 km/yr the annual clock always beats the 10,000 km trigger, so the owner pays for ~10 services in 10 years while only reaching 70,000 km — the ATF service lands once (around year 9), spark plugs about three times, and the 120,000 km belt service never at all. WARRANTY: Audi Taiwan promotes 5年保固 under 廠商優惠 on the 8891 A5 Sedan page, which is why years 1-5 carry routine servicing only and no repair allowance — a warranty covers repairs but never routine maintenance or wear items. It is flagged 指定車型, so if the real cover is 3 years the year-5 and year-7 periods should each rise by roughly NT$15,000-25,000. Periods 7 and 10 carry the FULL unsubsidised out-of-warranty cost, including realistic EA888-family risk items: water pump and thermostat housing, ignition coils, PCV/valve cover, plus suspension bushings and control arms, a well-known 8-10 year expense on German sedans in Taiwan. Air suspension is deliberately NOT costed — this trim rides on steel springs. No 48V starter-generator is costed either; note this rests on the unconfirmed mild-hybrid question in purchase.notes, and is the one line item that would need adding if 48V hardware turns out to be fitted. Ten-year total ~NT$414,000 (~NT$41,400/yr), several times a comparable Japanese sedan, driven by Audi dealer labour rates, premium tyres and out-of-warranty risk.

Second 12V battery and misc electrics
checkpoints.source: The 60,000 km service is priced directly from the Audi Taiwan official table (https://service-pricing.audi-service.com.tw), which lists 29,700-30,700 for the A5 Sportback 40 TFSI at that interval (uplifted to ~34,000 for 2026); its service matrix confirms 自動變速箱油 + Sealing Plug as the content that makes that interval expensive. The wear and risk items are an actuarial allowance at Taiwan dealer rates, not a quotation — this is the least certain period and where German ownership diverges most sharply from Japanese. assumptions.notes: 7,000 km/year assumed at every checkpoint (7k/21k/35k/49k/70k), far below the TW average of 12,000-15,000 km. At this mileage every service trigger is calendar-based, not distance-based, and tyres age out before they wear out. Low mileage also means resale sits at the TOP of the observed listing band for its age, which is how the value checkpoints were positioned. EXCLUDED BY DESIGN: 牌照稅/燃料稅 and insurance. ALSO EXCLUDED: home charger installation — a 7kW wallbox plus 專線 runs roughly NT$40,000-70,000 in Taiwan and is a real ownership cost, but it is a one-off capital item, not maintenance, so it appears nowhere in this record. Public DC fast-charging fees and electricity are likewise excluded (energy, not maintenance). SPEC FACTS RE-VERIFIED BY THIS AUDIT against the U-CAR spec table (fetched 2026-08-12 with a browser user-agent; the plain fetcher gets HTTP 403): the 280萬 column shows 車重 2,175 kg, 輪胎尺寸 235/45 R20 front and 後輪尺寸 265/40 R20 rear, 四輪碟煞, 後置馬達 1 具 永磁同步馬達, 電池總容量 83kwh / 可用電池容量 75.8kwh, DC 充電最大功率 225kW, DC 規格 CCS2, AC 規格 Mennekes (Type2), 風阻係數 0.21, 產地 德國, 經銷/代理 台灣福斯股份有限公司. 286 hp / 44.4 kgm comes from U-CAR's article text for this variant. TYRE-SIZE CAVEAT ADDED BY THIS AUDIT: U-CAR contradicts itself. The per-trim SPEC TABLE gives the 280萬 car staggered 20-inch tyres (235/45 R20 / 265/40 R20), but U-CAR's own article text on the same model page states 「A6 e-tron 入門車型標配了 19 吋胎圈組，S line 車型與 S 車型則是 20 吋胎圈組」. This record keeps the spec-table figure because it is the per-trim column, but the two tyre line items in maintenance should be read as an UPPER BOUND — a 19-inch set would be materially cheaper, and 19-inch fitments are more often square (rotatable) than staggered. The staggered assumption is therefore the conservative one. This trim does NOT have air suspension — ETtoday (verified) states 主動式氣壓懸吊 is standard only on the S6 — so no air-strut replacement is budgeted, which is the single biggest reason this car's later maintenance is lower than a comparable German air-sprung SUV.

purchase.source: List price INDEPENDENTLY RE-VERIFIED by this audit, not merely copied. Both U-CAR pages were re-fetched on 2026-08-12 with a browser user-agent. The overall page header reads 「3 車型 280 - 480 萬」 and its model table lists exactly three TW Sportback trims: Sportback e-tron 280萬 (純電動, 後輪驅動), Sportback e-tron performance 340萬 (純電動, 後輪驅動), S6 Sportback e-tron 480萬 (純電動, 四輪驅動). The SPEC page repeats the same three columns at 280 / 340 / 480 萬 and ties the 280萬 column to the 83kWh / 75.8kwh pack, confirming the 280萬 car is the 單馬達後驅 entry variant this record prices. NT$2,800,000 CONFIRMED — 0% deviation from the researcher's figure, no correction made. 8891's new-car page title reads 「2026 Audi A6 Sportback e-tron 價格車款介紹」, independently confirming 2026 is the model year on sale (its body is JavaScript-rendered, so no price was readable there). Discounts and on-road fees are estimates, reasoned in notes, not quoted figures.
purchase.notes: POWERTRAIN: pure BEV, correctly classified. The U-CAR spec table shows 動力系統 電動 / 能源 電能, a single rear 永磁同步馬達, 後輪驅動, and a COMPLETELY EMPTY 引擎系統 section (no 排氣量, 缸徑, 衝程, 引擎型號, 引擎最大馬力). There is no combustion engine and no 48V question — 'bev' is right, not 'hybrid' or 'phev'. PRICE HISTORY — CORRECTED BY THIS AUDIT. The researcher wrote that 280萬 is 'the post-adjustment 2026年式 figure, up from the 275萬 pre-sale, and buys more equipment'. That conflates two different cars. ETtoday (2025-09-01, re-fetched and read in full by this audit) describes the pre-sale lineup as 6 車型 spanning 275-495萬 and states 「標準款A6 e-tron採單馬達後輪驅動，分別輸出最大馬力326匹與381匹」 — i.e. the 275萬 pre-sale entry car was a 100kWh, 326hp variant. U-CAR states the 83kWh car is a LATER ADDITION: 「後續追加推出的入門車型，也就是單馬達後驅、以 e-tron 為名的版本，則是配置了總容量 83kWh、實際可用 75.8kWh 的鋰電池組」, with 286匹 and 44.4 公斤米. So 280萬 is not 275萬 plus equipment; it is a new, smaller-battery, lower-output entry trim added below the original range. The 2026 新年式 revision itself IS real and correctly reported: U-CAR states 「Audi Taiwan 在 2026 下半年時，藉由新年式的調整，除價格變動之外也做出配備提升，將原先亞洲市場都沒有提供的主動式車道維持功能，列為全車系標配之外，也將抬頭顯示器列為標配」, and that the 10.9 吋副駕駛座專屬螢幕 was standard from launch. DISCOUNT (180,000, 6.4%): estimate, not a quoted deal. German brands discount in Taiwan and discount harder on slow sellers, and the used-market evidence below shows Audi BEVs barely trade at all here. Audi Taiwan also runs an official 舊換新方案. 6.4% sits inside the 4.9-7.3% band used for comparable German BEVs in this table (BMW i4 5.4%, BMW iX2 4.9%, Mercedes EQE 6.9%, BMW i5 7.3%), so it was reviewed and LEFT UNCHANGED; audi.com.tw returned HTTP 503 on every attempt, so no official promotion page could be quoted either way. ON-ROAD FEES CORRECTED BY THIS AUDIT: 60,000 raised to 75,000. At 2.1% of list the researcher's figure was the lowest of any German BEV in this table, while same-class peers run 2.4-3.2% (BMW i4 at 279萬 uses 70,000 = 2.5%; BMW iX3 at the identical 280萬 uses 85,000 = 3.0%; Mercedes EQE 2.4%; BMW i5 3.2%). 45,000 of dealer-fitted 配件 is thin at this class, where 隔熱紙 alone runs 20,000-35,000 before 行車紀錄器, 鍍膜, 踏板 and 腳踏墊. 75,000 = 領牌+代辦 roughly 15,000 plus roughly 60,000 of 配件, which is 2.7% of list — mid-band for the peer group. BEVs are exempt from 貨物稅, but that is already inside the list price and is not a fee; tax and insurance are excluded by design. real_cost = 2,800,000 - 180,000 + 75,000 = 2,695,000.

value_checkpoints.source: EXTRAPOLATED, and REDUCED BY THIS AUDIT from the researcher's 1,950,000. The absence of data is itself the finding and was independently re-confirmed: fetching https://auto.8891.com.tw/audi/a6-sportback-e-tron on 2026-08-12 returns 「共找到 1180 輛車」 — the model filter falls through to the entire all-Audi inventory, i.e. not one A6 e-tron of any age is listed anywhere in Taiwan. The nearest real German-BEV anchor was also re-verified listing by listing: 8891 shows five Audi Q4 e-tron, all 2024 cars at about 2 years old on 5,300-18,000 km, dealer asking 143.8 / 148.0 / 158.0 / 158.0 / 176.8 萬. WHY THE CUT: the researcher worked back from those to a year-1 dealer asking of 220萬, which is 78.6% of list — the highest first-year retention of any German BEV in this table (BMW i4 72%, BMW i5 71%, BMW iX3 69%, Mercedes EQE 67%) — while simultaneously arguing, correctly, that Audi BEVs have the THINNEST used demand of the group. A car with literally zero used-market presence cannot out-retain the i4. The researcher's own reading of the Q4 anchor (Audi BEVs asking well under two-thirds of list at 2 years) implies roughly 74-76% of list at year 1, i.e. a dealer asking price near 211萬, not 220萬. ADJUSTMENT CHAIN APPLIED (8891 prices are 車商售價, dealer RETAIL, never what an owner receives): dealer retail 2,110,000 → private sale 1,880,000 (10.9% below, inside the 8-15% band) → dealer trade-in 1,630,000 (a further 13.3% below private). Implies a 30.2% first-year loss against real_cost, squarely in the peer range (i4 28.0%, i5 29.0%, iX3 30.7%, EQE 33.5%) and correctly front-loaded for a German BEV. The 7,000 km odometer is already credited — without it this would sit lower.

EXTRAPOLATED between two anchors that this audit re-fetched and verified line by line, since no A6 e-tron of this age exists anywhere. Upper anchor: 8891 Audi Q4 e-tron, five listings, 2024 cars at about 2 years, 5,300-18,000 km, dealer asking 143.8-176.8萬. Lower anchor: 8891 Audi Q8 e-tron, only two listings in the whole country — 「Audi Q8 e-tron 2024款 e-tron 55Q 純電」 2023年, 1.9萬公里, asking 208.0萬, and 「2024款 50 quattro advanced 進化版」 2024年, 7000公里, asking 198.8萬. Both confirm the years 1-3 slide continues hard with no plateau. Placing this car on that trajectory at 3 years gives a dealer asking price near 160萬. ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: dealer retail 1,600,000 → private sale 1,420,000 (11.3% below) → dealer trade-in 1,240,000 (12.7% below private). At 52.7% of real_cost this sits just under the BMW i4 at the same age (55.4%), which is the right relative position given Audi's thinner demand. The low 21,000 km is worth a few points against these comparators and is already reflected.

Strongest evidence point in this record, and every listing was RE-FETCHED AND CONFIRMED VERBATIM by this audit on 2026-08-12 from https://auto.8891.com.tw/audi/e-tron-sportback — the direct BEV predecessor. The page reads 「共找到 10 輛車」, the entire national supply, of which 8 carry prices and 2 read 電洽: 55 quattro S line asking 147.8萬 (2022年, 5萬公里), 147.8萬 (2022年, 5.8萬公里), 148.8萬 x2 (2021年, 4.14萬公里); 50 quattro S line asking 115.9萬 (2022年, 8.9萬公里) and 123.8萬 x3 (2022年, 2.7-2.8萬公里). SUM independently corroborates: https://www.sum.com.tw/carinfo-777056.php resolves to a live page titled 「AUDI e-tron Sportback 2022年 優惠價 149.8萬」, and https://www.sum.com.tw/carinfo-780646.php to 「AUDI E-TRON GT 2022年 優惠價 228.8萬」; 8891 shows the same e-tron GT generation at 218.8萬 / 5.5萬公里. CONFIDENCE DOWNGRADED BY THIS AUDIT from medium to low. The absolute used prices are hard and re-verified, but converting them to a level for THIS car requires a retention ratio whose denominator — the e-tron Sportback 55's original TW list price — could not be sourced by the researcher and could not be sourced by this audit either (every general search engine reachable from this environment blocked automated queries, and U-CAR has no reachable model page for the discontinued car). A ratio resting on an unverified denominator does not meet the medium bar, whatever the quality of the numerator. Working assumption unchanged: an original list in the 350-390萬 band puts dealer asking at 4-5 years near 38-42% of list; applying that to this car's real_cost and crediting our 35,000 km against those comparators' 41,000-89,000 km gives a dealer asking price near 120萬. ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: dealer retail 1,200,000 → private sale 1,060,000 (11.7% below) → dealer trade-in 920,000 (13.2% below private). Year 5 is also the exact month the 5-year/100,000 km vehicle warranty expires, which the used market prices in.

EXTRAPOLATED from predecessor-generation ratios per the newer-than-10-years rule — no current-generation A6 e-tron will exist at 7 years until 2032. Two predecessor families were used, and the SUM anchors were re-fetched and confirmed by this audit. ICE reference for shape: SUM's Audi search lists 「AUDI A6 AVANT C8 2019年, 2000cc, 107000公里, 桃園市 冠威汽車, 159.8萬」 and an A8 at 158.9萬 (3000cc, 47,860 km); 8891 shows an A6 Sedan C8 2021 40 TFSI Technik at 82.9萬 on 124,900 km — combustion A6s hold roughly half of original list at 7 years. BEV reference for level: the e-tron Sportback data above is already only about 40% of list at 4-5 years, i.e. a German BEV runs roughly 12-15 percentage points behind its combustion equivalent at the same age, and the gap widens rather than closes. Applying the BEV-adjusted ratio to real_cost gives a dealer asking price near 83萬. ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: dealer retail 830,000 → private sale 730,000 (12.0% below) → dealer trade-in 630,000 (13.7% below private). Partly cushioned: the 8-year/160,000 km battery warranty — sourced verbatim, see below — is still live at year 7, which is the only reason this is not lower.

EXTRAPOLATED from predecessor-generation retention ratios — no 10-year data can exist for this car. Anchors from SUM's Audi listings, all large German luxury at extreme age: A8 3.0 V6 from 2011 (15 years, 194,500 km) asking just 19.9萬; A7 Sportback 3.0 TFSI 2011 (15 years, 127,000 km) asking 33.0萬; A6 C7 2011 asking 19.8萬 (176,020 km) and 49.8萬 (132,865 km); A6 Avant C7 2014 (12 years, 213,253 km) asking 35.8萬. Big German luxury cars in Taiwan do NOT flatten out the way a Lexus does — the tail keeps falling because the used market prices in out-of-warranty repair risk. Expressed as a ratio of those cars' original list prices and applied to real_cost, then discounted further for three BEV-specific factors: the 8-year battery warranty has EXPIRED by year 10, replacement-pack risk is unquantifiable to a private buyer, and two further generations of EV will have launched by 2036. That gives a dealer asking price near 45萬. ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: dealer retail 450,000 → private sale 390,000 (13.3% below) → dealer trade-in 320,000 (17.9% below private — a wider cut than earlier checkpoints, because dealers take on an out-of-warranty EV only at a price that covers battery risk, and many simply decline). Curve check after this audit's year-1 correction: private sale runs 1,880,000 → 1,420,000 → 1,060,000 → 730,000 → 390,000, period losses of 815k / 460k / 360k / 330k / 340k. Front-loaded as required, and the tail does NOT flatten — the year 7-10 loss slightly exceeds the year 5-7 loss.

maintenance.plan_notes: HONESTY FIRST: no Audi Taiwan EV service price table and no owner receipt could be obtained, by the researcher or by this audit. audi.com.tw returns HTTP 503, myaudi.tw and audi-service.com.tw are JavaScript-rendered with no pricing, Mobile01 search returns HTTP 403, SUM's 保養工資查詢 sits behind a script, and every general search engine reachable from this environment (Bing, DuckDuckGo, Mojeek, Startpage, Ecosia, Brave, Yandex, three SearxNG instances) blocked automated queries. The ONE hard fact is the warranty, quoted verbatim in a live 8891 Q4 e-tron listing title and re-confirmed by this audit: 「Q4 e-tron 45/原廠新車保固5年10萬公里 電池保固8年16萬公里」 — 5 years/100,000 km vehicle, 8 years/160,000 km battery. Every cost figure below is a reasoned estimate at Audi Taiwan dealer labour rates, NOT a quoted price, and every checkpoint is therefore marked low confidence. STRUCTURAL FIX BY THIS AUDIT: the researcher's third checkpoint was labelled years 3 — a duplicate of the second — while carrying assumed_km 35,000 and a source string that reads 'Covers years 3-5'. It is the year-5 checkpoint and has been relabelled years 5, restoring the required 1/3/5/7/10 ladder and the assumed_km = 7000 * years rule. INTERVAL IS TIME-DRIVEN, NOT MILEAGE-DRIVEN: at 7,000 km/year this car reaches only 70,000 km in ten years, so no distance trigger ever fires — servicing is annual by the calendar, brake fluid is every two years by the calendar, and tyres are replaced because the rubber hardens with age, not because the tread is gone. WHAT A BEV SAVES: no engine oil, no spark plugs, no coil packs, no thermostat housing, no DPF, no 48V starter-generator, and regenerative braking means pads barely wear. WHAT IT DOES NOT SAVE, and why this is nowhere near a RAV4: Audi dealer labour rates apply unchanged; the car weighs 2,175 kg (spec table, re-verified) and its spec-table fitment is staggered 235/45 R20 front / 265/40 R20 rear, which cannot be rotated, so all four go together at premium prices; brake fluid and battery-circuit coolant still need changing; the 12V battery still dies on schedule; and low annual mileage plus Taiwan's humidity actively CORRODES brake discs that regen never scrubs clean, so discs get replaced for rust rather than wear. TYRE CAVEAT (added by this audit): U-CAR's article text says the entry trim's standard fitment is 19-inch, contradicting its own per-trim spec table. The two tyre line items below are priced on the 20-inch staggered assumption and are therefore an UPPER BOUND; on 19-inch square tyres they would be lower and rotation would become possible. Out of warranty the BEV-specific risk items are real money: electric coolant pump for battery thermal management, DC-DC converter, on-board charger and charge port, air-conditioning compressor (which on a BEV also serves battery cooling and therefore runs far more than on a combustion car), and control modules. NO AIR SUSPENSION on this trim — ETtoday, re-verified, states 「S6 e-tron 標配主動式氣壓懸吊」 and nothing equivalent for the standard car — so no air-strut budget, which is the main reason this is cheaper late-life than an air-sprung German SUV. PREPAID PACKAGES: Audi Taiwan does market prepaid service packages and its 舊換新方案, and a package is commonly bundled into a deal at this price point. No free package is assumed — the years 0-1 and 1-3 figures are the unsubsidised numbers. If a package is bundled, years 1 and 3 fall toward zero, but the years 5, 7 and 10 periods already carry the FULL unsubsidised cost and would not change. Ten-year total is NT$601,000 (8,000 + 32,000 + 116,000 + 155,000 + 290,000), roughly double a RAV4 and consistent with the German BEV peers in this table (BMW i4 519,000, Mercedes EQE 573,000, BMW iX3 528,000, BMW i5 825,000).

This is the out-of-warranty cliff: the sourced 5-year/100,000 km vehicle warranty has expired, though the 8-year/160,000 km battery warranty still holds. Two things drive the jump. First, brake discs — at 7,000 km/year with regenerative braking the pads are barely touched, but the discs corrode in Taiwan's humidity and get replaced for rust, roughly 55,000 for discs and pads all round on 四輪碟煞 (spec table). Second, a genuine repair allowance of about 60,000, because from year 5 the owner pays for the electric coolant pump, air-conditioning compressor, DC-DC converter and control modules rather than the warranty. A German car at this age does not stay at Japanese-brand service cost.

Everything is now out of warranty: the sourced 8-year/160,000 km battery warranty expires during this window, so from year 8 the owner carries traction-battery and power-electronics risk outright. Contains the second tyre set (about 85,000, again age-driven at roughly 5-6 years after the year-5 set, and again an upper bound on the 20-inch assumption), a second 12V battery, high-voltage battery coolant service, and a repair allowance near 130,000 for the items that actually fail on a 10-year-old German BEV — electric coolant pump, on-board charger and charge port, DC-DC converter, air-conditioning compressor and suspension arms. assumptions.notes: Checkpoints use assumed_km = 7000 * years (7000/21000/35000/49000/70000), the midpoint of the 6,000-8,000 km/yr profile and roughly half the Taiwan average. At this mileage servicing is TIME-driven, not mileage-driven: Audi Taiwan's schedule is annual with a secondary kilometre trigger that 7,000 km/yr never reaches, so every checkpoint carries exactly one paid visit per year and consumables age out rather than wear out. (The scout quoted that trigger as '10,000 km within 12 months'; the exact figure could not be re-verified on Audi Taiwan's service site, but the conclusion is unaffected at any trigger from 10,000 km upward.) Tax (approx 17,410/yr = 11,230 licence + 6,180 fuel fee) and all insurance are EXCLUDED by design. IMPORTANT CORRECTION TO THE SCOUT'S LOW-MILEAGE PREMIUM CLAIM: the scout asserted that same-year 2023 A6s ask 148-150万 at 35,000-47,000 km but 188万 at 12,300 km, and used that ~20-point spread to push every checkpoint toward the top of its band. The 188万 / 12,300 km car is a 2024 40 TFSI S line, NOT a 2023 - it is a year younger and a higher trim, so that spread is age and trim, not mileage. Inside a genuinely same-year set the mileage premium is approximately zero: a 2023 40 TFSI Technik with 4,714 km asks 148.0万 while a 2023 40 TFSI Technik with 35,000 km asks 149.0万 - the lower-mileage car asks slightly LESS. Low mileage is therefore treated as protecting this car from the bottom of each observed band, not as earning a premium at the top of it. This trim is the FWD 204 PS entry car; quattro, rear-axle steering and adaptive air suspension are not fitted, so no air-spring replacement is carried in the maintenance tail (that risk belongs to the 200 kW quattro S line). The 48V MHEV plus starter-generator and its lithium pack ARE fitted and are carried as an out-of-warranty risk item from year 7.

purchase.source: List price INDEPENDENTLY RE-VERIFIED and the scout's NT$2,880,000 is CONFIRMED CORRECT. Two sources were fetched and read directly in this audit: Yahoo Autos 2026 A6 Sedan model page returns TFSI 150kW = 288万 (1984cc, 204hp@4300-6000rpm, 4-door 5-seat, fuel type 汽油) and TFSI 200kW quattro S line = 346万; CARTURE's 2026-01-14 full-range price table returns A6 Sedan TFSI 150kW 288万 / Sedan TFSI 200kW quattro S line 346万 / Avant TFSI 150kW 298万 / Avant TFSI 200kW quattro S line 356万. The Avant's 298万 matters because it is the denominator of the year-1 CPO anchor. Deviation from the scout is 0%, so the scout's figure stands. Discount is an estimate, not a sourced transaction: Audi Taiwan publishes only non-cash sweeteners for the A6 (5年保固, 最高250万48期0利率, 低月付5,888元起), and the single 購車菜單 on 8891 for this nameplate is an unfilled 徵求 for the previous-generation car. 150,000 (5.2%) reflects a normal negotiated cash-plus-accessory concession on a just-launched large German sedan in an SUV-dominated Taiwan market - new generations discount less than run-out stock, so this is deliberately conservative. On-road fees are estimated at this price class, not quoted.
purchase.notes: 48V MILD HYBRID, CLASSIFIED GASOLINE. The C9 A6 2.0 TFSI uses Audi's MHEV plus - a 48V battery driving a belt starter-generator - which boosts and coasts but cannot move the car on electricity alone, so it is 'gasoline' for this table, not 'hybrid'. Note that Yahoo Autos labels the sibling TFSI 200 kW quattro as 油電混合/Hybrid; that trim runs the same 48V architecture and would also be 'gasoline' under these rules. Spec: 1984cc turbo I4, 204 PS / 340 Nm, 7-speed S tronic, FRONT-WHEEL DRIVE (independently confirmed by the drivetrain field 前驅 on Audi Taiwan's own Approved :plus listing for the same 150kW powertrain). Generation C9 went on sale in Taiwan in late 2025; the 200 kW quattro opened for order 2026-01. Arithmetic check: 2,880,000 - 150,000 + 65,000 = 2,795,000, verified. onroad_fees = 領牌 + 代辦 + 配件 only: government items are small (新領牌照登記費 600 + 行照 300 + 號牌 200) and the bulk is dealer 代辦費 ~12,000 plus a typical delivery accessory pack for this class (隔熱紙 for a large glass area ~30,000, 玻璃/車身鍍膜 ~18,000, 行車紀錄器 ~8,000, 腳踏墊與防水托盤 ~5,000). EXCLUDED from discounts on purpose: the 汰舊換新再減5万 shown on 8891 is a 貨物稅 rebate, conditional on scrapping a qualifying old vehicle, and tax is out of scope for this table. Also excluded: the 0% / low-monthly finance offers, which change cash flow, not price. The scout's classification and spec were audited and found correct - no change.

selling_costs.notes: Assumes a private sale (自售), which is what private_sale_price represents. Government transfer paperwork itself is only a few hundred NT$ (行照換發 200); the 2,000 is the usual 代辦 fee to have it done. Detailing is set at the upper end because a German luxury sedan has to present well against dealer stock - a scruffy car simply does not achieve the private price quoted here. Total 12,000 sits in the normal 6,000-15,000 band for this class. A dealer trade-in instead of a private sale would avoid most of this, which is part of why dealer_tradein_price is lower. Unchanged from the scout; audited and found reasonable.

value_checkpoints.source: REDUCED from the scout's 2,020,000. Anchor re-verified by direct fetch and it is genuine: Audi Approved :plus (official CPO) listing 5196 - A6 Avant TFSI 150kW, 2026年式, registered 2025/11, ~1,000 km, 前驅, Kronos Gray, warranty to 2030/11, asking NT$2,488,000 against the Avant's 298万 list = 83.5% as CERTIFIED retail. Step-down chain: CPO carries roughly a 6% premium over ordinary dealer retail, and private sale runs a further ~10-11% under dealer retail, giving ~70% of list. The scout stopped there (0.835 x 0.94 x 0.90 x 2,880,000 = 2,020,000). Two corrections pull it down. (a) The anchor is an AVANT with 1,000 km and a live factory warranty to 2030; our car is the higher-volume Sedan with 7,000 km, and the Avant is the scarcer, more sought-after body in Taiwan. (b) A year-2 bridge now exists that the scout mis-dated away: the 40 TFSI S line with 12,300 km asking 188.0万 is a 2024 car, not a 2023, so against the C8 S line's 293.5万 list it reads 64.0% dealer retail at 2 years = ~57% private. A curve running 70% (y1) -> 57% (y2) -> 48% (y3) is too steep between y1 and y2; 67.7% of list at y1 makes the sequence coherent. 0.677 x 2,880,000 = 1,950,000 (69.8% of real_cost, a 30% first-year loss - a German number, not a Toyota one). NOT used: 8891's algorithmic 保值率 model claims 89.0% at year 1, which is mileage-blind, brand-generic and contradicted by Audi's own CPO asking price; rejected, as the scout also rejected it. Dealer trade-in set 12.1% under private.

REDUCED from the scout's 1,420,000 - this is the checkpoint the scout's dating error distorted most. Predecessor-generation (C8) evidence at exactly this age, converted to a ratio then applied to real_cost. Genuine 3-year-old cars on 8891 中古車 A6 Sedan, re-read directly in this audit: 2023 40 TFSI Technik豪華版 4,714 km asking 148.0万; 2023 40 TFSI Technik豪華版 35,000 km (3.5万公里) asking 149.0万; 2023 40 TFSI 28,000 km (2.8万公里) asking 149.8万. Against C8 list prices (享馭版 269.5万, Technik豪華版 277.5万) that is a TIGHT dealer-retail band of 53-55%. The scout reported the band as 53-64% and took the 64% as 'the clean low-mileage read' - but the 64% belongs to the 12,300 km car asking 188.0万, which is a 2024 model, not a 2023. Remove that mis-dated car and the top of the band disappears. Note also that within the true 2023 set the 4,714 km car asks 148.0万 while the 35,000 km car asks 149.0万, so there is no mileage premium to harvest at this age; our 21,000 km sits mid-pack and earns no uplift. Audi's own CPO 40 TFSI Technik registered 2023/08 at 168万 = 60.5% brackets the top as CERTIFIED retail, consistent with a ~6-7% CPO premium over the 53-55% ordinary band. Taking 54% dealer retail and the standard ~11% step down to private gives 48.1%; 0.481 x 2,795,000 = 1,345,000. THESE ARE NOT DEALER ASKING PRICES COPIED ACROSS - the 148-150万 figures were reduced before use. Dealer trade-in set 13.0% under private.

Essentially unchanged in value from the scout's 1,000,000, but the supporting reasoning was wrong and is restated. Real 8891 listings, model years re-verified in this audit: 2022 40 TFSI Technik豪華版 43,400 km (4.34万公里) asking 123.8万 against 274万 list = 45.2% at FOUR years; 2022 40 TFSI Technik豪華版 124,900 km (12.49万公里) asking 82.9万 = 30.3% at FOUR years; 2021 40 TFSI Premium 97,000 km asking 85.8万 against ~269万 = 31.9% at FIVE years. The scout filed that 124,900 km car as a 2021 five-year car, so its stated '5-year band' actually contained a 4-year car. Corrected, the only genuine 5-year point is the 2021 Premium at 97,000 km / 31.9%, and the useful bracket is 45.2% (4yr, 43,400 km) to 31.9% (5yr, 97,000 km). Our car is 5 years old with 35,000 km - lower mileage than every comparator - so it interpolates to ~40% dealer retail, and ~11% down to private gives 35.4%; 0.354 x 2,795,000 = 990,000. Sense check in absolute terms: the 43,400 km 4-year car asks 123.8万 at a dealer, so a 5-year 35,000 km car asks roughly 110-115万 at a dealer and ~99万 privately, scaled to the C9's higher base. Marked low because the mileage correction, not any single listing, is doing the work, and because the 82.9万 cluster shows how wide the dispersion is at this age.

REDUCED from the scout's 800,000, because the scout's 7-year comparator is really a 6-year car. Real 8891 listings with model years re-verified: 2020 40 TDI 30,000 km asking 93.8万 against ~259万 list = 36.2%; 2020 40 TDI 87,000 km (8.7万公里) asking 89.0万 = 34.4%; 2020 40 TDI Premium 156,000 km asking 72.8万 = 28.1%. All three are 2020 cars, i.e. SIX years old in 2026. The scout dated the 87,000 km car as a 2019 and read it as '~34% at 7 years'; it is 34% at 6 years, so the whole 7-year read was anchored a year too generously. There is in fact NO genuine 7-year comparator in the current listing set, making this a one-year extrapolation beyond the data. Starting from 36.2% dealer retail at 6 years / 30,000 km and adding a year plus 19,000 km gives ~30.5% dealer retail at 7 years / 49,000 km; ~11% down to private gives 27.0%; 0.270 x 2,795,000 = 755,000. Held deliberately low rather than flattened, because Audi Taiwan's factory warranty (3 years unlimited + years 4-5 under 100,000 km) has expired by now and the Taiwanese used market discounts an out-of-warranty German car for repair risk. One genuine 個人自售 point exists - 2020 40 TDI Premium, 205,000 km, private asking 80.0万 - and is useful only as a reminder that private ASKING prices run optimistic; it was not used as a comparator. Comparators are diesel C8s, a further reason for low confidence. Dealer trade-in set 15.2% under private - dealers widen the spread on older German stock.

REDUCED SHARPLY from the scout's 515,000 - the second big correction. No 10-year data exists for this generation (C9 launched in Taiwan late 2025), so this is extrapolated from the C7.5 A6, expressed as a retention ratio and applied to this car's real_cost. Real 8891 listings as of 2026-08: 2017 35 TFSI 142,400 km (14.24万公里) asking 53.9万; 2018 35 TFSI 59,900 km (5.99万公里) asking 46.9万; 2016 35 TFSI 141,000 km asking 42.8万; 2016 35 TFSI 120,000 km asking 32.2万; 2016 35 TFSI 190,000 km asking 29.8万. Original list: A6 Sedan 35 TFSI 238万 from 2015, 248万 for 2017年式. That gives 10-year dealer RETAIL retention of 12.5-18.0% for the true 2016 cars, and 21.7% for the 9-year 2017. The scout claimed 'our 70,000 km is far below the 120,000-190,000 km typical of these survivors, so the top of that band applies: ~20%'. That reasoning inverts the data: the TOP of the band (53.9万, 21.7%) belongs to the HIGHEST-mileage car in the set (142,400 km), while the genuinely low-mileage car (2018, 59,900 km) asks only 46.9万 = 18.9% despite being two years YOUNGER. Mileage barely orders price at this age. A defensible read for a 10-year car at 70,000 km is therefore ~17% dealer retail - above the 13-18% of the 2016 survivors on mileage, but bounded above by the 8-year 59,900 km car's 18.9%. Private after the usual ~11% step down is 15.1%; 0.151 x 2,795,000 = 420,000. Absolute sense check that the scout's figure fails: at 515,000 a private seller of a 10-year C9 would be getting MORE than a dealer asks for the newer, similar-mileage 2018 C7.5 (46.9万) - internally inconsistent. At 420,000 the car sits just under that dealer ask, which is where a 2-year-older private car belongs. Dealer trade-in set 17.9% under private; at this age many dealers will only wholesale the car. Low confidence by construction: two generations removed, and the C9 carries far more electronics (48V MHEV plus, twin OLED displays) than the C7.5 1.8T, which if anything argues the real tail is worse, not better.

maintenance.plan_notes: Scheduled-service figures come from Audi Taiwan's own published price tool, service-pricing.audi-service.com.tw ('保養透明 安心啟航'), queried per service year. The tool was re-fetched in this audit and CONFIRMED to exist and to work as described - it returns a roughly NT$1,000-wide price band per model / 年式 / 使用年份, and states that quoted prices are reference figures for 定期保養 under normal use, with the final amount depending on inspection. The specific per-year query the scout ran could NOT be reproduced here, so the figures below are reported-but-unreproduced and every checkpoint is capped at medium confidence. The C9 A6 is not yet in that database, so the closest available petrol A6 was used: A6 Avant, 2019年式, 45 TFSI quattro (same 1984cc EA888 2.0 TFSI family, same 定期保養 schedule) - note this is a quattro, so it is not a perfect proxy for a FWD car. Per-year midpoints used: y1 12,400, y2 13,600, y3 16,800, y4 13,600, y5 12,400, y6 30,200 (the big one: 自動變速箱油, 火星塞, 皮帶與調整器), y7 9,300, y8 9,300, y9 13,400, y10 9,300. INTERVAL IS TIME-DRIVEN, NOT MILEAGE-DRIVEN at this profile: the schedule is annual with a secondary kilometre trigger that 7,000 km/yr never reaches, so each checkpoint carries exactly one paid visit per year and nothing is saved by driving less. WARRANTY SHAPES THE EARLY PERIODS: Audi Taiwan gives 3 years unlimited mileage plus years 4 and 5 if under 100,000 km, and the current A6 campaign advertises 5年保固. Our buyer is at 35,000 km by year 5, so years 1-5 carry scheduled servicing and wear parts only - no repair cost. That subsidy ends there, and the years 5-7 and 7-10 periods deliberately carry the FULL unsubsidised cost: out-of-warranty repair risk, Audi dealer labour rates, 18-19 inch tyres and large brakes. Audi Taiwan's table covers scheduled servicing ONLY - tyres, brake pads and discs, the 12V AGM battery, the 48V lithium pack and the belt starter-generator, suspension wear and any repair are added on top from Taiwan parts-and-labour pricing for this class. Ten-year total is 482,000, about 48,000/yr; the scheduled portion alone is only ~140,000, so roughly 70% of lifetime maintenance is items the official table does not show. That total is far above a Japanese equivalent of this size (a Camry-class car runs roughly half), which is the correct shape for an out-of-warranty German luxury sedan. Excluded by scope: tax, insurance, fuel, tyres damaged by road hazard.

Timing of the tyre replacement is judgement, hence medium. Audited and left unchanged - age-driven tyre replacement at year 5 is the right call for a 7,000 km/yr car.

purchase.notes: POWERTRAIN - the classification trap, and it is 12V not 48V. U-CAR's spec text for this exact variant describes a '12V 輕型複合動力系統' built from a belt-driven starter-generator (BSG), a DC-DC converter and a 12V lithium battery, giving up to 5 kW of recuperation and start-stop down to 22 km/h. The 48V system in the A7 range belongs to the 55 TFSI V6, not this car ('A7 Sportback 55 TFSI 則搭載 3.0 升雙渦輪增壓 V6 引擎，搭配 48V 輕型複合動力系統'). Either way it cannot move the car on electricity alone, so this is 'gasoline'. Yahoo Autos mislabels this trim's 動力型式 as 油電混合 - verified on the page 2026-08-12, and that label is wrong. Powertrain detail: 1,984cc inline-4 TFSI turbo, 265 hp @ 5,250-6,500 rpm, 7-speed S-tronic, quattro AWD, 12.6 km/L combined, 1,815 kg, 5,021 mm long. A slow-selling German liftback in run-out, in a bodystyle Taiwanese buyers do not want, supports a discount well above the 5% a fast-moving model would get. Audi Taiwan also runs a standing 舊換新 trade-in programme. 8.6% is deliberately conservative; a determined buyer at model-year end could plausibly do better. Note the 'lineup is down to two trims' framing needs care: U-CAR shows two A7 trims (372.5 / 414.5萬) because it files RS7 separately, while Yahoo's 2025 A7 page shows three (372.5 / 414.5 / RS7 Performance 785萬). Scaled to price; excludes tax and insurance per the table's design. MODEL YEAR: labelled 2026 to match the rest of this batch because the car is on sale in Taiwan today, but TW catalogues still list it as the 2025 model year and no 2026 A7 page exists. Treat it as a run-out C8, not a fresh model year.

value_checkpoints.source: EXTRAPOLATED from the Audi TW year-1 pattern, not from an A7 listing - no 1-year-old A7 exists on the TW market (the youngest C8 A7 found in the 2026-08-12 sweep was a 2022-registered car). Method: comparable near-new low-mileage Audis on 8891 show dealer RETAIL asks around 70% of list at 3,000-11,000 km (e.g. A4 Avant 2022 40 TFSI advanced, 11,000 km, 128.0萬 against a ~209萬 list). The A7 must sit below that: a 1-year-old competes directly against a discounted new one at 348萬, and the buyer pool for a run-out liftback is tiny. Implied dealer retail ~273萬 (73% of list); took 12% off retail for the private 自售 figure of 240萬 (8891 asks are 車商售價, never what an owner receives), then a further 14% off private for dealer trade-in. That is a 31% loss of real_cost in year one - steep, as a German luxury car should be, and nowhere near Toyota-like retention.

PARTLY ANCHORED. C8 A7 45 TFSI listings at age 3 exist on 8891 but are listed 電洽 (price withheld), so they fix the age/mileage point without giving a number - my own 2026-08-12 sweep confirms this by returning no age-3 A7 with a disclosed price. I therefore anchored on same-age Audi siblings from the same sweep and interpolated by price class, because retention falls as list price rises: Q5 2023 40 TFSI Technik 豪華版, 44,800 km, 122.9萬 (~51% of list); A6 Sedan 2022 40 TFSI Technik, 125,500 km, 82.9萬. The A7 at 372.5萬 sits above these, giving ~53% dealer retail = ~199萬. Our car also has only 21,000 km, well under the 40,000-130,000 km on the real comparables, which supports the upper half of the range. Adjusted to private sale at 12% below dealer retail (175萬) and dealer trade-in a further 15% below private. Cross-check: a real 2022-registered (age 4) A7 45 TFSI quattro享馭版 with 130,000 km asks 149.8萬 dealer retail, and a 21,000 km age-3 car sitting ~33% above that very-high-mileage car is consistent. Years 1-3 carry the steepest loss, as expected for this segment.

INTERPOLATED between the year-3 estimate and the year-7 real anchor, with one real A7 bracketing point re-verified in my own 2026-08-12 sweep: a 2022-registered (age 4) A7 Sportback 45 TFSI quattro享馭版 with 130,000 km asks 149.8萬 dealer retail on 8891 (新北市). That car has 3.7x our assumed mileage, so a 35,000 km car must sit clearly above it - used ~172萬 dealer retail. Private sale at 12% below retail = 151萬 (8891 figures are 車商售價, not owner proceeds); dealer trade-in a further 15% below private. Note the curve is deliberately flattish from year 3 to year 7: the thin TW A7 market is dominated by mileage rather than age, which the real listings show directly - the 47,000 km 2019 car asks MORE (155.8萬) than this 130,000 km 2022 car (149.8萬).

STRONGEST ANCHOR IN THIS RECORD - a real, near-perfectly matched listing, independently re-verified on 2026-08-12: Audi A7 Sportback 2019款 45 TFSI quattro 2.0L, registered 2019 (age 7), 47,000 km, asking 155.8萬 DEALER RETAIL, 高雄市. Same generation, same 45 TFSI quattro drivetrain, age 7 vs our 7, 47,000 km vs our 49,000 - and at 6,714 km/yr it is almost exactly this buyer's usage profile, so it is a genuine low-mileage comparable, not a mileage-blind average. Its original list price is now DOUBLE-SOURCED at 349萬 (U-CAR's 2019-08-22 launch report AND Yahoo Autos' 2019 and 2020 A7 model pages, which both show '45 TFSI quattro 349萬 | 1984cc'), giving 44.6% dealer-retail retention. FULL ADJUSTMENT CHAIN, stated honestly: scaling 44.6% to our higher 372.5萬 list implies ~166萬 dealer retail; I then applied a -9% nameplate/negotiation markdown to ~151萬 (single dealer asks on rare cars negotiate down, and by the time our car is 7 the A7 nameplate will be several years discontinued with a replacement generation on sale); then -12% from that dealer-retail level to the private 自售 figure of 133萬; then -15% from private for dealer trade-in = 113萬. Total gap from the scaled dealer ask to private sale is therefore ~20%, of which 12 points are the standard dealer-retail-to-private adjustment and 9 points are the named nameplate risk - the two are separate and are not both 'the dealer margin'. This is the one checkpoint with a like-for-like A7 data point, hence 'medium'.

PREDECESSOR-GENERATION EXTRAPOLATION - no 10-year-old C8 exists (the C8 launched in TW in Aug 2019, so the oldest is 7). CORRECTED: the prior version of this record applied a retention ratio against an ESTIMATED ~300萬 C7 list price which it could not verify. I verified it. Yahoo Autos' archived model pages show the C7 A7 Sportback 40 TFSI quattro - 1,984cc / 252 hp, the direct 2.0L predecessor of our 45 TFSI and precisely the car used as the age-10 comparable - listed in Taiwan at 340萬 (2017 page) and 341萬 (2018 page), NOT ~300萬. Real age-10 comparable, re-verified in my own 2026-08-12 8891 sweep: A7 Sportback 2016款 40 TFSI quattro 2.0L, registered 2016, 57,000 km, 78.8萬 dealer retail, 台南市 - the closest match on generation-role, engine and low mileage. Retention = 78.8/340 = 23.2% of list at age 10 (the old record's 26% was an artefact of the too-low denominator). Applying 23.2% to our 372.5萬 list gives ~86.3萬 dealer retail at 57,000 km. Mileage-adjusting to our 70,000 km using the two same-age C7 50 TFSI listings that differ only in mileage (70,000 km 76.8萬 vs 110,000 km 68.8萬, i.e. ~2萬 per 10,000 km) subtracts ~2.6萬, giving ~84萬 dealer retail. Private sale at 12% below that = 740,000; dealer trade-in a further 15% below private = 630,000. Note the prior record claimed 'two independent routes agree at ~96-98萬' - they were not independent, both used the same unverified 300萬. The tail keeps falling rather than flattening, which the C7 data confirms: age 13 (2013, 3.0 TFSI, 110,000 km) 45.8萬 and (2013, 2.8 FSI, 130,000 km) 29.8萬, with no Lexus-style plateau. Confidence stays 'low' because it is still a cross-generation extrapolation, but the single weakest link - the unverified predecessor list price - is now closed with a real source.

maintenance.plan_notes: SCHEDULE IS TIME-DRIVEN, NOT MILEAGE-DRIVEN. Audi's long-life service is 1 year / 15,000 km; at 7,000 km/yr this car never reaches the mileage trigger, so it is serviced annually on the calendar and reaches only 70,000 km at 10 years. The owner pays for 10 services while accumulating under 5 services' worth of wear - low mileage does NOT scale the bill down proportionally. TYRE SIZE CORRECTED: U-CAR's spec table gives 245/45 R19 for the 45 TFSI 享馭版; the 255/40 R20 in the same table belongs to the 55 TFSI. The prior version of this record budgeted 20-inch tyres at NT$60,000-70,000 per set, which overstated this trim - a 245/45 R19 premium set in Taiwan runs roughly NT$50,000-55,000. That saving has been reallocated to genuine out-of-warranty risk in the 5-7 year window, which was previously under-budgeted to the point that the year-7 period cost fell BELOW year-5. WARRANTY ASSUMPTION (flagged, not verified): assumed Audi Taiwan's standard 3-year unlimited-mileage new-car warranty, so years 0-1 and 1-3 carry routine servicing only, and every period after year 3 carries the FULL unsubsidised cost including out-of-warranty failures. www.audi.com.tw returns HTTP 503 to every fetch attempt (re-confirmed 2026-08-12), so the warranty term and all figures below are informed estimates for a German luxury dealer network in Taiwan, not quotes from an official table. If Audi TW bundles a prepaid service package, the year 0-3 figures would fall and the later ones would not change. WHY THIS IS MUCH HIGHER THAN A JAPANESE EQUIVALENT: Audi dealer labour rates, 19-inch tyres replaced on age rather than tread, oversized brakes on an 1,815 kg car, a wet-clutch 7-speed S-tronic needing its own oil-and-filter service, and EA888-family risk items after warranty - water pump / plastic thermostat housing, coil packs, PCV and valve cover. Two batteries are budgeted, not one: the main AGM starter battery plus the separate 12V lithium battery feeding the mild-hybrid BSG. Air suspension is NOT budgeted - it is not standard on the TW 45 TFSI 享馭版 (U-CAR lists 獨立五連桿 front and rear) - but if a particular car was optioned with it, add NT$60,000-120,000 per corner-pair in the 7-10 window. There is no DPF and no 48V starter-generator on this variant, so those two common German risk items do not apply. Ten-year total ~NT$660,000, roughly 2.5-3x a Japanese equivalent.

checkpoints.source: Estimated. RAISED from the prior version, which put this period BELOW year 5 - a non-monotonic dip that is wrong for an out-of-warranty German car entering its 6th and 7th years. The S-tronic service (~NT$22,000) is the scheduled big-ticket item, due on the ~60,000 km / time window. Both batteries land here: the AGM starter battery typically dies at 5-7 years in Taiwan's heat, and the separate 12V lithium battery supporting the BSG mild-hybrid is an Audi-specific cost a naturally-aspirated Japanese car simply does not have. Rear pads plus discs at Audi dealer rates on a 5m, 1,815 kg car run ~NT$35,000. The added unscheduled-repair line reflects that years 5-7 on an EA888 A7 realistically produce at least one oil leak or bushing job at full dealer labour.

checkpoints.source: Estimated, and deliberately the largest period - a 7-10 year-old German luxury liftback out of warranty is where the real money goes, and pricing it like a RAV4's tail would be wrong. Three annual services plus a second complete tyre set (age again, not tread - the car has still done only 70,000 km in total). The water pump and plastic thermostat housing are a well-documented EA888 wear item landing squarely in this window, and coil packs typically fail as a set around this age. Suspension dampers and bushings are included because 10-year-old German chassis components perish on time in Taiwan's climate regardless of mileage, and an MMI/module line is budgeted because the electronics on this generation are a real out-of-warranty exposure. Total 10-year maintenance across all five periods is ~NT$660,000, roughly 2.5-3x a Japanese equivalent over the same period - that gap is the honest picture, not a rounding artefact.

assumptions.notes: Buyer drives 6,000-8,000 km/year, far below the Taiwan average of ~12,000-15,000 km/year. Every checkpoint uses assumed_km = 7000 * years (7,000 / 21,000 / 35,000 / 49,000 / 70,000). Because mileage is so low, servicing is TIME-driven, not km-driven: the car needs an annual visit regardless, so the owner makes 10 workshop visits over 10 years but only reaches 7 km milestones (10k through 70k). Tax (牌照稅 NT$15,210 + 燃料稅 NT$7,200 per year) and insurance are excluded by design. LOW-MILEAGE PREMIUM — APPLIED ONLY WHERE IT IS NOT ALREADY IN THE COMPARABLE: at years 3, 5 and 7 the comparables carry 45,000-53,000 km against this car's 21,000-49,000 km, so a premium is warranted and stated. At year 10 it is NOT applied, because the anchor comparable is itself a 71,000 km car — essentially identical to this car's assumed 70,000 km — so a further premium would be double-counting (this was the main correction made to the researcher's record). IMPORTANT CONTEXT: Audi confirmed in March 2026 that the D5 A8 has stopped taking orders worldwide, with no successor until roughly 2030 (co-developed with the next Porsche Panamera on MSB61w). Anything bought in Taiwan today is remaining stock of a discontinued flagship, which makes the discount bigger and the residual worse than a mid-cycle car.

purchase.source: VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY AND UNCHANGED — NT$4,500,000. Confirmed by two separate sources fetched directly: KingAutos 2024-09-21 (kingautos.net/359178) and Storm.mg (storm.mg/lifestyle/5241335) both state Taiwan Audi raised the A8 range by NT$120,000 for the 2024 model year, taking the short-wheelbase 55 TFSI quattro to NT$4,500,000 and the A8 L to NT$5,680,000. The A8 launched in Taiwan in May 2022 at NT$4,380,000; KingAutos' own lineup table and Yahoo Autos' 2023 trim page still show that stale pre-2024 figure and were NOT used. NAMING NOTE: both 2024MY articles name the NT$4,500,000 car 'A8 55 TFSI quattro S line Black', while 8891 still labels 2024 used cars '55 TFSI quattro 享馭版'; the assigned trim label is retained but the two names refer to the same NT$4,500,000 short-wheelbase car. Discount of NT$500,000 (11.1%) reflects end-of-life clearance: the D5 stopped taking orders globally in March 2026, and Taiwan Audi's March 2026 promotion sheet (auto-online, fetched and read) lists A3/A5/A6/Q3/Q5/Q7/Q8/e-tron and does not mention A8 at all. This remains the least-evidenced number in the record — no published A8 購車菜單 was found — but for unsold flagship stock in a market that moves a handful of A8s a year it is realistic and arguably conservative.
purchase.notes: Standard-wheelbase A8 (5,190 mm), not the A8 L. 3.0 V6 TFSI turbo, 340 hp / 51.0 kgm, 8-speed tiptronic, quattro, 2,038 kg, 265/40R20 all round, standard adaptive air suspension. POWERTRAIN CLASSIFICATION: this car carries Audi's 48V MHEV (輕型複合動力) belt-alternator starter system. It cannot move the car on battery alone, so it is correctly classified 'gasoline' here, and this was checked rather than inherited — Audi's own Approved :plus listing states '48V Mild hybrid' and the Yahoo 2021 copy says '48V輕型複合動力系統'. Note that KingAutos, 8891 and SUM all mislabel it '油電混合(HEV)' in their spec tables — that is a data-entry convention on their side, not a series hybrid. onroad_fees NT$90,000 = 領牌 + 代辦 ~NT$20,000, top-tier full-car window film ~NT$45,000 (large glass area on a flagship), paint coating ~NT$25,000. Scaled to the price class; tax and insurance excluded. Taiwan's 特種貨物及勞務稅 (luxury tax) on cars was abolished in 2016, so no extra levy applies above NT$3M.

value_checkpoints.source: REVISED DOWN from the researcher's NT$2,650,000 / NT$2,250,000 for internal consistency of the dealer-retail discount. Anchor verified directly on Audi Taiwan Approved :plus (approvedplus.audi.com.tw/listing/5201/a8): an A8 registered 2025/3 with 3,275 km asking NT$3,280,000 — a genuine ~1.4-year-old car at ultra-low mileage, and confirmed to exist. That is a CPO DEALER RETAIL ask carrying a certification+warranty premium, so it is stepped down to independent dealer retail ~NT$2,900,000. That step-down is corroborated from the other direction by the 8891 curve for this exact trim (2023 at 50,000 km asking NT$1,888,000-1,998,000, 2022 at 53,600 km asking NT$1,800,000), which extrapolates back to ~NT$2,850,000-2,900,000 independent dealer retail at one year on low mileage. PRIVATE SALE = 12% BELOW independent dealer retail = NT$2,550,000; the researcher used only 9% here while using 12% at years 3, 5 and 7 — the 12% is applied uniformly. Dealer trade-in = 14.5% below private = NT$2,180,000. Held down deliberately because at year 1 this seller competes against remaining discounted NEW clearance stock of the same discontinued car. Sanity check against real stock: the 27,371 km car on the same CPO page asks NT$2,488,000, so a two-year-old private sale is ~NT$2,190,000 — this year-1 figure sits sensibly above it.

UNCHANGED — verified independently and the listings are real. Fetched auto.8891.com.tw/audi/a8 directly and confirmed four listings of the EXACT trim, all 2023 cars at 50,000-51,000 km: NT$1,998,000, NT$1,998,000, NT$1,998,000 and NT$1,888,000 — average ~NT$1,960,000 DEALER RETAIL ASKING. Our car at 21,000 km is well under half that mileage, so +10% low-mileage premium → ~NT$2,150,000 dealer retail. The premium is if anything conservative: the same page shows a 2022 at 53,600 km asking NT$1,800,000 against a 2022 at 112,000 km asking NT$1,288,000, i.e. roughly 2x mileage costs ~28% of price. Private sale set 12% below dealer retail = NT$1,890,000; dealer trade-in a further 14% below private = NT$1,620,000. The 46% retention this implies is not an error: a German flagship losing over half its money in three years is exactly what the Taiwan listings show.

UNCHANGED — comparable verified on the 8891 page fetched directly: a 2021 A8 55 TFSI quattro at 47,000 km listed NT$1,589,000 dealer retail (also carried by SUM at 47,860 km, one owner). Its original list was NT$4,290,000 (Yahoo Autos 2021 trim page), so that is 37.0% of list at dealer retail. A higher-mileage 2021/2022 pairing on the same page shows how strongly mileage bites (2022 at 112,000 km asks only NT$1,288,000). Our car at 35,000 km sits well under the 47,000 km comparable → ~+8% → dealer retail ~NT$1,700,000, then trimmed to NT$1,650,000 because by 2031 this will be a five-year-discontinued model. Private = 12% below dealer retail = NT$1,450,000; trade-in = 14.5% below private = NT$1,240,000. Note this anchors on the comparable's absolute price rather than rescaling its retention ratio up to our higher NT$4,500,000 list, which is the conservative choice.

UNCHANGED — comparables verified on the 8891 page fetched directly. Same D5 generation but the 50 TDI variant (original list NT$3,980,000 per U-CAR 2019 launch report): 8891 shows a 2019 50 TDI with 45,000 km at NT$1,050,000 and one with 93,000 km at NT$1,088,000 — 26-27% of list at independent dealer retail. Audi's own CPO channel asks NT$1,488,000 for a 2019 50 TDI with 49,942 km, almost exactly our checkpoint mileage but carrying the CPO premium (that ~39% CPO gap on an older car is why the year-1 CPO anchor above had to be stepped down too). Taking ~28% of our NT$4,500,000 list = ~NT$1,260,000 independent dealer retail, with the low-mileage premium embedded since our 49,000 km beats the 80,000-105,000 km a typical 7-year-old A8 shows. Private = 12% below = NT$1,100,000; trade-in = 14.5% below private = NT$940,000. Cross-variant substitution (TDI→TFSI) is the weakness here; petrol 55 TFSI short-wheelbase cars of 2019 vintage barely exist in Taiwan.

CORRECTED — the researcher's NT$700,000 / NT$590,000 double-counted the low-mileage premium and is revised down by ~21%. EXTRAPOLATED: no genuine 10-year data exists for the current D5 generation, which only launched in Taiwan in 2018, so per method this uses the PREDECESSOR D4 generation's retention ratio applied to this car's cost. Real D4 data verified on the 8891 page fetched directly: an A8 50 TFSI quattro at 71,000 km asks NT$580,000 and one at 112,000 km asks NT$498,000 — both are 2016 cars (the researcher recorded them as 2015; a 2016 car is in fact exactly ten years old in 2026, so the comparable is better than claimed). Against a D4 original list of NT$4,230,000 (Yahoo Autos trim page) that is 13.7% and 11.8% retention at dealer retail. THE KEY FIX: the NT$580,000 car is a 71,000 km car, essentially identical to this car's assumed 70,000 km at year 10, so its 13.7% ALREADY IS the low-mileage figure — the researcher's further +20% premium on top was double-counting. Applying 13.7-14% with no extra premium gives ~NT$625,000 dealer-retail equivalent; private = 12% below = NT$550,000; trade-in = 15% below private = NT$465,000. Cross-check: real asking prices fall from NT$1,050,000 for a 7-year-old D5 to NT$580,000 for a 10-year-old D4, a ~45% drop, and this checkpoint drops 50% from year 7 — appropriate for an orphaned flagship carrying air suspension and 48V electronics with no factory successor. Explicitly extrapolated, not observed.

maintenance.plan_notes: Built from Audi Taiwan's OFFICIAL published service price table (service-pricing.audi-service.com.tw), whose underlying data endpoint was fetched and read directly during this check. The exact variant row 'Audi A8 / 55 TFSI quattro / Petrol' (2021) was CONFIRMED VERBATIM: 10,000 km NT$13,900-14,900 / 20,000 km NT$24,400-25,400 / 30,000 km NT$17,700-18,700 / 40,000 km NT$24,400-25,400 / 50,000 km NT$13,900-14,900 / 60,000 km NT$100,200-101,200 / 70,000 km NT$13,900-14,900. Midpoints are used. The separate 'Audi A8 L 55 TFSI quattro Premium' (2022) row at NT$9,500-10,500 also exists and was confirmed, but it is a different, long-wheelbase model line and is treated as a lower bound only; the exact short-wheelbase variant match is used. The service matrix drives those steps: oil + oil filter + cabin filter every 10,000 km; brake fluid + SPARK PLUGS every 20,000 km; air filter every 30,000 km; AUTOMATIC TRANSMISSION OIL every 60,000 km — which is why the 60,000 km visit is NT$100,700 and, at 7,000 km/year, lands at year 8.6, squarely in the 7-10 year window. AT ONLY 7,000 km/YEAR THE INTERVAL IS TIME-DRIVEN, NOT MILEAGE-DRIVEN: the car needs an annual service regardless, so there are 10 visits across 10 years but only 7 km milestones; the 3 extra visits are time-based oil-and-filter services billed at roughly the base rate. WARRANTY — CORRECTED: the researcher assumed a 五年原廠保固 running to year 5 and therefore carried NO repair allowance in the 3-5 year window. Fetching Taiwan Audi's March 2026 programme (auto-online) shows the A8 IS NOT LISTED in it — the table covers A3/A5/A6/Q3/Q5/Q7/Q8/e-tron only. The 5-year cover cannot be assumed for A8, so this record works from standard cover expiring around year 3 and adds an out-of-warranty allowance from the 3-5 year window onward. Later-period items reflect what actually breaks on this car in Taiwan: the standard adaptive AIR SUSPENSION (an entire Taiwanese repair industry exists around Audi/A8 air struts — CG 氣壓避震器 and M&B Power both document A8 front-strut leaks as routine work), the EA839 3.0 TFSI water pump / thermostat housing / coil packs, the 48V mild-hybrid lithium battery and belt starter-generator, and two sets of 265/40R20 tires (Michelin PS4S at this size runs ~NT$11,500-15,000 each fitted in Taiwan). AIR SUSPENSION ALSO CORRECTED: the researcher budgeted two struts at NT$50,000 total using independent-specialist rates only, which is the cheapest possible path on this car's single most notorious failure item; it is re-weighted to NT$90,000 to blend specialist and dealer OEM pricing. Sanity check: NT$727,000 over 10 years = ~NT$72,700/year, consistent with and slightly above the PTT owner consensus of '年抓5萬/yr' for an out-of-warranty A8 once tires and the NT$100,700 ATF service are included, and far above any Japanese equivalent — as it should be.

checkpoints.source: RAISED from the researcher's NT$345,000. The three scheduled visits, including the NT$100,200-101,200 60,000 km transmission-oil service, come from the Audi Taiwan official price table and were confirmed verbatim from its data endpoint. The correction is the air-suspension line: the researcher budgeted two struts at NT$50,000 using independent-specialist rates only, while its own open question conceded dealer OEM could make this NT$150,000-250,000. Budgeting the cheapest possible path on this car's best-documented failure mode is not a neutral estimate, so it is re-weighted to NT$90,000. Air-suspension failure frequency is evidenced by Taiwanese specialists who document A8 front air-strut leaks as routine work (cgairtw.com, m-b-power.com). Water pump/thermostat/coil and 48V items remain risk-weighted allowances for a fully out-of-warranty EA839 V6 with 48V MHEV, not observed invoices — hence low confidence on the total.
