assumptions.notes: Buyer drives 6,000-8,000 km/year; all checkpoints use the 7,000 km/year midpoint (7,000 / 21,000 / 35,000 / 49,000 / 70,000 km). That is roughly half the Taiwan average, so servicing is TIME-driven (one annual visit) rather than mileage-driven, and the mileage milestones in Audi Taiwan's official price table arrive far later in calendar time than for an average-mileage owner — the 60,000 km major service lands around year 9 rather than year 4. Used-value estimates therefore quote low-mileage listings, which sit above the mileage-blind average for this model, and every value source string names the specific low-mileage comparables used. Annual road tax (牌照稅 NT$7,120 for the 1,498 cc band) and fuel tax (燃料稅 NT$4,800), plus all insurance, are EXCLUDED by design and appear nowhere in purchase, maintenance or selling costs. Fuel/energy cost is also out of scope. Two market facts shape this record. (1) THE 2026 PRICE RESET, now verified trim-by-trim in this pass rather than asserted. Audi Taiwan collapsed the Q2 range from five trims to two with the 2026年式 launched 2026-03-05. Verified on Yahoo Autos model pages I fetched myself: the 2024 lineup was 35 TFSI 享馭版 NT$1,560,000 / Technik 豪華版 NT$1,620,000 / Advanced 進化版 NT$1,740,000 / S-Line 運動版 NT$1,840,000 / SQ2 NT$2,450,000, and the 2022 lineup was 享馭版 NT$1,510,000 / Technik 豪華版 NT$1,570,000 / Technik 旅型特仕 NT$1,670,000 / Advanced 進化版 NT$1,690,000 / S-Line 運動版 NT$1,790,000 / SQ2 NT$2,390,000. The 2026 lineup is Advanced 進化版 NT$1,399,000 / S line 運動版 NT$1,699,000. So the entry price fell NT$161,000 (-10.3%) and the car wearing the 'advanced 進化版' badge fell NT$341,000 (-19.6%) — though the badge moved down the range, so the honest reading is that the 2026 advanced sits between the old 享馭版 and the old 進化版 on content while carrying Matrix LED and the 8.8-inch MMI as standard. IMPORTANT CORRECTION to the reviewed record, which stated the previous entry was NT$1,560,000 and implied that was the same trim: NT$1,560,000 was the 享馭版, not the 進化版. Note also that the Carture launch report does NOT itself announce a price cut; the cut is established by comparing the verified 2024 and 2026 lineups, not by any single article. This reset has ALREADY re-priced the live used Q2 market, so the Aug 2026 listings quoted below are post-cut market-cleared prices and the 2026 buyer starts from the lower base. The cut must be counted ONCE, not twice. (2) The Q2 is widely reported to be ending production in 2026 with no direct successor. I could NOT independently verify that claim in this pass (web-search budget exhausted; the Carture launch coverage I re-read makes no mention of it), so it is treated as a soft downward factor on the tail — a single-digit percentage haircut from year 5 on — rather than as an established fact. If the nameplate in fact continues, the year 5-10 values are slightly conservative.

purchase.source: 官方建議售價 NT$1,399,000, re-verified again in this pass on two sources I fetched myself: Yahoo Autos 2026 Q2 model page (https://autos.yahoo.com.tw/new-cars/model/audi-q2-2026) shows 35 TFSI Advanced進化版 139.9萬 and 35 TFSI S-Line運動版 169.9萬, 1,498 cc, 150 hp; Carture launch report (https://www.carture.com.tw/news/article/39840) shows NT$1,399,000 / NT$1,699,000 with a 2026-03-05 on-sale date and no announced incentive. List price unchanged. Discount and on-road fees are estimates, justified in notes.
purchase.notes: COST BASIS — DIRECT ANSWER TO THE REVIEWER'S QUESTION. real_cost NT$1,382,000 is NOT the list price. It is 1,399,000 - 65,000 discount + 48,000 on-road fees. It lands within 1.2% of list only because the on-road fees very nearly cancel the discount, which is the same arithmetic every sibling record in this batch uses (A3: 1,580,000 - 70,000 + 52,000 = 1,562,000, also 98.9% of list; Q3: 1,910,000 - 40,000 + 45,000 = 1,915,000, 100.3% of list). So the 'list price used as cost while quoting real-world resale' failure mode the reviewer suspected is NOT what happened here — the discount is applied, and the cost basis is constructed identically to the siblings the Q2 was being compared against. The year-1 error was entirely on the resale side and is corrected in value_checkpoints. POWERTRAIN: 1.5 TFSI (1,498 cc) inline-4 turbo petrol, 150 hp, 7-speed S tronic dual-clutch (DQ200 dry-clutch), front-wheel drive. NO 48V mild-hybrid system and no electric drive of any kind — a pure combustion car, correctly classified 'gasoline'. Its only efficiency aid is 主動式汽缸管理 (cylinder-on-demand), which deactivates cylinders but cannot move the car on electricity. Audi Taiwan's Q3 does use a 1.5+48V setup; the Q2 does not, so no 48V starter-generator is carried into the maintenance plan (a real difference from the sibling A3 record in this batch, which does carry a 48V BSG provision). MODEL YEAR: 2026年式, on sale in Taiwan from 2026-03-05, range simplified from five trims to two 35 TFSI trims (advanced 進化版 NT$1,399,000 / S line 運動版 NT$1,699,000) with Matrix LED headlights and an 8.8-inch MMI touchscreen now standard. DISCOUNT NT$65,000: two forces pull in opposite directions. Upward — a slow-selling entry SUV reportedly in run-out, on which Audi Taiwan runs cash-equivalent programmes (low monthly payment plans, body-insurance subsidies). Downward — Audi Taiwan has just taken NT$161,000 off the entry price at the factory level, and a freshly re-priced model normally leaves dealers LESS room to discount, because the cut IS the discount. NT$65,000 is 4.6% of list, in line with the 4.4% used on the mechanically near-identical Audi A3 35 TFSI advanced in this same batch. A real quote could land anywhere from NT$40,000 to NT$100,000; at the top of that range real_cost would fall to NT$1,347,000 and every retention ratio below would rise about 2.5 points. This is an estimate, not a published figure; the launch coverage I verified announces no incentive. ON-ROAD FEES NT$48,000 = 領牌 government fees and plates (~NT$1,500-1,900), dealer 代辦費 (~NT$5,000), and accessories typical for this class (window film ~NT$15,000, dashcam ~NT$10,000, mats/trays ~NT$5,000, paint coating ~NT$11,000). Scales correctly against the batch (A3 at NT$1,580,000 carries NT$52,000). Tax and insurance excluded by design. REAL COST = 1,399,000 - 65,000 + 48,000 = 1,382,000.

value_checkpoints.source: RAISED from NT$835,000 private / NT$725,000 trade-in after re-sourcing this row, which is what the reviewer asked for. THE ROOT CAUSE OF THE OLD 60% FIGURE — it was neither a run-out transaction price nor a 領牌車 sale, as hypothesised; it was an AGE-SLOT ERROR. The previous pass anchored year 1 on two SUM listings I re-verified again in this pass (https://www.sum.com.tw/carsearch/AUDI/Q2?v=4): a 2024 Q2 with 8,000 km at NT$928,000 and a 2024 Q2 with 6,338 km at NT$958,000. In Aug 2026 a 2024 model-year car is roughly TWO years old, not one. Those cars were placed in the 1-year slot at their face value, which silently charged the buyer two years of depreciation in the first year and produced the 60% outlier the reviewer flagged. Both listings are still live and their prices are confirmed — the data was right, the age slot was wrong. RE-DERIVED LADDER, in absolute post-cut NT$ against the current NT$1,399,000 new price: 2 years ~NT$940,000 dealer retail (the two 2024 cars above, both genuinely low-mileage at 3,000-4,000 km/year, exactly the profile of this buyer); 4 years NT$768,000 dealer retail (2022 Q2 35 TFSI, 29,251 km, verified on https://www.findcar.com.tw/datalist.aspx?u=1&q=Audi%20Q2). Stepping the 2-year point back one year at a typical 11-13% year-two decline for a German compact gives ~NT$1,070,000 DEALER RETAIL asking at 1 year / 7,000 km, i.e. 76% of the NT$1,399,000 list — a normal 1-year-old dealer asking level, and it makes the ladder 76% / 67% / 55% of list at 1 / 2 / 4 years, which is smooth and monotonic where the old figure put 1 year and 2 years at the same place. ADJUSTMENT APPLIED (dealer retail is NOT what the owner gets): private sale = dealer retail minus 11% = NT$950,000; dealer trade-in = private minus 13% = NT$825,000. That is a 31.3% first-year loss against real_cost (68.7% retention) — still the weakest of the three compact Audis in this batch (A3 72%, Q3 73%), which is right for a run-out entry model whose factory price was just cut, but no longer the A8/Q6-e-tron-class collapse the reviewer objected to, and it restores the front-loaded shape: the 1-to-3 step is now 19 points, steeper than the A3's 13 and in line with the Q3's 18. CONFIDENCE stays medium and not high: there is NO 2025 model-year Q2 listed on FindCar, SUM or 8891 in Aug 2026, so no genuine 1-year-old comparable exists — this figure is a one-year step off real 2-year-old listings, not a direct observation.

Not objected to by the reviewer; re-checked in this pass and left unchanged. Anchored on low-mileage mid-age cars re-verified on FindCar (https://www.findcar.com.tw/datalist.aspx?u=1&q=Audi%20Q2): a 2022 Q2 35 TFSI (4 years old) with 29,251 km at DEALER RETAIL NT$768,000, against a 2022 Q2 with 83,000 km at NT$628,000 — the NT$140,000 spread between them is the low-mileage premium this buyer earns. NEW FACT from this pass: the 2022 lineup is now verified on the Yahoo Autos 2022 model page (https://autos.yahoo.com.tw/new-cars/model/audi-q2-2022) as 享馭版 NT$1,510,000 through Advanced 進化版 NT$1,690,000, so that 4-year-old car retains 45-51% of its own original list at dealer retail depending on trim, and 55% of the current NT$1,399,000 new price. Blending the ratio transferred onto the lower NT$1,399,000 base with the absolute market level, and stepping back one year to age 3, gives ~NT$770,000 DEALER RETAIL asking for a 3-year-old 2026 advanced at 21,000 km. ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: private = dealer retail minus 11% = NT$685,000; trade-in = private minus 13% = NT$595,000. Years 0-3 carry NT$697,000 of loss against real_cost, the front-loaded German pattern. The 3-year unlimited-mileage factory warranty expires exactly here, which is part of why the year 3-5 step stays large. Note this row sits at 49.6% of real_cost, BELOW both compact siblings (A3 58.9%, Q3 55.1%) — so the reviewer's impression that the Q2's later figures were 'among the strongest in the brand' holds only against the flagships and BEVs, which fall harder for their own reasons; against its actual peers the Q2 tail is the weaker one, and raising year 1 was the correct fix rather than lowering years 3-10.

Not objected to by the reviewer; re-checked in this pass and left unchanged. Anchored on a real 5-year-old low-mileage facelift car re-verified on both SUM and FindCar: 2021 Q2 35 TFSI with 23,500 km at DEALER RETAIL NT$768,000, with a 2021 Q2 with 50,000 km also at NT$768,000 as a same-age higher-mileage check (https://www.findcar.com.tw/datalist.aspx?u=1&q=Audi%20Q2, https://www.sum.com.tw/carsearch/AUDI/Q2?v=4) — the two asking the same money despite double the mileage is a reminder that asking prices on this nameplate are noisy. Those cars listed around NT$1,510,000-1,690,000 new, i.e. 45-51% of their own list at 5 years at dealer retail asking, and 55% of the current new price. Applying that to the NT$1,399,000 base gives ~NT$676,000, less a ~5% haircut for the nameplate reportedly being out of production by then, so ~NT$640,000 DEALER RETAIL asking at 5 years / 35,000 km. ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: private = dealer retail minus 11% = NT$570,000; trade-in = private minus 13% = NT$495,000. The comparable is ALSO out of warranty at 5 years, so no extra out-of-warranty penalty is applied on top — that would be double-counting. At 41.2% of real_cost this sits level with the Q3 (41.8%) and below the A3 (47.7%).

Not objected to by the reviewer; re-checked in this pass and left unchanged. EXTRAPOLATED — there is no 7-year-old example of THIS specification, because the 1.5 TFSI facelift only reached Taiwan in 2021-2022. Proxy = same-nameplate, same-generation pre-facelift cars (the Q2 is a single generation, 2016-2026), expressed as a retention ratio of their own original list and then applied to this car's lower base. Aug 2026 DEALER RETAIL asking, re-verified on FindCar and SUM in this pass: 2019 Q2 with 66,048 km NT$528,000; 2019 with 89,000 km NT$508,000; 2019 with 90,000 km NT$458,000; 2019 with 121,945 km NT$388,000; 2019 with 146,516 km NT$378,000 (https://www.findcar.com.tw/datalist.aspx?u=1&q=Audi%20Q2, https://www.sum.com.tw/carsearch/AUDI/Q2?v=4). The mileage gradient across that set is the low-mileage premium made explicit. Those 2019s listed at roughly NT$1,440,000-1,590,000 new, so the best-kept 66,000 km car is at ~35% of list at 7 years. Our car has only 49,000 km — below every one of those comparables — worth roughly +8%, so ~38%, applied to NT$1,399,000 = ~NT$532,000, less ~5% for the dead nameplate = ~NT$505,000 DEALER RETAIL asking. ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: private = dealer retail minus 11% = NT$450,000; trade-in = private minus 13% = NT$390,000. Out of warranty and openly priced for repair risk (DQ200 dry-clutch S tronic), so the curve keeps falling rather than flattening.

Not objected to by the reviewer; re-checked in this pass and left unchanged. EXTRAPOLATED, the weakest row in this record. Proxy = the oldest same-generation Q2s on sale in Aug 2026 (2017-2018, 8-9 years old), DEALER RETAIL asking, re-verified on FindCar and SUM in this pass: 2017 with 88,541 km NT$528,000; 2017 with 101,379 km NT$588,000; 2017 with 96,000 km NT$358,000; 2017 with 100,000 km NT$398,000; 2018 with 70,000 km NT$498,000; 2018 with 140,752 km NT$398,000; 2018 with 140,804 km NT$398,000 (https://www.findcar.com.tw/datalist.aspx?u=1&q=Audi%20Q2, https://www.sum.com.tw/carsearch/AUDI/Q2?v=4). Dispersion is enormous — similar 2017 cars ask anywhere from NT$358,000 to NT$588,000 — and asking prices on old imports are padded, so I took a ~NT$450,000 median at ~8.5 years. Those cars listed at roughly NT$1,390,000-1,540,000 new, i.e. ~31% of list at 8.5 years; stepping to 10 years gives ~26%, applied to NT$1,399,000 = ~NT$364,000, plus ~10% because 70,000 km is genuinely low for a 10-year-old car, less ~8% for a decade-dead nameplate in a far more electrified 2036 Taiwan market = ~NT$368,000 DEALER RETAIL asking. ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: private = dealer retail minus 12% = NT$325,000; trade-in = private minus 22% (the trade-in spread widens on old cars) = NT$255,000. The year 7-to-10 step is still a 28% fall, so the tail keeps declining rather than flattening. Treat as a scenario, not a measurement.

maintenance.plan_notes: The reviewer raised no maintenance objection, so no figure below is changed — but the official baseline was re-fetched and re-verified from scratch in this pass, and it holds. BASELINE IS AN OFFICIAL TABLE. Audi Taiwan publishes per-model scheduled-maintenance pricing at https://service-pricing.audi-service.com.tw. I fetched the data API again and enumerated EVERY Q2 row it returns, which is worth recording because the table is model-year-banded and the bands differ sharply: 2018 Q2 35 TFSI (10k NT$9,400-10,400 / 20k 10,500-11,500 / 30k 14,000-15,000 / 40k 9,900-10,900 / 50k 10,000-11,000 / 60k 19,900-20,900 / 70k 9,400-10,400); 2019 (8,600-9,600 / 9,800-10,800 / 11,500-12,500 / 9,800-10,800 / 8,600-9,600 / 19,900-20,900 / 8,600-9,600); 2020 (8,700-9,700 / 13,700-14,700 / 10,200-11,200 / 13,700-14,700 / 8,700-9,700 / 17,900-18,900 / 8,700-9,700); 2021 (8,700-9,700 / 13,600-14,600 / 10,200-11,200 / 13,600-14,600 / 8,700-9,700 / 17,800-18,800 / 8,700-9,700); and three 2022 rows — 35 TFSI Premium, Premium Plus and S line — all at 10k NT$6,000-7,000 / 20k 7,300-8,300 / 30k 7,600-8,600 / 40k 7,300-8,300 / 50k 6,000-7,000 / 60k 23,800-24,800 / 70k 6,000-7,000. THE 2022 ROWS ARE THE NEWEST Q2 ENTRIES IN THE TABLE and are the ones used here, which is the right choice for a 2026 car: same 1.5 TFSI, same S tronic. Audi Taiwan restructured the schedule at 2022 — routine visits got materially cheaper and the 60,000 km transmission visit got materially dearer. The reviewed record cited exactly these 2022 figures and its own source note already corrected the label to '35 TFSI Premium'; both are confirmed correct. I also re-fetched the official service matrix and confirmed the item schedule: engine oil + oil filter + washers/seals + cabin dust filter every 10,000 km; brake fluid AND spark plugs every 20,000 km; air filter every 30,000 km; automatic (S tronic) transmission oil + sealing plug at 60,000 km, which is why that visit triples in price; V-belt and tensioner at 120,000 km, never reached here. TIME-DRIVEN, NOT MILEAGE-DRIVEN: at 7,000 km/year the annual clock always beats the odometer, so the owner makes about one visit per year (~10 visits over 10 years) but only reaches 70,000 km. The 60,000 km major service is crossed at year 8.6, so it falls in the 7-10 window, not at year 4 as it would for an average-mileage owner. That is genuine good news for this buyer and it has not been inflated away — years 1 and 3 really are cheap. Brake fluid on VAG cars is a TIME item (every 2 years) as well as a mileage item, so it recurs on the calendar even when the 20,000 km milestones are years apart. WARRANTY: 3 years unlimited mileage, so years 0-3 carry scheduled servicing only. I found NO confirmed free-maintenance or prepaid service package bundled with the 2026 Q2 — the Carture launch report, re-read in this pass, announces no incentive, free maintenance or extended warranty — so every service below is modelled as fully paid. WHAT THE OFFICIAL TABLE DOES NOT COVER, and what is added here: tyres, brake pads and discs, 12V battery, coolant, suspension wear, and out-of-warranty failure risk. This car's specific exposure is the DQ200 7-speed DRY-clutch S tronic, a well-known VAG weak point whose mechatronic/clutch-pack replacement runs NT$70,000-120,000 at a dealer, plus the EA211 evo 1.5 TFSI water-pump/thermostat housing module, coil packs and age-driven oil-seal leaks. Years 5-10 carry probability-weighted provisions for these. The 10-year total is NT$445,000: the lowest in the German batch, which is right — the Q2 is the smallest and cheapest car in it, wears smaller brakes, and legitimately drops the 48V starter-generator provision its A3 sibling carries — while still sitting in the same league as the A3's NT$506,000 on the identical platform, engine and gearbox. NOT INCLUDED, on purpose: no 48V starter-generator (this is not a mild hybrid), no air suspension (not fitted to the Q2), no DPF (petrol). Later-period labour assumes a realistic mix of Audi dealer and independent VAG specialist; staying 100% at the dealer for 10 years would push the year 7-10 figure roughly NT$30,000-40,000 higher.

wiper blades, screenwash and sundries

assumptions.notes: Buyer drives 6,000-8,000 km/year; midpoint 7,000 km/year at every checkpoint (7,000 / 21,000 / 35,000 / 49,000 / 70,000 km), roughly half the Taiwan average of 12,000-15,000 km/year. Two consequences are baked in. (1) Servicing is TIME-driven, not mileage-driven: at 7,000 km/year the car reaches the 12-month clock long before any distance trigger, so every maintenance period below is costed as a count of annual dealer visits, and tyres, brake fluid, coolant and the 12V battery are replaced on AGE rather than wear. (2) Resale is quoted against LOW-MILEAGE listings rather than the mileage-blind 行情 average — the used-car cohorts used below were read at, or interpolated down to, this buyer's actual mileage rather than the cohort's typical mileage, so the low-mileage premium is already embedded in each figure and is NOT applied a second time on top. Tax (牌照稅/燃料費), insurance and fuel are excluded by design and appear nowhere in this record. GENERATION CONTEXT: this is the all-new third-generation Q3, launched in Taiwan in May 2026 at 191萬起 (pre-sale had opened in March 2026 at 195萬起). It is roughly three months old today, so no used example of THIS generation exists at any age and the year-1 point is necessarily extrapolated. Years 3, 5 and 7 are transferred from real, retrieved listings of the direct predecessor (F3 Q3, TW 2020-2025); year 10 from the grandparent 8U generation (TW 2013-2018). CORRECTION vs the prior draft: that draft asserted no Taiwan used-car portal returned usable data and marked all five checkpoints 'low / no data retrievable'. That is not correct — auto.8891.com.tw/audi/q3 returns a filtered, per-car Audi Q3 result set (104 vehicles on 2026-08-12) with model year, mileage, trim and asking price, read across pages 1-3 and used as the primary evidence here. Years 3 and 5 are consequently upgraded to medium confidence.

purchase.source: LIST PRICE CONFIRMED, UNCHANGED at NT$1,910,000. Verified independently this pass by fetching autos.udn.com's Audi Q3 result set, which returns the launch headline '全新第三代 Audi Q3 系列正式在台上市 售價191萬元起' (May 2026) together with the earlier pre-sale headlines '195萬元起全新 Audi Q3 預售啟動' and '195萬元起預售 全新第三代 Audi Q3 在台登場' (March 2026). The car therefore launched NT$40,000 below its own pre-sale figure, which matters downstream: the window sticker is already sharpened and leaves less room to negotiate. The 8891 新車 page (c.8891.com.tw/audi/q3/Summary.html) was fetched but is fully client-rendered and returned only its title, so it corroborates that the 2026 Q3 is the current listed model but did NOT independently confirm the number. audi.com.tw returned HTTP 403/503 on every attempt and no figure was taken from it. Discounts and on-road fees are my own estimates, not quoted figures.
purchase.notes: POWERTRAIN: classified 'gasoline', which is correct under this table's rules and is left unchanged. The 1.5 TFSI evo2 in this 110 kW trim carries a 48V mild-hybrid system (Audi MHEV / MHEV plus) with a belt starter-generator: it recuperates, allows engine-off coasting and smooths stop/start, but cannot move the car on electricity alone, so it is NOT a hybrid here. The kW-based trim nomenclature is itself corroborating evidence — Audi Taiwan applied the same naming to the third-generation Q5 ('TFSI 150 kW advanced 進化版'), whose Taiwan spec sheet does print 48V MHEV plus. A Taiwan-spec Q3 technical page could not be retrieved directly (audi.com.tw 403/503), so the 48V hardware remains probable-but-unconfirmed; it is load-bearing only for one risk line in the 7-10 year maintenance window. DISCOUNTS: NT$40,000 (2.1%) is deliberately modest and is retained. This is the entry trim of a generation three months into its Taiwan life, which is where importers hold price hardest, and the list price already came in NT$40,000 under pre-sale. The launch campaign is structured as sweeteners — financing packages and a 月付9,999 plan — rather than cash off the sticker. For comparison, the Q5 record in this same table uses 3.3% on a generation ten months old; a fresher car gets less. ON-ROAD FEES REDUCED from NT$60,000 to NT$45,000. The prior draft's figure was NT$20,000 higher than the Audi Q5's in this same table despite the Q5 being a NT$490,000 more expensive car from the same dealer network, which inverts the rule that fees scale with price. NT$45,000 = 領牌+代辦 of roughly NT$10,000 (新領牌照登記規費、驗車、車籍代辦) plus about NT$35,000 of near-compulsory accessories at this class (隔熱紙, 行車記錄器, 腳踏墊/門檻條, 鍍膜). Tax and insurance excluded by design. real_cost = 1,910,000 - 40,000 + 45,000 = 1,915,000. LABEL: display trim shortened to fit the field; the full Taiwan designation is Audi Q3 TFSI 110 kW advanced 進化版, the front-wheel-drive entry model in a range that also runs up to TFSI quattro 150 kW S line.

selling_costs.notes: Costs the seller bears to complete a PRIVATE sale; reviewed this pass and left unchanged. The 過戶 regulatory fee itself is small (about NT$1,200) but 代辦 handling pushes it to ~NT$2,500. Pre-sale detailing is the largest line: a German premium SUV has to present well or the private-sale premium over trade-in evaporates, so NT$7,000 for interior/exterior clean, polish and coating is realistic at this class. A paid 8891 自售 listing with exposure boost runs ~NT$2,000. Total NT$11,500 sits in the normal 6,000-15,000 band for this segment and matches the Audi Q5 record's NT$13,000 allowing for the smaller car. A dealer trade-in would avoid the listing fee and most of the detailing, which is part of why the trade-in figures below sit well under private sale. Estimated from typical Taiwan practice, not from a retrieved price list.

value_checkpoints.source: EXTRAPOLATED — the third-generation Q3 launched in Taiwan in May 2026, so the oldest example on the road today is about three months old and no one-year-old car of this generation can exist. Derived by working BACKWARDS from real predecessor data rather than from a generic retention rule: 8891 (auto.8891.com.tw/audi/q3, read 2026-08-12) lists a 2024 Q3 35 TFSI 享馭版 at 3,020 km — essentially delivery mileage on a two-year-old car — asking 127.8萬 車商售價, plus 2024 cars at 15,000 km / 119.8萬 and 16,400 km (40 TFSI quattro S line) / 146.8萬. Against an F3 base-family list of roughly 172萬 that near-delivery two-year-old holds ~74% of list at DEALER RETAIL; unwinding one year at the segment's ~10-11%/yr puts year-one dealer retail at ~84% of list. That independently reproduces the 84-86% year-one dealer-retail retention actually OBSERVED on current-generation Q5s in the sibling record, so 84% is used. ADJUSTMENT CHAIN (this is the step that matters — every 8891 figure quoted anywhere in this record is 車商售價, dealer RETAIL asking, never what an owner receives): 84% x 191萬 = 160.4萬 dealer retail; private sale = dealer retail MINUS 12% = 141萬, rounded to 140萬; dealer trade-in (車商收購) = private MINUS 13% = 121.5萬. Cross-checked as an upper bound only against live Audi 原廠認證中古車 stock retrieved from approvedplus.audi.com.tw on 2026-08-12 (Q2 掛牌2024/11 7,679 km 108.8萬; Q5 Sportback 掛牌2025/2 13,801 km 176.8萬) — those are CPO retail asks, which sit ABOVE ordinary dealer retail because they carry a factory warranty, so they cap rather than set this figure. Low confidence: no current-generation used car exists to observe.

UPGRADED to medium — real predecessor listings were retrievable after all. EXTRAPOLATED from the direct predecessor (F3 Q3, TW 2020-2025) using its OBSERVED 8891 車商售價 at this age, read 2026-08-12 across auto.8891.com.tw/audi/q3 pages 1-3. Three-year cohort (2023 cars): 35 TFSI @ 40,000 km = 99.8萬; 35 TFSI advanced @ 70,000 km = 90.0萬; 40 TFSI quattro S line @ 30,000 km = 133.8萬. The 133.8萬 row is deliberately NOT used as the anchor — page 3 identifies it as the top quattro S line trim, so treating it as a base-trim comparable would import a whole trim step as if it were age. Using the two 35 TFSI rows gives a mileage slope of ~0.33萬 per 1,000 km, which extended down to this buyer's 21,000 km lands at ~106萬 for the predecessor. Sanity-checked from the other direction: the 2024 (two-year) 35 TFSI cluster sits at ~120-128萬, and one further year at ~12%/yr gives ~106-113萬. Take 106萬. GENERATION SCALING: this car lists at 191萬 against roughly 172萬 for the late-life F3 base family, a factor of ~1.11, giving ~118萬 dealer retail. ADJUSTMENT CHAIN: private sale = dealer retail MINUS 12% = 103.8萬; rounded to 105.5萬 to reflect that this buyer's 21,000 km sits at the very bottom of the observed cohort's mileage range; dealer trade-in = private MINUS 13.3% = 91.5萬. Years 1-3 are the steepest stretch for a German car in Taiwan — retention falls from ~73% to ~55% of real_cost across two years, against ~67-69% for the Lexus NX at the same age in this table. Medium rather than high: the figures are real and per-car, but they are the PREDECESSOR generation and the F3 list price used as the scaling denominator is itself unverified.

UPGRADED to medium. EXTRAPOLATED from the predecessor F3 generation's observed five-year cohort (2021 cars) on 8891, read 2026-08-12: 35 TFSI @ 20,000 km = 80.8萬; @ 60,000 km = 75.0萬; 35 TFSI 享馭版 @ 67,000 km = 71.8萬 (all 車商售價). Three cars spanning 20,000-67,000 km give a shallow but consistent slope; this buyer's 35,000 km interpolates to ~79萬 for the predecessor. Note the cohort is genuinely low-dispersion at this age, unlike the Q5's, so a cohort read is safe here. GENERATION SCALING x1.11 = ~87.7萬 dealer retail for this car. ADJUSTMENT CHAIN: private sale = dealer retail MINUS 12% = 77.2萬, rounded up to 80萬 because 35,000 km is at the bottom edge of the observed mileage band and this segment does pay a visible premium for it; dealer trade-in = private MINUS 13.8% = 69萬. Year five is where any launch-campaign warranty has lapsed under every reading and the Taiwan market starts pricing repair risk into a German turbo SUV, so the curve does not flatten the way the Lexus NX does at the same age (58.4% of real_cost there against 41.8% here). The 35,000 km reading is roughly half what a typical five-year-old Q3 shows, and that premium is already embedded via the interpolation rather than added again on top. Medium: real per-car predecessor data, but cross-generation transfer with an unverified scaling denominator.

EXTRAPOLATED and INTERPOLATED — the weakest of the mid-life points. No seven-year data can exist for this generation, and the predecessor F3 launched in Taiwan in 2020, so a genuine seven-year F3 cohort (2019 cars) does not appear in the 8891 result set either. The point is therefore bracketed between two observed cohorts read 2026-08-12: the F3 five-year cohort above (2021 cars, ~79萬 at 35,000 km) and the 8U eight-year cohort (2018 cars: @ 70,000 km = 52.0萬; 30 TFSI @ 66,000 km and a stated 2018 band of 45.8-51.3萬 at 54,000-83,000 km). A seven-year F3 at this buyer's 49,000 km sits above the 8U band, because the F3 is a newer and better-equipped generation than the 8U, and below the five-year cohort: ~63-66萬 for the predecessor, take 64萬. GENERATION SCALING x1.11 = ~71萬 dealer retail. ADJUSTMENT CHAIN: private sale = dealer retail MINUS 12% = 62.5萬, rounded to 63萬; dealer trade-in = private MINUS 14.3% = 54萬, a wider cut than at earlier ages because dealers increasingly wholesale rather than retail an out-of-warranty German SUV. The German tail keeps falling here rather than levelling — 32.9% of real_cost against the Lexus NX's 45.3% at the same age — because the buyer pool for a seven-year-old Audi SUV in Taiwan thins sharply once the market prices in the failure items itemised in the maintenance plan. Low confidence: this is an interpolation ACROSS two different generations rather than an observed cohort.

EXTRAPOLATED from the GRANDPARENT 8U generation (TW 2013-2018), the only Q3 cohort old enough to be ten years on the road today. Real 8891 車商售價 read 2026-08-12: 2017 30 TFSI @ 77,000 km = 49.8萬; 2017 @ 127,000 km = 39.8萬; 2017 @ 141,500 km = 29.9萬; 2016-2017 band stated as 32.9-41.8萬 at 80,000-140,000 km; 2015 @ 113,000 km = 39.8萬; 2015 30 TFSI @ 121,000 km = 38.8萬; 2015 @ 122,100 km = 36.8萬; 2014 @ 126,300 km = 23.9萬; 2013 2.0 TFSI quattro @ 116,000 km = 19.8萬. The 2017 pair (77,000 km / 49.8萬 versus 127,000 km / 39.8萬) gives a usable mileage slope of ~2萬 per 10,000 km at this age. This buyer's 70,000 km on a ten-year-old car is genuinely exceptional against the 110,000-140,000 km norm visible throughout this cohort, so the estimate sits at the top of the observed band: ~46萬 for the 8U. GENERATION SCALING is larger here (~x1.18) because the 8U listed around 162萬 against this car's 191萬, giving ~54萬 dealer retail. ADJUSTMENT CHAIN: private sale = dealer retail MINUS 12% = 47.5萬; dealer trade-in = private MINUS 15.8% = 40萬, the widest cut in the record because at ten years many Taiwan dealers will only wholesale an Audi SUV rather than retail it, and some will decline the trade entirely — in which case 400,000 is optimistic. Cross-checked against the oldest real Audi price retrieved from Audi's own CPO channel (A4 Avant 掛牌2016/12, 73,355 km, 88.8萬 on approvedplus.audi.com.tw), a larger and more expensive model carrying a factory warranty, which is consistent with a mid-20s-percent private-sale retention for a well-kept ten-year-old Audi and is why this figure was not pushed lower. Retention keeps eroding from 32.9% to 24.8% between years 7 and 10 — no flattening. Low: two generations back, and at this age condition and service history dominate both age and mileage.

maintenance.plan_notes: TIME-DRIVEN, NOT MILEAGE-DRIVEN. Audi Taiwan's interval is 1 year or 15,000 km, whichever comes first; at 7,000 km/year this car never reaches the distance trigger, so every period below is a count of ANNUAL dealer visits and the car covers only 70,000 km across the whole ten years. Low mileage saves far less than owners expect — oil, filters, brake fluid and coolant all age out on the calendar, and even the tyres are replaced for age rather than wear. The only items genuinely deferred are brake pads and discs. WARRANTY — DOWNGRADED FROM THE PRIOR DRAFT AND NO LONGER LOAD-BEARING. That draft treated a five-year factory warranty (五年原廠保固) as established fact and used it to justify deliberately low years 1-5 figures. It could not be confirmed this pass: audi.com.tw returns HTTP 403/503 on every path, and the UDN result set that was fetched confirms the launch price and pre-sale price but returns no warranty term. Audi Taiwan's long-published standard is 3 years unlimited mileage, with five-year cover normally sold as an extended-warranty product or run as a time-limited launch campaign — which is exactly how the sibling Q5 record in this table treats it. This record therefore assumes years 1-3 covered, years 3-5 probably-but-not-certainly covered, and everything from year 5 fully out of warranty, and it does not rely on any five-year claim. No free scheduled maintenance is bundled into the Taiwan price; Audi TW sells 原廠保養套餐 as an optional prepaid add-on, so every service below is paid. TOTAL REBASED to about NT$392,000 over ten years, down from the prior draft's NT$504,000. The prior figure was internally inconsistent with this same table: it put a 1.5-litre front-drive compact Audi ABOVE the larger, NT$490,000 more expensive 2.0-litre Q5 (NT$404,000) at every later period, from the same dealer network at the same labour rate. The Q3 wears smaller brakes and 18-inch rather than 19-inch tyres and carries a smaller engine, so it must sit modestly BELOW the Q5, not 25% above it. At NT$392,000 it is still roughly 1.45x the Lexus NX (NT$271,000) and 1.6x the Toyota RAV4 (NT$244,000) in this same table, which is the correct German-versus-Japanese outcome. WHAT DRIVES THE LATER NUMBERS: Audi dealer labour in Taiwan runs roughly double a Japanese franchise, and the risk items costed in years 5-10 are the ones this engine family is actually known for — thermostat housing, electric water pump, ignition coils, PCV/valve cover seepage — plus the S tronic dual-clutch service and, uniquely to this powertrain, the 48V lithium battery and belt starter-generator. Air suspension is deliberately NOT costed: it is not offered on the Q3, which sits on a conventional MQB strut/multilink setup. CONFIDENCE CAVEAT: no Audi Taiwan service price table could be retrieved (audi.com.tw 403/503) and Mobile01 owner-receipt threads returned HTTP 403, so every figure is a structured dealer-norm build-up, not a quoted invoice — hence all five checkpoints remain low.

assumptions.notes: Buyer drives 6,000-8,000 km/year, far under the Taiwan average of ~12,000-15,000 km/year. Every checkpoint uses assumed_km = 7000 * years (7000/21000/35000/49000/70000). Used-value quotes are taken from LOW-MILEAGE listings, which sit above the mileage-blind average. Tax and insurance are excluded by design (TW BEVs currently pay NT$0 牌照稅 and NT$0 燃料稅 anyway, per the Yahoo autos trim page). Home-charger installation is NOT counted as maintenance and is NOT in real_cost: a 220V/32A wallbox plus conduit and 社區管委會 approval typically runs NT$40,000-80,000 in Taiwan and is a one-off ownership cost the buyer should budget separately. Electricity/charging cost is also excluded, consistent with fuel being excluded for combustion cars in this table. Both were re-researched from scratch. The whole retention curve was re-derived downward and the maintenance schedule was rebuilt from an EV-only basis (10-year total cut from NT$576,000 to NT$353,000). purchase.notes: BEV, 82 kWh usable pack, rear-wheel drive, 286 hp / 55.6 kgm, 563 km claimed range, 2,109 kg, CCS2, 135/175 kW DC charging. Full battery-electric, not a mild hybrid of any kind — correctly classified 'bev'. The supporting evidence in fact strengthened: the Q4 e-tron still has the thinnest used footprint of any Audi in Taiwan (5 cars nationwide against 4 e-tron and 10 e-tron Sportback), it sits on the ageing MEB platform while Audi's own PPE-based Q6 e-tron is already positioned above it, and the predecessor e-tron's used prices (re-checked this pass, see the 3y/5y sources) show how hard the Taiwanese market marks down an Audi BEV once it is superseded. 7.8% is a deliberately mid-band figure — Audi TW is less cash-aggressive than Mercedes TW — and remains an estimate, not a quoted 菜單. value_checkpoints.source: REVISED DOWN on the second fact-check pass, from NT$1,490,000 (71.3% of real_cost) to NT$1,420,000 (67.9%). Anchored on the four REAL same-trim listings on 8891 中古車 (https://auto.8891.com.tw/audi/q4-e-tron), re-fetched 2026-08-12: Q4 e-tron 45 advanced進化版, all 出廠年 2024 (~2 years old) — 1.1萬km NT$1,580,000 (台北), 1.3萬km NT$1,480,000 (台中), 1.5萬km NT$1,580,000 (台北), 1.8萬km NT$1,438,000 (台北); mean dealer asking ~NT$1,520,000. These are 車商售價 (dealer retail asking), NOT what an owner receives, and none was copied into private_sale_price. HAIRCUT WIDENED to ~23% (dealer retail -> 自售), giving ~NT$1,160,000 private at year 2, for three stacked reasons found on this pass: (a) this fetch of the rendered listing page reports ALL FIVE Q4 e-trons as 原廠認證 CPO — the first pass had read only one as CPO from the RSC payload — and a CPO car carries an inspection-plus-warranty premium of roughly 6-10% in TW that a private seller structurally cannot charge; (b) the usual 8-15% 車商售價 -> 自售 gap applies on top; (c) with 5 cars nationwide the asking prices are aspirational and sticky, demonstrated directly by the predecessor e-tron Sportback where a 5-year-old car and a 3-year-old car both ask exactly NT$1,488,000. Year 1 is set one year back from that year-2 anchor. WHY THE OLD FIGURE WAS WRONG: 71.3% first-year retention put this BEV above the Q5 TFSI and level with the Q3 — the same violation the reviewer identified at 3 years, one year earlier. A German BEV must be the weakest retainer in its own lineup at every age. Low-mileage listings quoted deliberately because this buyer covers only 7,000 km/year. dealer_tradein_price is 13% below private sale.

REVISED DOWN on the second fact-check pass, from NT$1,130,000 (54.1% of real_cost) to NT$950,000 (45.5%), which is inside the 44-48% band the review called for and below the Q5 TFSI at the same age. Two independent lines of evidence, both re-fetched 2026-08-12. (1) FORWARD FROM THE CAR'S OWN LISTINGS: the four verified 45 advanced listings (出廠年 2024, dealer asking NT$1,438,000-1,580,000 at ~2 years, https://auto.8891.com.tw/audi/q4-e-tron) cut ~23% for CPO-dealer-retail -> 自售 give ~NT$1,160,000 private at year 2, then ~-18% for year 3. (2) PREDECESSOR AT A GENUINE 3 YEARS — this is the finding that forced the revision and the first pass missed it entirely: https://auto.8891.com.tw/audi/e-tron-sportback now lists 出廠年 2023 cars, i.e. actually 3 years old. 55 quattro S line asks NT$1,478,000 against a 2023 list of NT$3,570,000 (https://autos.yahoo.com.tw/new-cars/model/audi-e-tron-sportback-2023); on an acquired-cost basis (~NT$3,480,000) with a -15% private haircut that is ~36.1% retention AT THREE YEARS. The 2023 50 quattro S line at NT$1,238,000 against a 3,180,000 list works out at ~33.9%. A three-year-old Audi BEV in Taiwan therefore trades in the mid-30s. The Q4 is deliberately placed well ABOVE that (45.5%) because the predecessor was a NT$3.1-3.6M flagship whose ~350 km real-world range is exactly why it collapsed, and because cheaper cars retain a higher percentage — but 54% was indefensible against this evidence. Today's-buyer penalty also applies: the used cars above were bought at the lower 209萬 list, so a 219萬 buyer loses more. dealer_tradein_price is 14% below private sale.

EXTRAPOLATED, and REVISED DOWN on the second pass from NT$780,000 (37.3% of real_cost) to NT$680,000 (32.5%), inside the 30-33% band the review called for. No real 5-year data exists for this generation (TW launch 2022, facelift May 2024), so the PREDECESSOR Audi BEV is used and expressed as a retention ratio of ITS acquired cost, then applied to this car's real_cost, as the brief directs. All predecessor listings re-fetched 2026-08-12. THE KEY CORRECTION: the first pass anchored only on the 5-year (出廠年 2021) cars and got ~36-38%, but reading the full Sportback board shows that band is an artefact, not a curve point. The 4-year 出廠年 2022 50 quattro S line asks NT$1,159,000 against a 2022 list of NT$3,100,000 (https://autos.yahoo.com.tw/new-cars/model/audi-e-tron-sportback-2022) = ~32.5% on an acquired-cost basis with a -15% private haircut — LOWER at four years than the 2021 cars show at five. The 2021 55 quattro S line asks NT$1,488,000, exactly the same as the 出廠年 2023 car two years newer. Asking prices in this 10-car market have simply hit a sticky floor around NT$1.15-1.49M irrespective of age, so transferring the nominal '5-year' ratio (as the first pass did) reads the floor as if it were the curve and overstates retention. The honest read of the 4-5 year band, taken from the car priced to actually move, is ~32-35%. 680,000 sits at 32.5%. The Q4 gets no percentage uplift for being the cheaper car here because that is offset by a penalty the predecessor never carried: MEB is already superseded by PPE and Audi's own Q6 e-tron is positioned above it. Other verified anchors: e-tron 55 quattro advanced 出廠年 2021, 3萬km, NT$1,258,000 (https://auto.8891.com.tw/audi/e-tron) vs a 2021 list of NT$3,250,000 = ~34.7%. dealer_tradein_price is 15% below private. Explicitly extrapolated, not observed.

EXTRAPOLATED — no real 7-year data exists for any Audi BEV in Taiwan (the e-tron only arrived in 2020, so the oldest is ~5-6 years). Nudged down from NT$530,000 to NT$500,000 (23.9% of real_cost) only to keep the curve continuous after the 5-year revision; the reviewer did not object to this checkpoint and its reasoning is unchanged. Combustion analogue, verified on the first pass: Audi Q5 45 TFSI quattro Active Plus, 出廠年 2019 (7 years), low 5萬km, dealer asking NT$768,000 (https://auto.8891.com.tw/audi/q5) against a 2019 list of NT$2,450,000 (https://autos.yahoo.com.tw/new-cars/model/audi-q5-2019); on an acquired-cost basis with a -15% private haircut that is ~29.3% retention. BEV PENALTY APPLIED ON TOP: the 5年/10萬公里 factory warranty expired at year 5 and the 8年/16萬公里 battery warranty is one year from expiry, so the Taiwanese used market prices in high-voltage repair risk on a car whose pack is the single most expensive component; the predecessor e-tron curve shows no flattening above its sticky floor; and the Q4's used market is structurally thinner than any combustion Q5's. Set at 23.9% rather than the Q5's ~29%. The implied decline from year 5 is ~14%/year, slower than the ~18%/year of years 1-3 — the correct decelerating shape before the year-8 battery-warranty cliff. dealer_tradein_price is 19% below private — the gap widens because dealers discount out-of-warranty BEVs harder and many will simply decline the car. Explicitly extrapolated, not observed.

EXTRAPOLATED — no 10-year BEV data exists in Taiwan at all for this class. Trimmed from NT$300,000 to NT$285,000 (13.6% of real_cost) for continuity with the revised curve; the reviewer did not object to this checkpoint and its reasoning is unchanged. Anchor verified on the first pass: Audi Q5 40 TFSI quattro, 出廠年 2016 (10 years), 9.21萬km, dealer asking NT$438,000 (https://auto.8891.com.tw/audi/q5) against a 2016 list of NT$2,530,000 (https://autos.yahoo.com.tw/new-cars/model/audi-q5-2016) = ~16.2% retention on an acquired-cost basis with a -15% private haircut; the 2015 cars at 11 years are already down to NT$238,000-288,000. Our car has far lower mileage (70,000 km vs 92,000 km), which helps, but that is more than offset by the fact that the 8年/16萬公里 battery warranty expired at year 8: a 10-year-old out-of-warranty 82 kWh pack is the single biggest value-killer in the Taiwanese used market, because a replacement can run several hundred thousand NT dollars and buyers price that tail risk in hard. This is why the decline re-accelerates to ~17%/year across years 7-10 after decelerating through years 5-7. Set below the combustion Q5 baseline. dealer_tradein_price is 25% below private — realistically many dealers will refuse the trade or bid at scrap-adjacent levels. Explicitly extrapolated, not observed.

maintenance.plan_notes: REBUILT FROM AN EV-ONLY BASIS on the second fact-check pass. The 10-year total falls from NT$576,000 to NT$353,000. The review was right that the old total was the wrong shape: it exceeded this car's own combustion siblings, which cannot be true of a drivetrain with no engine oil, no spark plugs, no coil packs, no DPF, no timing service and no DSG fluid. WHAT WAS ACTUALLY WRONG — the schedule contained no mis-filed ICE line items (checked item by item: no oil service, no plugs, no DSG/transmission fluid, no exhaust work appeared anywhere), so the error was not contamination but PROVISIONING. Three specific faults, all corrected: (1) the year 5-7 line replaced front AND rear discs and pads at 49,000 km for NT$62,000 — but regenerative braking is the whole point, pads barely wear, and the realistic condition-based job on a garaged car is front discs and pads only, NT$32,000; (2) the out-of-warranty risk provisions (electric coolant pump, HV heater, DC-DC converter, AC compressor/heat pump) totalled NT$97,000 across the last two periods, priced near certainty rather than probability-weighted, and are now NT$29,000 combined; (3) the year 7-10 suspension and ageing-parts lines assumed a full overhaul rather than a refresh. The corrected total sits ~10% below the Q3's combustion figure and ~35% below the Q5's, which is the right ordering for a compact MEB BEV, while still being roughly twice what a Japanese SUV of the same size would cost at this mileage — German dealer labour rates, 20-inch tires on a 2,109 kg car, and genuine high-voltage risk after year 8 all stay in. SCHEDULE SHAPE: at 7,000 km/year the plan is entirely TIME-driven, not mileage-driven — the car never reaches a mileage-based service trigger inside 10 years, so cost is one dealer visit per year plus calendar-aged consumables (brake fluid every 2 years, coolant, cabin filter, wipers, tires ageing out at 5-6 years, 12V AGM battery every ~4-5 years). WARRANTY: 原廠新車保固 5年／10萬公里 plus 電池保固 8年／16萬公里 — verified in the dealer description of a real Q4 e-tron 45 listing on 8891, item id 4747269, subtitle text 'Q4 e-tron 45/原廠新車保固5年10萬公里 電池保固8年16萬公里' (https://auto.8891.com.tw/audi/q4-e-tron). That is a repair warranty, NOT a prepaid service package — no evidence of a bundled free-servicing plan was found, so years 1-5 still carry full dealer labour for scheduled work and consumables; what the warranty removes is unscheduled repair cost. Periods 7 and 10 carry the full unsubsidised out-of-warranty burden. BEV-SPECIFIC COSTS THAT REMAIN REAL: at 2,109 kg the car eats 20-inch tires, brake discs corrode from disuse under regen and get replaced on condition rather than wear, the 12V AGM battery still dies on schedule, and MEB's electric coolant pump, high-voltage heater and electric AC compressor (which also cools the pack) are known out-of-warranty risk items. NOTE: this trim rides on conventional steel springs — there is NO air suspension on the 45 advanced, so no air-strut replacement is included. Home-charger installation is excluded from maintenance by design (see assumptions.notes). SOURCING HONESTY: amounts are Audi Taiwan authorised-dealer pricing estimates built from published TW dealer labour rates and parts norms, not from a published Audi TW service-price table — audi.com.tw returned HTTP 503 again on this second pass (https://www.audi.com.tw/tw/web/zh/service-and-accessories.html) and Mobile01 blocks automated access, so no owner receipts or official price list could be obtained on either pass. Treat the absolute amounts as modelled, not quoted; every checkpoint stays 'low' for that reason.

assumptions.notes: Buyer drives 6,000-8,000 km/year, far below the Taiwan average of ~12,000-15,000 km/year. All checkpoints use the 7,000 km/year midpoint, so assumed_km = 7000 x years (7,000 / 21,000 / 35,000 / 49,000 / 70,000). Consequence 1: servicing is TIME-driven, not mileage-driven — the owner never reaches Audi's 10,000 km step inside a year, so visits are annual and the car takes about ten visits to cover 70,000 km. Consequence 2: mileage-triggered big-ticket items land LATE — the automatic transmission fluid + Sealing Plug service is tied to 60,000 km in Audi Taiwan's official service matrix, which at 7,000 km/year arrives around year 8.6, i.e. inside the 7-10 window rather than the 5-7 one. Consequence 3: tires age out rather than wear out, so they are replaced on rubber age (~5-6 years), not on tread depth. Consequence 4: used values are read off LOW-MILEAGE listings, which sell materially above the mileage-blind median — the MY2023 Q5 listing set shows a 76,000 km car asking 1,005,000 against a 14,000 km car asking 1,558,000, a spread driven by mileage alone. Vehicle licence tax (牌照稅), fuel tax (燃料費) and insurance are EXCLUDED by design and appear nowhere in this record. POWERTRAIN: this car carries Audi's 48V MHEV Plus mild-hybrid system (belt-driven starter-generator plus a small 48V lithium battery). It cannot move the car on electricity alone, so it is classified 'gasoline', not 'hybrid'. TRIM POSITION: the advanced 進化版 is the front-wheel-drive entry car — Audi Taiwan's first FWD Q5 — while quattro starts higher up the range. FWD is a resale negative in the Taiwan used German-SUV market and there is no historical FWD Q5 resale record to measure it against, so a judgement penalty of ~4-5% is applied at each checkpoint and flagged as judgement.

purchase.source: LIST PRICE CORRECTED BACK TO 2,400,000 — see notes. Chain of evidence: (1) the October 2025 LAUNCH table for the all-new Q5, fetched directly from 8891 新車頻道 (https://c.8891.com.tw/news/audi/q5/20805) and independently from 7Car (https://www.7car.tw/articles/read/113533), both printing 'Q5 TFSI 150 kW advanced 進化版 = 2,300,000', 'Q5 Sportback advanced = 2,410,000', 'Q5 TFSI quattro 150 kW S line 運動版 = 2,700,000', 'Q5 Sportback S line = 2,810,000', SQ5 3,829,000 / 3,939,000, SQ5 Edition One 3,415,000 / 3,525,000, launch 2025-10-02; (2) TVBS Auto, 2026-07-16 (https://news.tvbs.com.tw/cars/3259163), fetched directly, reporting Audi Taiwan's 2026 model-year adjustment verbatim: '包含A5、A5 Avant、A6 Sportback e-tron、A6 Avant e-tron、Q5、Q5 Sportback等多數車型均較舊年式調漲10萬元' and 'Q5及Q5 Sportback另新增TFSI quattro 150kW進化版車型，開價分別為257萬元、268萬元'. 2,300,000 + 100,000 = 2,400,000 for the model year on sale today. This is a DERIVED figure, honestly labelled: TVBS prints no per-trim table naming the entry FWD car's new number, and audi.com.tw returns HTTP 503 to every automated fetch. Coherence cross-check supports it — the MY2026 ladder 2,400,000 (FWD advanced) / 2,570,000 (new quattro advanced) / 2,800,000 (quattro S line) gives sensible 170,000 and 230,000 steps, whereas holding the entry car at 2,300,000 would leave an implausible 270,000 gap to the new quattro variant directly above it. Discount and on-road fees are my own estimates (see notes), not published figures.
purchase.notes: THE RESEARCHER'S 'CORRECTION' WAS ITSELF THE ERROR. The prior pass overrode the scout's NT$2,400,000 down to NT$2,300,000, asserting the scout had misread the Q5 SPORTBACK row. That reasoning fails twice. First, the Sportback advanced lists at 2,410,000, not 2,400,000, so it is not a clean match for the scout's figure. Second and decisively, 2,300,000 is the OCTOBER 2025 LAUNCH (MY2025) price, and Audi Taiwan raised Q5 and Q5 Sportback prices by 100,000 for the 2026 model year in July 2026 (TVBS, 2026-07-16). This record carries model_year 2026 and is dated 2026-08-12, so the price of the model year actually on sale is 2,400,000. The prior pass even flagged this exact risk in its own open questions ('I could not confirm whether Audi Taiwan has adjusted the Q5 price since the October 2025 launch') and then resolved it the wrong way. POWERTRAIN: 2.0 TFSI four-cylinder turbo, 150 kW / 204 hp, 34.6-34.7 kgm, with Audi's 48V MHEV Plus system fitted across the whole Q5 range. This is a MILD hybrid — a belt-driven starter-generator plus a small 48V lithium battery that assist, restart and coast, but CANNOT drive the car on electricity alone. It is therefore classified 'gasoline' for this table, not 'hybrid'. DRIVETRAIN: the advanced 進化版 is front-wheel drive, headlined by KingAutos as '同級唯一前驅'; quattro begins with the new TFSI quattro 150 kW 進化版 (2,570,000) and the S line 運動版. DISCOUNT (NT$80,000, 3.3%): reduced from the prior pass's NT$100,000 because that figure was set against the 2,300,000 launch car. The MY2026 price list landed only in July 2026, so the car on the floor today is a fresh model year with no run-out pressure behind it. Audi Taiwan's published campaigns lead with a 5-year factory warranty and a first-two-years NT$9,999/month finance scheme rather than headline cash off, and 8891 notes that cash buyers who forgo the finance subsidy can negotiate an unpublished '隱藏版現金折扣'. NT$80,000 is a conservative achievable cash-buyer figure on a fresh model year. ON-ROAD FEES (NT$60,000): 領牌規費 ~NT$3,500 (new registration and plates) + 代辦費 ~NT$11,000 + dealer accessory package ~NT$45,000 (window film, dashcam, mats and boot tray, paint coating). The accessory line scales with class and is the bulk of the number on a NT$2.4m SUV. These are estimates from typical Taiwan luxury-SUV purchase quotes; no verbatim published 菜單 for this trim could be retrieved. Vehicle licence tax, fuel tax and insurance are excluded by design. real_cost = 2,400,000 - 80,000 + 60,000 = 2,380,000.

value_checkpoints.source: CORRECTED UPWARD, and now built on genuine current-generation evidence the prior pass said did not exist. 8891 中古車 (https://auto.8891.com.tw/audi/q5, fetched directly this pass) carries two real B10 listings: MY2025 'TFSI quattro 150kW S line' @ 2,000 km = 2,280,000 and @ 2,360 km = 2,280,000, both 車商售價 (dealer RETAIL asking). Against that trim's 2,700,000 launch list that is 84.4% dealer-retail retention at roughly ten months. Those are near-delivery-mileage cars, so a genuine 1-year / 7,000 km example sits a step below — I take ~81% — and the FWD entry trim carries a further ~4% penalty for weaker used demand, giving DEALER RETAIL 1,870,000 (78% of the 2,400,000 list). ADJUSTMENT APPLIED (the dealer-retail trap): private sale = dealer retail -11% => 1,660,000; dealer trade-in = private -13% => 1,440,000. Cross-check: 1,660,000 is 69.7% of real_cost, i.e. a ~30% first-year loss, which is the German shape and sits at the steep end of the 20-30% Taiwan first-year band rather than the Toyota-like high-70s the prior pass's method would have implied for a fresh generation. Low-mileage basis: 7,000 km is far under the ~16,000 km median of comparable 1-2 year listings, which supports the upper half of the range.

CORRECTED UPWARD — the prior pass claimed a low-mileage read and then did not perform it. Predecessor-generation (B9) proxy, trim-matched. 8891 中古車 (fetched this pass) lists a MY2023 '40 TFSI quattro advanced' @ 6,100 km = 1,380,000, the same car carbook.tw (https://carbook.tw/cars/audi-q5/2023, n=23, fetched this pass) shows at 6,000 km = 1,380,000. The same page shows 76,000 km => 1,005,000, 45,000 km => 1,229,000, 36,000-37,000 km => 1,238,000-1,288,000, 30,000 km => 1,230,000 and 14,000 km => 1,558,000, with a blended median of 1,229,000 at 45,000 km — and 8891 shows the mid-mileage cars are mostly the lower 'Technik' trim, which is why the trim-matched 6,100 km advanced point is the right anchor. Our buyer sits at 21,000 km, about 15,000 km above that anchor; at the ~0.4% per 1,000 km slope implied by the same listing set that is about -6%, giving a B9 advanced at 3 years / 21,000 km of ~1,300,000, i.e. 57.8% of the B9 advanced's ~2,250,000 list. Applying that ratio to this car's 2,400,000 list and taking a further ~4% off for the FWD entry trim gives DEALER RETAIL 1,330,000 (55% of list). ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: private sale = dealer retail -11% => 1,190,000; dealer trade-in = private -13.5% => 1,030,000. Note on the correction: the prior pass wrote that it read retail 'off the low-mileage end rather than the median' and cited 14,000 km => 1,558,000, then stated a retail of 1,200,000 — which is BELOW the 1,229,000 median it was supposedly reading above. The stated method did not produce the stated number.

Predecessor-generation (B9) proxy, corrected for the same self-contradiction as year 3. carbook.tw (https://carbook.tw/cars/audi-q5, fetched this pass) gives MY2021 Q5 median dealer asking 958,000 at 67,000 km (n=13) and MY2022 1,093,000 at 72,000 km (n=22); 8891 corroborates with MY2021 45 TFSI quattro @ 48,000 km = 958,000, @ 61,600 km = 979,000, @ 62,700 km = 979,000 and @ 110,000 km = 875,000. The MY2021 sample is 45 TFSI quattro, whose list was ~2,590,000, so the median is 37.0% retention. Our buyer carries 35,000 km against that 67,000 km median; at the ~0.4% per 1,000 km slope measured on the MY2023 listing set that is a ~12% low-mileage uplift, lifting retention to ~41.4%. Applied to this car's 2,400,000 list and reduced ~4% for the FWD entry trim, DEALER RETAIL 950,000 (40% of list). ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: private sale = dealer retail -12% => 840,000; dealer trade-in = private -14% => 720,000. Cross-check: 840,000 is 35.3% of real_cost, i.e. cumulative five-year depreciation near 65%, consistent with Taiwan guidance putting luxury brands near 60% at five years and German marques steeper. The 5-year factory warranty expires right at this point and the used market prices that in. Correction note: the prior pass said it applied '~15% low-mileage uplift then ~5% FWD penalty' to the 958,000 median — arithmetic that yields ~1,046,000 — but then stated a retail of 920,000, below the raw median.

EXTRAPOLATED from the predecessor generation — the B10 is under a year old and has no genuine 7-year data. Method: take real B9 used prices at that age, express them as a retention ratio of that car's own original list, then apply the ratio to this car. carbook.tw MY2019 Q5 (7 years old in Aug 2026) median dealer asking 728,000 at 50,000 km (n=5); 8891 corroborates with a MY2019 45 TFSI quattro Active Plus @ 50,000 km = 768,000. Median mileage matches this buyer's 49,000 km almost exactly, so NO mileage adjustment is applied. Against that trim's ~2,590,000 original list the two points give 28.1% and 29.7% retention; I take ~28.9%. Applied to this car's 2,400,000 list and reduced ~5% for the FWD entry trim gives DEALER RETAIL 660,000 (27.5% of list). ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: private sale = dealer retail -12% => 580,000; dealer trade-in = private -16% => 485,000 (a wider trade-in spread than the 10-15% norm, because dealers price reconditioning risk harder on an out-of-warranty German SUV). The car is two years out of warranty here and the market discounts repair risk, so the tail keeps falling rather than flattening. Small sample (n=5) at the anchor year — hence low confidence.

EXTRAPOLATED across two generations — no B10 or even late-B9 data exists at this age. This is the weakest checkpoint in the record. carbook.tw MY2016 Q5 (10 years old in Aug 2026) median dealer asking 438,000 at 92,000 km (n=5), corroborated exactly by 8891's MY2016 40 TFSI quattro @ 92,100 km = 438,000; surrounding years: MY2017 median 525,000 at 120,000 km (n=19), MY2015 383,000 at 130,000 km (n=12). MY2016 is the outgoing B8, whose 2.0 TFSI quattro listed around 2,390,000, giving 18.3% retention at the sample's 92,000 km. This buyer's 70,000 km is 22,000 km under that, worth about a 9% uplift on the same slope, lifting retention to ~20.0% and giving 479,000 on this car's 2,400,000 list. I then take that back down twice: ~8% because the B10 carries materially more electronics than a B8 (48V MHEV Plus, its lithium battery, the belt starter-generator), which a 10-year-old market discounts as future repair liability rather than rewarding as content, and ~4% for the FWD entry trim. Net DEALER RETAIL 425,000 (~18% of list). ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: private sale = dealer retail -13% => 370,000; dealer trade-in = private -18% => 305,000 (dealers barely want a 10-year-old out-of-warranty Audi except as trade fodder). The curve does not flatten into the tail: 580,000 at year 7 to 370,000 at year 10 is a further 36% over three years, which is the correct out-of-warranty German shape.

maintenance.plan_notes: BASIS — VERIFIED THIS PASS. Audi Taiwan publishes an official transparent scheduled-maintenance price table at https://service-pricing.audi-service.com.tw/ and I pulled its underlying JSON endpoints directly (/api/v1.0/pricing, 175 rows; /api/v1.0/service-matrix). The prior pass's quoted figures were re-checked row by row against the live API and are EXACTLY correct: 2021 Audi Q5 45 TFSI quattro (Petrol) returns 10,000 km [11,000-12,000]; 20,000 km [19,000-20,000]; 30,000 km [13,400-14,400]; 40,000 km [19,000-20,000]; 50,000 km [11,000-12,000]; 60,000 km [39,100-40,100]; 70,000 km [11,000-12,000]; 80,000 km [19,000-20,000]; 90,000 km [13,400-14,400]; 100,000 km [19,000-20,000]; 110,000 km [11,000-12,000]; 120,000 km [56,700-57,700] — a midpoint sum of NT$248,600 of scheduled servicing alone across 120,000 km. The official service matrix was likewise verified verbatim for Petrol: 原廠引擎機油, 機油濾清器, 華司與油封 and 粉塵濾清器 at every 10,000 km step; 煞車油 and 火星塞 every second step (20,000 km); 空氣濾清器 every third (30,000 km); 自動變速箱油 and Sealing Plug at 60,000 and 120,000 km only; V 型皮帶/綜合皮帶 and 皮帶調整器 at 120,000 km only. CAVEAT ADDED THIS PASS: the table's Q5 rows stop at model year 2022 — there is NO row for the B10, so every figure below carries a judgement uplift of roughly 15-25% for the B10's added complexity (MHEV Plus 48V hardware, more electronics) and 2026+ dealer labour rates. That uplift is unsourced, which is why the year-1 and year-3 checkpoints are marked medium rather than high. Worth noting as an upper bound: the same API's 2022 Q5 45 TFSI quattro Premium Plus row runs roughly three times the 2021 row (10,000 km [34,000-35,000], 60,000 km [106,800-107,800]); I did not build on it because its scope is unclear, but it shows the downside risk is on the expensive side, not the cheap side. INTERVAL IS TIME-DRIVEN, NOT MILEAGE-DRIVEN: at 7,000 km/year the owner never reaches the 10,000 km step inside a year, so servicing is annual and the car takes about ten visits (1 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 3) to reach 70,000 km. Brake fluid therefore falls due on its 2-year time limit, spark plugs on their ~4-year limit, and the 60,000 km transmission-fluid service arrives around year 8.6 rather than year 6, landing in the 7-10 window. WARRANTY: 8891 (https://c.8891.com.tw/news/21771, fetched this pass) confirms the Q5 is sold with 5年原廠保固 alongside a first-two-years NT$9,999/month finance scheme, and that the 5年10萬公里免費保養 benefit applies ONLY to the e-tron range, not the Q5 — so the owner pays every service from year 1. Note that article is dated 2026-05-08 and its campaign window closed 2026-05-31, so treat the warranty term as the recurring structure of Audi Taiwan's campaigns rather than a live quote. Years 1-5 therefore carry scheduled servicing and wear items only; from year 5 the car is unsubsidised and the 5-7 and 7-10 periods carry the full out-of-warranty repair burden, which is where cost concentrates. CONSUMABLES are placed on age, not tread: tires roughly every 5-6 years (a set of four fitted ~NT$38,000-40,000 on 19-inch 235/55 R19), front brakes around year 6-7 and rears around year 9-10 (large discs, dealer prices), 12V AGM battery about every 5 years. LATER-PERIOD RISK ITEMS in years 7-10: the EA888's well-known water pump and thermostat housing, coil packs, the 48V lithium battery and belt-driven starter-generator, plus suspension bushings. TOTAL ~NT$547,000 over 10 years / 70,000 km (~NT$54,700 per year, ~NT$7.8 per km) — several times a comparable Japanese SUV over the same period, which is the correct shape for a German luxury SUV serviced at a main dealer.

assumptions.notes: Buyer drives 6,000-8,000 km/yr (~7,000 km/yr midpoint), roughly half the Taiwan average of 12,000-15,000 km/yr. Checkpoint mileage = 7,000 x years (7,000 / 21,000 / 35,000 / 49,000 / 70,000). Three consequences shape this record. (1) EVERYTHING IS TIME-DRIVEN, NOT MILEAGE-DRIVEN. Audi Taiwan's vehicle warranty is 5 years OR 100,000 km and the high-voltage battery warranty is 8 years OR 160,000 km (>=70% capacity retained) — both confirmed by direct fetch. At 7,000 km/yr this car reaches only 35,000 km at year 5 and 70,000 km at year 10, so it never gets near either km cap: both warranties expire on the CALENDAR, and every service, brake-fluid change, coolant change and tyre replacement is triggered by age rather than wear. (2) RESALE IS QUOTED AGAINST LOW-MILEAGE LISTINGS. The used comparables used below are deliberately the lowest-mileage Q6 e-tron examples on the market (9,000 km and 14,400 km), which sit above the mileage-blind 行情 average. (3) HOME CHARGER IS EXCLUDED. A wallbox plus installation in a Taiwanese apartment building runs roughly NT$40,000-100,000 once the 社區管委會 application, the dedicated meter and the cable run are paid for. It is a real one-off ownership cost but it is NOT maintenance, so it appears in neither purchase nor maintenance here. Electricity, 牌照稅/燃料費 (both NT$0 for a BEV in Taiwan anyway) and insurance are excluded by design.

The bare 'Q6 e-tron' line is the entry single-motor RWD SUV, so 2,760,000 is the correct MY2026 建議售價 for this trim. The prior researcher's concern that 276萬 might be a Sportback mix-up is correctly resolved: 276萬 WAS the MY2025 Sportback RWD price, and became the SUV RWD price only after the +11萬 MY2026 adjustment (which pays for 主動式車道維持機能 and an AR HUD). The MY2025 SUV RWD baseline of 265萬 is corroborated by the launch coverage (Taiwan launch 2025-03-28), and a pre-sale figure of 269萬 for the same car appears in contemporaneous coverage (Mobile01/TVBS/Yahoo pre-sale reports), consistent with the reported 4萬 cut at launch. CAUTION NOTED: the same Yahoo MY2026 table is internally garbled on the SQ6 line ('SQ6 e-tron：326 萬 (降價 9 萬元)', which cannot be reconciled with a 369萬 MY2025 SQ6). That noise does not touch the Q6 e-tron 後驅版 line, which is consistent across the +11萬 pattern applied to every other Q6 variant. discounts 150,000 remains an INFERENCE, not a fetched figure — see notes.
purchase.notes:
TRIM ID: Q6 e-tron 後驅版 — single rear motor, 252 hp, 83 kWh battery, 533 km WLTP, 20-inch alloys as standard, CCS2, 800V PPE platform shared with the Porsche Macan EV. NO AIR SUSPENSION on this trim — 氣壓懸吊 is exclusive to the SQ6 e-tron, so the entry RWD rides on conventional steel springs and dampers. That is a genuine long-run saving versus air-sprung German SUVs and is why no air-strut replacement appears in the year-7 or year-10 maintenance windows; conventional dampers are replaced on age at year 10 instead.

DISCOUNTS 150,000 (5.4%) — INFERRED, and still the weakest number in this record. No published Audi TW cash-discount figure for the Q6 e-tron could be fetched (audi.com.tw returns HTTP 503 to automated fetches, confirmed again on this pass). The inference rests on four observations: (a) Audi Taiwan structurally leads with FINANCING rather than cash — 48期0利率 and a 3年保證買回 — which is how German brands in TW protect list price; (b) Audi has already shown willingness to move on this exact car, cutting 4萬 off the 269萬 pre-sale price at launch; (c) the car is ~1.4 years into its Taiwan life, not a launch model, and Audi has just raised the price 11萬 while MY2025 stock is still being cleared, both of which create negotiating room; (d) luxury BEV demand in Taiwan is thin and BEVs discount harder than equivalent ICE. RETAINED UNCHANGED after cross-checking the rest of this comparison table, where 150,000 is exactly the peer-consistent figure: the BMW i4 eDrive40 at a near-identical 2,790,000 list carries 150,000 (5.4%), the BMW iX2 carries 120,000 on 2,430,000 (4.9%) and the Mercedes EQB250+ carries 120,000 on 2,220,000 (5.4%). Treat as a realistic negotiated cash-equivalent — 掛牌金, 配件抵用, or a charging-equipment credit — rather than a quoted figure.

ONROAD_FEES RAISED 45,000 -> 55,000. The prior figure was scaled off the ICE Audi Q5's 40,000 in this same table, which is internally coherent but lands below every comparable German BEV SUV in the comparison set: Mercedes EQE300 SUV uses 72,000, BMW iX3 uses 85,000, BMW iX2 uses 65,000, Mercedes EQB250+ uses 60,000. 55,000 = 領牌 + 代辦 (~12,000: 新領牌照登記規費、驗車、車籍代辦; note a BEV pays no 貨物稅, and that is already inside the list price) + 配件 (~43,000: 高階隔熱紙 across a large glazed area, 行車記錄器, 腳踏墊, 車身鍍膜, 20吋輪圈防刮). This is a calibration adjustment against peers rather than a sourced correction, and is deliberately kept at the conservative end of the peer band. EXCLUDES the home wallbox and its installation (see assumptions.notes) and, by design, excludes tax and insurance.

real_cost = 2,760,000 - 150,000 + 55,000 = 2,665,000.
