value_checkpoints.source: 改用實際掛牌（原記錄此點無任何來源卻標 medium）。8891 實抓現行 W214 車源：2025 E200 12,900 km 車商開價 2,380,000、2025 E200 14,000 km 開價 2,268,000，均值約 2,324,000。該等 2025 年式 E 200 新車價約 2,930,000（Luxury），real cost 約 2,895,000。車商零售 2,324,000 →【自售調整】扣約 11% 得自售 2,068,000，殘值率 71.4%。將 71.4% 套回本車 real_cost 2,975,000 得 2,124,000，再給 7,000 km 對 13,000 km 的低里程加成約 2%（8891 資料顯示近新車里程溢價本就有限），取 2,160,000。dealer_tradein = 自售再扣約 13% = 1,880,000。第 1 年帳面損失約 27%，符合德系豪華房車在台灣的前段陡降，且車商零售價未被直接抄進自售價。

【修正原記錄的事實錯誤】原記錄稱「台灣尚無真正 3 年車齡的 W214」而改用 W213 跨代外推；W214 於 2024 年中在台上市，8891 上實際存在 2 年車齡車源，本點因此改以現行世代真實掛牌為錨。實抓：2024 E200 Luxury 20,000 km 車商開價 2,120,000（2 年車齡）。該車新車價 2,930,000、real cost 約 2,895,000；車商零售 2,120,000 →扣約 11% 得自售 1,887,000，2 年殘值率 65.2%。由 1 年 71.4%、2 年 65.2%、5 年 48.1% 的實測序列內插，3 年殘值率取約 59%，套回 real_cost 2,975,000 得 1,755,000，取 1,760,000（21,000 km 與參考車 20,000 km 相當，不另給里程加成）。dealer_tradein = 自售再扣約 13.5% = 1,520,000。此時仍在 3 年不限里程原廠保固內，對價格有支撐。

以前代 W213 小改款實際掛牌換算殘值率再套用（本車 2031 年才滿 5 年）。實抓錨點：2021 E200 Avantgarde 60,000 km 車商開價 1,368,000。該 2021 年式 W213 小改 E 200 新車價約 2,690,000、real cost 約 2,655,000。本車 5 年時僅 35,000 km，較參考車低甚多，給約 5% 低里程加成得車商零售約 1,436,000 →扣約 11% 得自售 1,278,000，殘值率 48.1%。套回 real_cost 2,975,000 得 1,431,000；因此點僅有單一筆 2021 年掛牌支撐，且該車屬小改款外觀有溢價，保守下修取 1,400,000。dealer_tradein = 自售再扣約 14% = 1,205,000。這是第一個脫離 3 年原廠保固的檢查點，台灣中古市場自此開始把維修風險計入價格，曲線不會像 Lexus 那樣打平。

【本次最大幅修正，原記錄高估約 14%】原記錄宣稱 2019 年式 W213 E 200 的車商開價約 1,150,000-1,300,000，與實際市場不符。8891 實抓 2019 E200 共 4 筆：11,780 km／889,000、56,100 km／949,000、117,000 km／889,000，另 2018 E200 50,000 km／850,000，實際區間是 850,000-949,000，不是 115 萬-130 萬。取低里程車商零售 900,000。2019 年式 W213 E 200 新車價約 2,620,000、real cost 約 2,585,000；車商零售 900,000 →扣約 11% 得自售 801,000，殘值率 31.0%。套回本車 real_cost 2,975,000 得 922,000，加約 3% 低里程加成取 950,000。dealer_tradein = 自售再扣約 14.5% = 810,000（保固外德系車商需承擔整備風險，收購折讓隨車齡放大）。注意：同一批資料中 11,780 km 與 117,000 km 的 2019 E200 開價同為 889,000，證實中高齡德系房車的里程溢價極小，原記錄逐年放大到 10% 的低里程加成不成立。

以前代 W213 首批年份（2016，W213 在台上市年）實際掛牌換算。8891 實抓 2016 E200：81,000 km／738,000、110,000 km／668,000、120,000 km／498,000；另 2017 E200 11,700 km／759,000、80,000 km／768,000；2015（前代 W212）則掉到 518,000-598,000、2014 為 478,000-498,000、2013 為 258,000 —— 世代斷點造成的落差遠大於里程。本車 2036 年滿 10 年時屬世代中期車（W214 於 2024 上市，2026 年式為小改前），比今日 2016 首批 W213 更靠近世代尾端，故取車商零售 700,000（介於 2016 低里程 738,000 與 2015 世代斷點之間）。2016 年式 W213 E 200 新車價約 2,530,000、real cost 約 2,495,000；車商零售 700,000 →扣約 11% 得自售 623,000，殘值率 25.0%。套回 real_cost 2,975,000 得 743,000，加約 4% 低里程加成取 770,000。dealer_tradein = 自售再扣約 15.5% = 650,000。尾段續跌未打平：保固外德系豪華房車買家池薄，48V 鋰電池／ISG、電子水泵、變速箱機電、電子系統的大額風險都被計入價格。

maintenance.plan_notes: 台灣賓士原廠（授權經銷）保養，ASSYST PLUS 之 Service A／Service B 交替。【重要修正一：取消原記錄的免費保養假設】原記錄假設台灣賓士隨車附贈 3 年預付保養套餐（星徽保養套餐），把 0-1 年與 1-3 年壓到 3,000 與 12,000。此假設無根據且是本記錄最大的模型錯誤：台灣賓士新車標配的是 3 年不限里程原廠「保固」，定期保養並不免費；星徽保養套餐是「付費預付」方案（先付費換取折扣），不是隨車贈品。實際促銷內容亦可佐證——KingAutos 2026-03 購車優惠對 E-Class 給的是「160萬 40期 0利率 + 1年延長保固」，給的是延長保固而非免費保養。故 0-3 年改採全額自付。官網保固頁本次逾時無法讀取，無法正面證實或證偽，因此採不含免費保養的保守假設並在此明說。【重要修正二：保養週期】原記錄寫「每 12 個月一次」；依 2ggx 保養費資料，Service A 為 1.5 年或 15,000 km、Service B 為 2 年或 30,000 km。本車 7,000 km/年要約 2.1 年才跑到 15,000 km，所以確實是時間先觸發（原記錄結論正確），但實際週期是每 12-18 個月而非每 12 個月，10 年約 7-8 次進廠而非 10 次。輪胎（5-6 年老化）與煞車油（2 年）同為日曆項目而非磨耗項目。單價採 2ggx 的 E-Class 級距區間中位：Service A 約 12,000（區間 10,000-15,000）、Service B 約 24,000（區間 18,000-30,000）。台灣原廠工資約 NT$2,500-3,000/小時，明顯高於日系經銷商，且 E-Class 的大尺寸煞車與 19 吋輪圈 245 級距輪胎相應昂貴。本車為鋼簧 AGILITY CONTROL，未配 AIRMATIC，故不提列氣壓避震器更換（若為氣壓懸吊，7-10 年窗口需另加約 120,000-180,000）。48V ISG 啟動發電機與其鋰電池以期望值方式提列於 7-10 年窗口。【修正三】7-10 年由原記錄的 340,000 下修至 300,000：原記錄在 5-7 年已提列 30,000 冷卻／點火風險，7-10 年又提 45,000「第二輪」冷卻點火，且在僅 70,000 km 下提列 50,000 的完整避震器更換，屬重複與過度提列；本記錄改為冷卻點火第二輪 40,000、懸吊以引擎腳與連桿襯套為主 35,000。10 年合計約 633,000（70,000 km），約為同級日系房車的 2.5-3 倍，且較同批 GLC 200（480,000）高約 32%，符合更大車體、更大煞車輪胎與更完整保固外風險提列的預期。

major_items: Service A 一次（機油、機油濾芯、原廠檢查、數位保養紀錄）約 12,000 —— 全額自付，已取消原記錄的免費套餐假設

assumptions.notes: Buyer drives 6,000-8,000 km/year; every checkpoint uses the 7,000 km/year midpoint (7,000 / 21,000 / 35,000 / 49,000 / 70,000 km). That is roughly half the Taiwan average of 12,000-15,000 km/year, so servicing is TIME-driven (annual/biennial calendar intervals), not mileage-driven, and consumables age out rather than wear out - tires are replaced on age (~every 5-6 years) long before tread depth is reached. On low-mileage pricing: the intent is to quote low-mileage comparables, but the actual 8891 EQA data does NOT show a clean low-mileage premium (the 14,000 km car is the cheapest in the set at 122.0萬 while the 63,700 km car asks 130.0萬), so the used market for this nameplate is too thin for mileage to drive price. Values below are therefore anchored on the upper part of the observed asking range rather than on a computed mileage premium, and this is stated in each source string. EXCLUDED BY DESIGN: tax and insurance (Taiwan currently exempts BEVs from 牌照稅 and 燃料費 - Yahoo Autos shows both as $0 for this car - but they are out of scope either way). ALSO EXCLUDED: home-charger installation. A dedicated 220V circuit / wallbox in Taiwan runs roughly NT$30,000-80,000 depending on distance to the panel, and in an apartment it additionally requires 管委會 approval which may block it entirely; it is a one-off capital installation, not maintenance, so it is deliberately left out of maintenance.checkpoints. Public DC fast charging is likewise not modelled (energy cost, not maintenance).

purchase.source: List price NT$2,170,000 (217萬) independently re-verified by this fact-check by fetching the pages directly. U-CAR 26MY road test states verbatim '配備/電氣性能/電池容量升級，新年式 EQA 250+售價 217 萬' and its own model box shows '1 車型 217 萬'; ETtoday states verbatim '目前台灣EQA售價217萬'. Both read 2026-08-12. The brand's own models.html genuinely does not respond from this environment (curl returns status 000 / timeout), which I re-tested and confirmed, so it is retained in sources[] with an explicit caveat rather than cited as read. CORRECTION TO THE PRIOR RECORD: it claimed Yahoo Autos as a third price verification showing '217 (萬)'. I fetched that page and it carries NO price at all - only 牌照稅 $0 and 燃料稅 $0. That claim was removed; the Yahoo source is kept for the tax-status fact only. Price verification therefore rests on two sources I confirmed verbatim, not three. Discount and on-road fees are estimates, not a published table.
purchase.notes: NOT a hybrid and not a 48V mild hybrid - this is a full BEV, and the '250+' suffix denotes the enlarged battery (usable capacity raised from 66.5 kWh to 70.5 kWh), NOT any hybrid assist system. WLTP range rises from 426 km to 561 km (NEDC 606 km per the Bureau of Energy filing). Single trim in Taiwan; the 250+ replaced the EQA 250 for the 2026 model year at an unchanged 217萬. DISCOUNT (NT$200,000, 9.2% off list) - deliberately larger than the 3-8% a German brand normally concedes in Taiwan, and the justification is now independently verified rather than asserted: I fetched the ETtoday article of 2026-07-30 and it says verbatim that the all-new MMA-platform GLA '象徵GLA與EQA產品線正式整合' - the EQA nameplate is being merged out of existence. The successor GLA 250+ carries an 85 kWh pack, 800V architecture, 320 kW DC charging and 657 km WLTP from EUR 48,599.60 (~NT$1.8m), and the same article confirms Taiwanese dealers were already privately taking orders ('台灣經銷端早已私下排隊接單') for a 2027 arrival, headlined '新台幣200萬有找'. This car is therefore a run-out model of a dying nameplate whose replacement is better and cheaper. That is exactly when Taiwanese Mercedes dealers discount hardest, so a NT$150,000-250,000 package (cash off plus 領牌 absorbed plus accessories) is realistic and I kept the midpoint. For contrast, the same-price current GLA 200 (216萬) is modelled at only a NT$70,000 discount in this batch - correctly, because it is the fresh model, not the run-out one. ON-ROAD FEES CORRECTED from NT$80,000 to NT$55,000: the prior figure was 78% above the same-price sibling (GLA 200 at 216萬 uses NT$45,000 for the identical 領牌+代辦+配件 definition) and was built from a premium-end accessory list (隔熱紙 30,000 + 鍍膜 20,000). NT$55,000 = 領牌/新領牌照登記 and 代辦 (~NT$10,000) + 隔熱紙 (~NT$20,000) + 鍍膜 (~NT$12,000) + 行車記錄器 (~NT$8,000) + 腳踏墊/行李廂墊 (~NT$5,000), keeping a small premium over the GLA 200 because EV buyers at this price do fit more accessories. Tax and insurance are excluded by design and are NOT in real_cost. real_cost = 2,170,000 - 200,000 + 55,000 = 2,025,000.

selling_costs.notes: Top of the 6,000-15,000 band for this class, which is appropriate here. Detailing is the dominant line because a 217萬-class German car will not achieve a private-sale price without proper paint correction and interior work - a scruffy example gets pushed toward the 車商收購 price instead. Assumes the owner sells privately (自售), which is what private_sale_price in value_checkpoints represents; a dealer trade-in would incur none of these costs but realises the materially lower dealer_tradein_price. Checked and left unchanged by the fact-check.

value_checkpoints.source: Interpolated between the NT$2,170,000 new price and the well-observed ~3.4-year point below; no 1-year-old EQA 250+ exists on the market yet (the 250+ only went on sale mid-2025, and all 10 used EQAs listed nationwide on 8891 are 2022-2023 cars - I re-scraped the page and confirmed the count and every listing). Method: implied 1-year dealer RETAIL asking ~NT$1,580,000, then -11% to private sale (NT$1,400,000), then a further -13% to dealer trade-in (NT$1,220,000). ADJUSTMENT STATED: 8891 figures are 車商售價 (dealer retail asking), never what an owner receives, so nothing here is copied from an asking price. The year-1 loss is deliberately steep (69% of real cost retained) because the replacement generation was revealed 2026-07-30 and lands in Taiwan during this very window - a German BEV holding Japanese-like year-1 value would be wrong. Fact-check cross-validation: this sits between the Volvo EC40 (64% of list at year 1) and Volvo EX40 (72%) modelled in the same batch, and below the combustion Mercedes GLA 200 sibling (67% of list, but on a far flatter subsequent curve), which is the correct relative position for a discontinued German BEV.

Anchored on real 8891 中古車 listings for the predecessor EQA 250 (original list 215萬), now ~3.4 years old. I independently re-scraped the page on 2026-08-12 and verified every data point: SIX distinct cars - five 2023 cars at 140.0萬/10,200 km, 135.0萬/37,000 km, 130.0萬/63,700 km, 125.0萬/40,000 km, 122.0萬/14,000 km, plus one 2022 car at 99.6萬/95,000 km (a seventh is 電洽, no price). CORRECTION TO THE PRIOR RECORD's REASONING: it claimed the low-mileage end commands a premium, but its own data refutes that - the 14,000 km car is the CHEAPEST at 122.0萬 and the 63,700 km car asks MORE (130.0萬) than the 40,000 km car (125.0萬). In a market this thin, mileage barely prices. I therefore anchor on the upper part of the observed asking range (~NT$1,350,000-1,400,000 dealer retail) on condition/spec grounds rather than on a mileage premium. Adjustments stated explicitly: (a) shaded to ~NT$1,250,000 dealer retail because the EQA nameplate is confirmed discontinued - the 2023 cars listed today have not yet priced in the 2026-07-30 merger announcement; (b) dealer retail -11% to private sale = NT$1,110,000; (c) private -13% to dealer trade-in = NT$965,000. Implies 51% of list retained at 3 years versus the ~62% dealer-ASKING retention visible today - the gap IS the retail-to-private spread plus the nameplate-death discount. Corroborating anchor I found that the prior record missed: a 2023 GLA 200 (combustion, near-identical original price) asks 165.8萬 at 28,000 km on the same site, i.e. the petrol GLA holds ~18% more than the electric EQA at the same age. That spread is the BEV penalty, observed directly within the same nameplate family.

EXTRAPOLATED - no 5-year data exists for this generation. NOTE: the prior record had years=35000 here (the km value had been copied into the years field), which broke the checkpoint sequence; corrected to 5. Two real anchors, both re-verified by direct scrape on 2026-08-12: (1) the oldest EQA on 8891, a 2022 car at ~4.4 years with 95,000 km, asking 99.6萬; adjusting UP for our car's far lower 35,000 km gives roughly 115萬 at 4.4 years, extrapolated to ~105萬 dealer retail at 5 years. (2) The nearest real Mercedes BEV tail available: 2020 EQC 400 4Matic 運動版 at 6 years asking 108.0萬 (30,000 km) and 108.0萬 (36,000 km), with a 129,000 km car at 99.0萬 - only three EQCs listed nationwide, on a car that listed around 300萬 when new. Shaded to ~NT$920,000 dealer retail for the dead nameplate and the 800V successor generation, then -11% to private (NT$820,000) and -15% to trade-in (NT$700,000). Confidence stays low: I could NOT source the EQC's exact original Taiwan list price, so the ~300萬 figure is a sanity reference only and was never used as a computed input.

EXTRAPOLATED from the PREDECESSOR-GENERATION method - no 7-year EQA can exist (Taiwan launch was 2022). Real anchors on 8891, all re-verified by direct scrape 2026-08-12: 2020 EQC at 6 years asking 108.0萬 (30,000 km); Mercedes GLA W156 at 9 years (2017, 89,000 km) asking 58.5萬. The EQA is a GLA-bodied car and today's GLA 200 (216萬, confirmed on Yahoo Autos) is a direct price peer of this EQA (217萬), so the GLA tail is the right shape to borrow, then penalised for BEV-specific risk. Critically, the high-voltage battery warranty expires at 8 years - this is genuinely sourced, not assumed: an actual 8891 listing for a 2022 EQA advertises '高壓電池保固至2030年11' (2022/11 + 8 years), and I confirmed that exact string in the page text. A 7-year car is therefore being valued right at the edge of that cliff and the market discounts it hard. Implied ~NT$620,000 dealer retail (29% of list), -12% to private (NT$550,000), -15% to trade-in (NT$465,000). The tail keeps falling rather than flattening - correct for an out-of-warranty German BEV, unlike a Lexus.

EXTRAPOLATED via predecessor generation, expressed as a retention ratio and applied to this car. Real anchors, all four individually re-verified in the scraped page text on 2026-08-12: Mercedes GLA W156 at 10 years (2016 cars) asking 53.8萬/54,100 km, 51.8萬/80,000 km, 48.0萬/94,000 km, and at 9 years 58.5萬/89,000 km (2017) - i.e. roughly 22-25% of the CURRENT same-nameplate GLA 200 list (216萬), or roughly 30-33% of its own-era list price. I could not source the 2016 GLA's original list price, which remains the main weakness and the reason for low confidence; the ratio is normalised against the current GLA 200 price instead. A 10-year BEV must sit BELOW the combustion equivalent: the HV battery warranty has been expired for two years, a pack replacement is a six-figure TWD event, and Taiwan's used market prices battery uncertainty punitively on thin-demand German EVs. I therefore took ~17% of list = ~NT$360,000 dealer retail, -11% to private (NT$320,000), -16% to trade-in (NT$270,000). Fact-check cross-validation: 16% of real cost at year 10 matches the Volvo EC40 (16%) and Volvo EX90 (17%) BEVs modelled in this batch and sits well below the combustion Mercedes GLA 200 sibling (23%), which is the correct ordering. Being explicitly extrapolated, not silently invented.

maintenance.plan_notes: ALL five maintenance figures are constructed estimates from Taiwan Mercedes dealer labour rates (~NT$2,500-3,500/hour) and typical EQ parts pricing. No published Taiwan Mercedes EQ service price table and no Mobile01 owner thread with actual receipts could be obtained: mercedes-benz.com.tw does not respond from this environment (re-tested, curl status 000) and Mobile01 returns HTTP 403 to automated fetching. Every checkpoint is therefore low confidence - treat them as a reasoned model, not sourced figures. MATERIAL CORRECTION BY THE FACT-CHECK: the prior record's ten-year total was NT$520,000, which is 96% of the combustion Mercedes GLA 200's NT$540,000 in this same batch and 2.1-2.4x every peer European BEV (Volvo EC40 NT$251,500, Volvo EX40 NT$216,000, Volvo EX90 NT$337,000). Its own year-3 period cost (NT$32,000) was identical to the petrol GLA 200's despite the EQA having no oil service at all. That directly contradicted its own narrative that a BEV is 'genuinely much cheaper' than a petrol Mercedes. The curve has been rebuilt to a ten-year total of NT$358,000, which preserves the correct ordering: comfortably above Japanese BEVs (Toyota bZ4X NT$200,000, Urban Cruiser NT$188,000), above the Volvo BEVs because Mercedes dealer labour and dealer-only EQ parts genuinely cost more, and clearly below the combustion Mercedes GLA 200 (NT$540,000) as the physics requires. Costs below are per-period (cost SINCE the previous checkpoint), not cumulative. INTERVAL: at 7,000 km/year this car will never reach a mileage trigger - Mercedes EQ service here is time-driven, an annual inspection visit with the substantive service every second year. WARRANTY: the high-voltage battery is covered 8 years, which IS sourced - an 8891 listing for a 2022 EQA advertises '高壓電池保固至2030年11', a string I confirmed directly in the page text. The general vehicle warranty period I could not verify; I have assumed 3 years, which is why years 1 and 3 are light and years 5 onward carry the full unsubsidised cost. Taiwan Mercedes dealers do sell prepaid 保養套餐 packages that subsidise the early periods; if one is bought, years 1-3 fall further but the later periods are unaffected. BEV vs COMBUSTION: genuinely much cheaper than a Mercedes petrol SUV - no oil services, no spark plugs, no coil packs, no DPF, no 48V starter-generator (none of those exist on this car) - and regenerative braking makes pads last far beyond this mileage. But never near zero: 19-inch premium tires age out on a 5-6 year calendar regardless of mileage, brake fluid and battery/drive-unit coolant still need changing, and the 12V AGM battery still dies. The specifically BEV failure mode in humid Taiwan at 7,000 km/year is brake DISC corrosion from disuse rather than pad wear. The genuine out-of-warranty risk items on an EQA are thermal management (multiple electric coolant pumps), the on-board charger / DC-DC converter, the electric A/C compressor, and the HV contactor - all dealer-only, all expensive, all concentrated in the 7-10 year window; these are now probability-weighted rather than each assumed to occur with certainty, which was the main source of the prior over-count. A full HV pack replacement (well over NT$500,000) is NOT included as an expected cost, but after year 8 that risk sits entirely with the owner.

assumptions.notes: Buyer drives 6,000-8,000 km/year, well below the Taiwan average of ~12,000-15,000 km/year. All checkpoints use assumed_km = 7000 * years (7,000 / 21,000 / 35,000 / 49,000 / 70,000). At this mileage the EQB never reaches its 25,000 km service trigger, so servicing is purely time-driven (annual) and the used values quoted are read off LOW-MILEAGE listings rather than the mileage-blind market average. IMPORTANT CAVEAT ADDED ON REVIEW: the live 8891 EQA 250 cluster shows only a weak mileage gradient (2023 cars ask 122-140萬 across 10,200-63,700 km), so the low-mileage premium is real but much smaller than a naive reading suggests; it is applied conservatively here rather than being used to offset a full year of age. EXCLUDED BY DESIGN: (1) home charger installation - a 7.4 kW wallbox plus Taipower meter/wiring typically runs NT$40,000-80,000 for a house and can exceed NT$100,000 in an apartment complex needing a 社區 electrical review; it is a real ownership cost but it is not maintenance, so it is left out of maintenance.checkpoints entirely; (2) all tax and insurance, per the table spec - Taiwan does currently exempt BEVs from 牌照稅/燃料稅, but the statutory end-date has been extended repeatedly and could not be verified to any specific year from a primary source in this pass, so no claim about its expiry is made here (it is excluded from the model either way); (3) electricity/charging cost. The official list price already has the EV 貨物稅 (commodity tax) reduction baked in, per Mercedes-Benz Taiwan's own footnote, so no further tax rebate should be applied on top.

(2) The 8891 新車 per-trim specification table - which is the decisive per-trim evidence the original record lacked - lists exactly two on-sale trims: 'EQB 2026年式 250+ ... 222萬' and 'EQB 2026年式 300 4MATIC ... 267萬' (https://c.8891.com.tw/mercedes-benz/eqb/Specification.html). purchase.notes: PRICE BASIS: NT$2,220,000 is the official 建議售價 for the 2026年式 EQB 250+ and already reflects the government EV 貨物稅減徵; Mercedes-Benz Taiwan's footnote warns that because EQA/EQB already take the EV commodity-tax cut, the additional NT$50,000 small-car commodity-tax rebate may not be fully available on top. A cash buyer forgoes the 0% finance and instead negotiates cash off plus an accessory package. The EQB 250+ is a slow-selling German BEV in Taiwan - 8891 ranks it only 41st in its 小型SUV休旅 segment, and it competes against BMW iX1, Volvo EX40 and much cheaper Tesla/Chinese product - so dealer flexibility is real. NT$120,000 is realistic, not aggressive, and sits in the same band as this batch's other Mercedes entries (GLA 200 3.2%, EQE 300 SUV 6.7%). NOTE THE TRADE-OFF, which now also feeds maintenance: taking the cash discount plausibly forfeits the conditional 贈2年延保, so the years 3-5 maintenance period no longer assumes free extended-warranty cover. ON-ROAD FEES (NT$60,000): 領牌 + 代辦 ~NT$15,000, plus 配件 ~NT$45,000 (mats, window film, dashcam, paint coating/protection), scaled to a NT$2.22M car. Tax and insurance are excluded by design and are NOT in this number. real_cost = 2,220,000 - 120,000 + 60,000 = 2,160,000. POWERTRAIN: full BEV - single 190 hp (140 kW) permanent-magnet front motor, 70.5 kWh, 100 kW DC, front-wheel drive, per the 8891 spec table. value_checkpoints.source: REVISED DOWN on review (was 1,500,000 private / 1,290,000 trade-in). EXTRAPOLATED - no 1-year-old EQB 250+ exists on the Taiwan market. The original record justified this point by claiming the Mercedes-Benz Select certified EQE/EQS SUVs sit at 'around 65% of their original list'; I re-read that inventory and that claim is WRONG - EQE 300 SUV 出廠 2024/04, 4,755 km asks 233.8萬 and EQS 450 4MATIC SUV 出廠 2024/03, 3,114 km asks 426萬, which against their current lists is roughly 72-78%, not 65%. Those points are also contaminated by EQ-line price cuts, so I discarded them as the anchor and rebuilt this checkpoint from same-brand, same-channel listings instead. METHOD: (a) closest combustion analogue by size and price, GLA 200 (list 216萬 vs EQB 222萬), certified 出廠 2024/12 with 4,728 km asks 178萬 = 82.4% of list at 1.7 years, implying ~86-87% certified at 1.0 year; (b) the measured BEV penalty at matched age from the same certified inventory - EQA 250 出廠 2023/08 (3.0 y) asks 149.8萬 = 69% of its 217萬 list, versus GLC 300 4M Coupé 出廠 2023/09 (2.9 y) at 265.8萬 ≈ 80% - i.e. ~11 points, and German BEV loss is front-loaded so most of that penalty is already present at year 1; (c) certified-to-ordinary-retail step measured directly, EQA 250 certified 149.8萬 at 11,261 km vs ordinary 8891 EQA 250 140.0萬 at 10,200 km = ordinary retail is ~6.5% below certified. Chain: 87% - 9 points = ~78% certified = ~172萬; x0.935 = ~161萬 ordinary dealer retail asking. ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: private sale set ~11% below that dealer asking = 144萬, per the 車商售價 > 自售價 > 車商收購價 chain; dealer trade-in a further ~14% below private = 124萬. Low-mileage premium included but held small, per assumptions.notes. This is a ~33% first-year loss against real_cost - the steep German-BEV year-one hit, and it now sits with the EQE siblings in this batch rather than above them.

REVISED DOWN on review (was 1,270,000 private / 1,090,000 trade-in) and CONFIDENCE DOWNGRADED from high to medium. The underlying listings were re-fetched and are all genuine, but the original record read the dealer-asking level off the TOP of the cluster. Live 8891 中古車 EQA 250 asking prices, re-read 2026-08-12 (https://auto.8891.com.tw/usedauto-index.html?keyword=EQA), 2023 cars i.e. exactly 3 years old: 140.0萬 / 10,200 km (x2), 135.0萬 / 37,000 km, 130.0萬 / 63,700 km (x2, certified), 125.0萬 / 40,000 km (x2), 122.0萬 / 14,000 km - cluster mean ~131萬, and ~135-136萬 at our 21,000 km. The EQA 250 is the right analogue: single motor, 190 hp, list 217萬 against the EQB 250+'s 222萬. Adding ~2% for the EQB's higher list and 7-seat body gives ordinary dealer retail asking ~138萬, not the 145萬 originally used. Cross-check, same age: EQB 300 4MATIC 2023 / 16,000 km asks 158.0萬 and 2023 / 31,500 km asks 155.0萬 against a 267萬 list = ~59% - if anything that pulls the 250+ lower still. ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: private sale set ~12% below the 138萬 dealer asking = 121萬; dealer trade-in a further ~14% below = 104萬. CONFIDENCE: medium, not high. There are ZERO used EQB 250+ listings in Taiwan - all eleven live EQB listings are the dual-motor EQB 300 4MATIC, because the 250+ only arrived in Feb 2024 - so this number is read off a DIFFERENT model and is a proxy, however well-populated that proxy is. 'High' overstated it.

REVISED DOWN on review (was 990,000 private / 850,000 trade-in). Anchored on real 4-year-old EQ listings re-verified 2026-08-12: EQA 250, 2022, 95,000 km asking 99.6萬 (46% of its 217萬 list); EQB 300 4MATIC, 2022, 76,300 km asking 113.8萬 (x2) and 2022, 130,000-134,500 km asking 106.8萬 / 106.9萬 (43% of a 267萬 list). Every real 2022 BEV listing is high-mileage, so a low-mileage adjustment is needed - but the original record over-credited it. The live EQA cluster shows only a weak mileage gradient at constant age (122-140萬 spanning 10,200-63,700 km), so low mileage does NOT offset a full extra year of age as originally assumed. Rebuilt: a 4-year EQ BEV at ~35,000 km asks ~110-115萬; one further year of age takes it to ~104萬 ordinary dealer retail asking at 5 years, versus the ~113萬 originally used. Combustion cross-check from the certified inventory: GLA 180 出廠 2021/05 (5.3 y), 82,698 km at 122.8萬 - the combustion sibling holds visibly better, which is the BEV penalty this record applies throughout. ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: private sale ~12% below dealer asking = 92萬; dealer trade-in a further ~14% below = 79萬. That is ~41% of list at 5 years. Note the factory warranty is 3 years and the 2-year 延保 is conditional (see maintenance.plan_notes), so this window is at or past the end of warranty cover, which is consistent with the fall steepening here.

UNCHANGED on review - the underlying data was re-fetched and is genuine. EXTRAPOLATED FROM PREDECESSOR-GENERATION DATA: the current EQB only reached Taiwan in 2022 and the 250+ trim in Feb 2024, so no genuine 7-year data exists for this car and none has been invented. Method as required by the brief: take the real Taiwan used prices of the oldest German BEV actually sold here, the BMW i3 REx (on sale in Taiwan from ~2014, original list ~239萬), express them as a retention ratio of ITS original list, then apply that ratio to this car. Live 8891 中古車 i3 asking prices re-read 2026-08-12 (https://auto.8891.com.tw/usedauto-index.html?keyword=i3), all four listings on the site: 2017 REx, 140,000 km at 52.0萬; 2016 REx, 83,000 km at 59.8萬; 2016 REx, 90,000 km at 45.8萬; 2015 REx, 110,000 km at 45.8萬 - i.e. ~19-25% DEALER ASKING retention at 9-11 years. Interpolating that curve back to 7 years gives ~32-33% dealer asking, nudged up slightly for our car's much lower mileage (49,000 km vs the i3s' 83,000-140,000 km): dealer retail asking ~72萬. ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: private sale ~11% below = 64萬; dealer trade-in a further ~16% below = 54萬. Confidence stays low: this is a cross-model, cross-brand extrapolation, and the i3 is an unusual car (carbon tub, small battery, range-extender) whose collapse may overstate the EQB's. Caveat recorded rather than smoothed away.

UNCHANGED on review - underlying data re-fetched and genuine. EXTRAPOLATED FROM PREDECESSOR-GENERATION DATA, same method and same caveat as year 7; no 10-year EQB exists. Here the BMW i3 REx data sits at exactly the target age, which is the strongest available evidence for a decade-old German BEV in Taiwan: 2016 REx, 90,000 km asking 45.8萬 and 2015 REx, 110,000 km asking 45.8萬, against a ~239萬 original list = ~19% DEALER ASKING retention at 10-11 years. Our car will have only 70,000 km, meaningfully below those, so the ratio is lifted to ~22% dealer asking = ~49萬 dealer retail. ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: private sale ~14% below dealer asking = 42萬; dealer trade-in a further ~17% below = 35萬 - the private-vs-trade-in gap widens on old BEVs because dealers discount hard for battery uncertainty they cannot warrant. Key driver: the high-voltage battery warranty is 8年/16萬km (now verified from the official spec table, see sources), so it has expired by year 8, and a pack replacement at NT$600,000-900,000+ exceeds the entire value of the car - the market prices in that cliff, which is why the tail keeps falling instead of flattening. Treat as directional, not precise.

maintenance.plan_notes: TIME-DRIVEN, NOT MILEAGE-DRIVEN. Mercedes EQ servicing is 1 year or 25,000 km, whichever comes first. At 7,000 km/year this buyer NEVER reaches the mileage trigger, so every service in all ten years is triggered by the calendar - one visit per year, ten visits total. WARRANTY: 3 years unlimited mileage on the vehicle and 12V battery 2 years unlimited mileage per Mercedes-Benz Taiwan's 原廠保固條款; the HIGH-VOLTAGE BATTERY WARRANTY IS NOW VERIFIED rather than inferred - the 8891 per-trim specification table states 電池保固 8年/16萬km for both the EQB 250+ and the EQB 300 4MATIC (and the same 8年/16萬km for the EQA), which supersedes the original record's inference from a used-car advert. CORRECTED ON REVIEW - THE CONDITIONAL EXTENDED WARRANTY: 8891 shows a Mercedes-Benz Taiwan promotion of 贈2年延保 on the EQB, but it is explicitly 需符合指定條件 and the advertised EQB incentive package is finance-shaped (貸款 150萬60期0利率). The original record simultaneously booked a NT$120,000 CASH discount AND assumed the 2-year extension applied - those are unlikely to both hold for the same buyer. This record no longer assumes free extended cover through year 5: the years 3-5 period now carries a modest out-of-warranty repair allowance, and only years 0-3 are treated as fully covered. BEV vs COMBUSTION: genuinely much cheaper than a German petrol SUV - no engine oil, no spark plugs, no air filter, no DPF, and regenerative braking means pads last far longer. But nowhere near zero: brake fluid every 2 years regardless, HV battery coolant, cabin filter annually, the 12V AGM battery (a notorious EQ weak point that dies around years 3-5 and again around 8-9), and tires that wear faster than on a combustion car because the EQB is heavy (2,105 kg per the official spec) and delivers 385 Nm (39.3 kgm) instantly. TIRE SIZE IS NOW VERIFIED: 235/50 R19 front and rear, so the 19-inch premium fitment assumed in the costs below is correct and the original record's open question on this is resolved. At 7,000 km/year tires are replaced on AGE, not tread - roughly every 5-6 years - so two sets fall inside ten years. Home charger installation is deliberately NOT in these numbers; see assumptions.notes. Per-visit and per-item costs remain class-norm estimates built from Mercedes-Benz Taiwan dealer-rate norms, not receipts: Mercedes-Benz Taiwan publishes no public service price table (its service page directs owners to the 0800-036-524 line for repair-cost information), which is the main weakness in this section and the reason nothing here is rated above medium.

FIRST TIRE SET - 4 premium 235/50 R19 tires, dealer-fitted (~NT$38,000); replaced on AGE not tread at this mileage
12V AGM battery replacement (~NT$14,000) - a well-known EQ-platform weak point
HV battery / power-electronics coolant service (~NT$8,000)

Brake fluid change (year 4)
Out-of-warranty repair allowance (~NT$15,000) - the 3-year factory warranty has expired and the 2-year 延保 is conditional
checkpoints.source: Covers years 3-5 only. REVISED UP on review, from NT$110,000 to NT$125,000. The original record applied no repair-risk loading here on the grounds that the 贈2年延保 extended cover to ~year 5, while simultaneously booking a NT$120,000 cash discount in purchase - but that promotion is 需符合指定條件 and the advertised EQB incentive is finance-shaped (150萬60期0利率), so a cash buyer plausibly does not qualify. A NT$15,000 risk-weighted allowance is now carried for this window instead of assuming free cover. The rest of the period is wear items, which no warranty covers in any case: tire replacement is age-driven (at 7,000 km/year the original tires reach only ~35,000 km but are 5 years old and rubber ages out regardless of tread; the 2,105 kg kerb weight and 385 Nm instant torque also wear tires faster than a comparable petrol SUV), and the rusted-disc item is a genuine BEV-specific failure mode in Taiwan's humidity because regenerative braking leaves the friction brakes barely used. Tire size 235/50 R19 verified from the official spec table. Costs are Mercedes-Benz Taiwan dealer-rate estimates for this class, not verified receipts.

major_items: Two annual EQ services (years 6 and 7) - OUT OF ALL WARRANTY from here
Rear brake discs and pads (~NT$20,000)
HV electric coolant pump (~NT$35,000) - a known wear item on the EQA/EQB platform
Suspension bushings and dampers (~NT$30,000)
Risk-weighted allowance for electric A/C compressor, 12V electrical faults and MBUX/head-unit failure (~NT$20,000)
Brake fluid, cabin filters, wipers
checkpoints.source: Covers years 5-7 only. FULL UNSUBSIDISED COST - the 3-year factory warranty and any 2-year 延保 extension have both expired, so this period carries genuine out-of-warranty repair risk, which is also why the residual value falls steeply here. The electric coolant pump and the electric A/C compressor are the expensive BEV-specific analogues to a combustion car's water pump and belt-driven compressor: fewer of them, but each far dearer at Mercedes dealer labour rates. Deliberately excludes any HV battery work, which is still inside the verified 8年/16萬km battery warranty in this window. Estimated from Mercedes-Benz Taiwan dealer-rate norms and known EQ-platform failure patterns, not from verified receipts - along with year 10 this is the least-sourced part of the record. Unchanged on review.

major_items: Three annual EQ services (years 8, 9, 10), out of warranty
SECOND TIRE SET (~NT$40,000) - again age-driven, ~5-6 years after the first set
Brake discs and pads front and rear (~NT$45,000)
Second 12V AGM battery (~NT$14,000)
HV battery coolant service (~NT$12,000)
Suspension and bushings refresh (~NT$35,000)
Risk-weighted allowance for electric A/C compressor, DC-DC converter, charging-port module, MBUX failure (~NT$60,000)
HV battery diagnostics and module-level risk (~NT$25,000) - the 8-year pack warranty has expired
checkpoints.source: Covers years 7-10 only. The heaviest period by far, and the honest reason a German BEV is not a cheap car to keep: everything is out of warranty, dealer labour rates are unchanged by the car's age, and from year 8 the high-voltage battery has outlived its warranty - now verified as 8年/16萬km from the official 8891 per-trim specification table rather than inferred from a used-car advert as in the original record. A full pack replacement (NT$600,000-900,000+) is deliberately NOT budgeted because almost no owner does it - they sell the car instead, which is precisely the behaviour that produces the ~19% year-10 residual above; only a module/diagnostic risk allowance is carried. Ten-year maintenance totals ~NT$571,000, roughly double a RAV4-class Japanese SUV - correctly reflecting German dealer rates, larger brakes and 19-inch tires, and out-of-warranty electronics risk - while still sitting below an equivalent German PETROL SUV because there is no oil service, no spark plugs and no DPF. Estimated from class norms, not verified receipts. Unchanged on review.

assumptions.notes: Buyer drives 6,000-8,000 km/year, far below the Taiwan average of ~12,000-15,000. Every checkpoint uses assumed_km = 7000 * years (7,000/21,000/35,000/49,000/70,000). At this mileage the Mercedes EQ schedule is entirely TIME-driven (annual, or 25,000 km whichever comes first) - the car never reaches the mileage trigger, so it gets 10 annual services in 10 years. Consumables are age-driven too: 235/55R19 tires harden out at ~5-6 years long before they wear out at 35,000 km, and brake discs on a regen-braked EV in humid Taiwan corrode from disuse rather than wear thin. EXCLUDED BY DESIGN: tax and insurance. ALSO EXCLUDED: home AC charger installation, typically NT$40,000-80,000 in Taiwan for a 7kW wallbox plus building-committee approval and cabling - a real ownership cost but not maintenance, so it appears in no maintenance period. Electricity/charging cost is not modelled. The official list price is already net of the government BEV commodity-tax reduction - verified against the footnote on the official Taiwan spec sheet, which I downloaded and text-extracted myself.

purchase.notes: PRICE VERIFIED - NT$3,000,000 stands, unchanged from the researcher's figure. POWERTRAIN: pure BEV, classified 'bev'. Spec re-verified line-by-line against the official Taiwan PDF rather than taken on trust: 90.56 kWh usable, 587 km WLTP, rear-wheel drive, 245 hp, 2,440 kg kerb. (EV Database lists 265 PS / 2,445 kg for its MY25 EU entry; the Taiwan sheet says 245 hp, and the Taiwan figure governs here.) Not a hybrid of any kind, and no 48V system is involved. KEY SPEC FOR COST: the EQE 300 SUV ships with 舒適型懸吊 (comfort steel springs, code 485) as standard. AIRMATIC air suspension is code 489, a NT$96,000 factory option on the 300 and 350, standard only on the AMG EQE 43. The maintenance model assumes the buyer does NOT tick 489, which removes the single biggest German out-of-warranty risk item; if the buyer options air suspension, the year-7 and year-10 periods must both rise materially. Wheels are 19-inch on 235/55R19 (codes R17/R55), not the AMG's 21-22 inch, which keeps tire cost down for this class. DISCOUNT: NT$200,000 (6.7%). Mercedes EQ models are slow sellers in Taiwan - the SUV lineup shrank to two variants for MY2026 (the AMG EQE 43, listed at NT$4,700,000 on the MY2025 sheet, was dropped), and the official spec sheet itself footnotes a 限時優惠充電方案 charging incentive. NT$150,000-250,000 in combined cash, accessories and charging credit is a realistic negotiated position on standing EQ inventory; middle of that band taken. ONROAD: NT$72,000 = 領牌規費+代辦 ~NT$12,000 plus ~NT$60,000 of accessories (mats, window film, coating, dashcam, charging cables) typical at this price point. Tax and insurance excluded by design.

value_checkpoints.source: CORRECTED BY AUDIT (was NT$2,020,000 private / NT$1,780,000 trade-in). Anchor verified by direct fetch this time, not via search snippet: 8891 listing auto.8891.com.tw/usedauto-infos-4400395.html is a real MY2025 EQE SUV at 車商 (dealer) asking NT$2,198,000, 上極汽車, Taichung - i.e. a genuine ~1-year-old dealer retail price. The researcher escalated that anchor to NT$2,250,000-2,300,000 on the grounds that a MY2026 car is newer than the MY2025 observed; that double-counts model-year freshness, because when this buyer's MY2026 car turns 1 in Aug 2027 it occupies exactly the slot the MY2025 occupies today, competing against MY2027 new cars. Correct method is to haircut the observed figure directly: NT$2,198,000 x 0.88 = ~NT$1,935,000, taken as NT$1,940,000 private (11.7% below dealer retail asking, inside the 8-15% band). Dealer trade-in a further 12% below private = NT$1,700,000. Quoted from low-mileage stock as this buyer does 7,000 km/yr. That is a 32.5% loss against real_cost in year one - correctly front-loaded for a German BEV in Taiwan and far steeper than a Japanese equivalent.

Two direct same-nameplate comparables on 8891, both re-confirmed by this audit at auto.8891.com.tw/mercedes-benz/eqe: a 2024 EQE SUV 300 with 11,000 km at dealer asking NT$2,050,000 (~2.5 yr, = 68.6% of its NT$2,990,000 launch list), and a 2023 EQE SUV 350 4Matic with 31,000 km at dealer asking NT$2,200,000 (~3 yr, on a NT$3,580,000 list = 61.5%). Applying 61.5% to this car's NT$3,000,000 list gives ~NT$1,845,000 dealer retail, plus ~4% for the low 21,000 km = ~NT$1,920,000 DEALER RETAIL. ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: private sale 13.5% below dealer retail (NT$1,660,000), trade-in a further 13% below private (NT$1,440,000). Both listed cars were deliberately chosen low-mileage. NOTE: the direct EQE SUV 300 comparable would imply a slightly HIGHER year-3 value (~NT$1,715,000 private); the more conservative 350-derived ratio is retained because both are thin-market asking prices, and the EQE 300 SEDAN evidence is much weaker (a 2023 EQE 300 sedan with 32,000 km listed 自售 at NT$1,500,000).

Live 8891 listings re-confirmed today: a 2020 car with 30,000 km at dealer asking NT$1,080,000 and another with 36,000 km at the same NT$1,080,000, i.e. 30.9% of original list as DEALER RETAIL at 6 years. Back-projecting that curve to 5 years gives ~37% of list, then +8% relative for the EQE SUV's much better range (587 vs 417 km) and 10-year battery warranty = ~43% of list, ~NT$1,290,000 dealer retail. ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: private 12% below (NT$1,130,000), trade-in 14% below private (NT$970,000). Years 3-5 re-steepen because the 3-year factory warranty has expired and the EQ generation is turning over.

EXTRAPOLATED from the same EQC predecessor proxy (list NT$3,500,000, verified). At 6 years the low-mileage dealer-retail asking is NT$1,080,000 = 30.9% of list. SOURCE CORRECTION BY AUDIT: the researcher also cited a 129,000 km EQC at NT$990,000 as a dealer-retail point (28.3% of list); 8891 in fact shows that car as a 自售 PRIVATE seller, so it is already a private price and the private-equivalent tail is LOWER than the researcher modelled, not higher. That reinforces keeping this checkpoint low rather than raising it. Extending the dealer-retail curve one more year gives ~26-27% of list, plus ~8% relative adjustment for the EQE SUV = ~29%, i.e. ~NT$880,000 DEALER RETAIL on this car's NT$3,000,000 list. ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: private 13% below dealer retail (NT$760,000), trade-in 14% below private (NT$650,000). The tail keeps falling rather than flattening - by year 7 the car is four years out of warranty and the used market is pricing in high-voltage repair risk on an obsolete EQ platform.

PURE EXTRAPOLATION - no German BEV in Taiwan has reached 10 years (the EQC, the oldest, only arrives at 10 years in 2029-2030), so there is no genuine data point and none has been invented. Method: extend the EQC retention curve (30.9% of list at 6 years, from real 8891 dealer listings verified today) to 10 years, which lands near 14% of list = ~NT$420,000 DEALER RETAIL, cross-checked against 10-year-old German luxury cars in Taiwan which sit around 12-15% of list. The BEV-specific penalty is that the 10-year/250,000 km battery warranty expires exactly here, so the year-10 buyer gets zero pack coverage on a 90.56 kWh battery that costs more to replace than the car is worth. ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: private 14% below dealer retail (NT$360,000), trade-in 17% below private (NT$300,000).

maintenance.plan_notes: WARRANTY: 3-year unlimited-mileage Taiwan factory warranty covers REPAIRS only - no prepaid scheduled-maintenance package is assumed standard on the EQE SUV, so the owner pays for servicing from year 1. That is why years 1-3 are low but not zero. (The official spec sheet carries no warranty or service-plan table, so this is an assumption, not a sourced fact - it is why years 1 and 3 are marked low confidence.) The traction battery carries a separate 10-year / 250,000 km warranty with a 70% capacity floor, which runs to the very end of this 10-year window - this is why NO pack-replacement line item appears in any period, and it is the single biggest thing keeping this car's long-run maintenance from being catastrophic. EXTENDED WARRANTY: Mercedes-Benz Taiwan sells years 4-6 cover (C-Class reference NT$42,000 for year 4, NT$77,000 for years 4-5; an EQE SUV would be meaningfully higher). It is NOT assumed taken, so periods from year 4 onward carry the FULL unsubsidised cost. INTERVAL IS TIME-DRIVEN: at 7,000 km/yr the car never hits the 25,000 km trigger, so it is one service per year, every year, for 10 years. BEV SCOPE: no engine oil, no spark plugs, no coil packs, no DPF, no thermostat housing, no 48V starter-generator - none of the usual German combustion risk items apply. SUSPENSION: the standard car runs comfort steel springs (code 485), so no air-strut replacement liability is carried. Note this is a spec assumption, not a universal truth - AIRMATIC is code 489, a NT$96,000 option on this variant, and a car so optioned would need a meaningful air-strut allowance added to years 7 and 10. What replaces the combustion risk items: the electric coolant pump and thermal valve block for battery conditioning, the A/C compressor (which runs a high duty cycle doing battery thermal management, not just cabin cooling), the on-board charger and DC-DC converter, and the 12V auxiliary battery, which on a Mercedes EQ needs coding and is not a cheap part. Tires and suspension wear faster than a normal SUV because the car weighs 2,440 kg. Overall this lands far above a RAV4 but well below a combustion Mercedes GLE - which is the honest answer for a German luxury BEV.

NT$3,310,000 stands — no correction to list_price. Discount and on-road figures are estimates; Taiwan Benz publishes no discount schedule.
purchase.notes: Pure BEV (96 kWh, 320 hp, rear-drive, 693 km WLTP, 2,415 kg, 19-inch wheels) — no combustion content at all, so the 48V/mild-hybrid classification question does not arise. CORRECTED PRICING HISTORY: the previous draft claimed the EQE 350+ launched in TW in 2022 at NT$3,580,000 and was later cut to NT$3,310,000, an 'official price cut of ~NT$270,000'. That is false and has been removed. The 2022 Taiwan EQE saloon lineup was the EQE 300 at NT$3,260,000 and the Mercedes-AMG EQE 43 4Matic at NT$4,820,000 — there was no 350+ saloon in 2022. The 350+ arrived later as the EQE 300's replacement at NT$3,300,000, i.e. NT$40,000 ABOVE the car it replaced (Mobile01: '新加入的EQE 350+為330萬元起，比起過往EQE 300僅小幅增加4萬元'), then +NT$10,000 to NT$3,310,000 for 2026MY. The NT$3,580,000 figure is real but belongs to a different car: the EQE SUV 350 4Matic, launched July 2023. Net: the saloon's official price has only ever gone UP. DISCOUNTS (NT$230,000, 6.9%): raised from the previous draft's NT$180,000. That draft kept the discount deliberately low on the reasoning that an official price cut had already eaten the negotiating headroom — since no such cut happened, that rationale is void. What is left is a slow-selling luxury BEV saloon in a lineup shrunk to one trim, which is exactly the profile that discounts hardest in TW. Composition assumed: ~NT$160,000 cash discount plus ~NT$70,000 of dealer-fitted goods/charging credit. ON-ROAD FEES (NT$80,000): 新領牌照登記 + 代辦 ~NT$15,000 (BEVs pay no 貨物稅), plus delivery accessories typical at this price point — 隔熱紙 ~NT$25,000, 鍍膜 ~NT$20,000, 行車紀錄器 ~NT$12,000, 腳踏墊/迎賓踏板 ~NT$8,000. real_cost = 3,310,000 - 230,000 + 80,000 = 3,160,000.

Nearest real anchors, 8891 (auto.8891.com.tw/mercedes-benz/eqe), read 2026-08-12, both 2 years old and both 車商 asking prices: 2024 EQE SUV 300, 11,000 km, NT$2,050,000; 2024 EQE SUV 350 4Matic, 31,000 km, NT$2,200,000. CORRECTION TO PREVIOUS DRAFT: it scored the first of these against a NT$3,580,000 launch list for 57% retention. Wrong denominator — the EQE SUV 300 launched in TW at NT$2,990,000 (U-CAR, Feb 2024, '正式發表EQE 300 SUV 299萬起'); NT$3,580,000 is the EQE SUV 350 4Matic (July 2023). The saloon trades below the SUV in TW, so I set year-1 saloon DEALER RETAIL at ~72% of list = NT$2,383,000 — above the observed 2-year band, as a 1-year car must be. ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: private sale 12% below dealer ask -> NT$2,100,000 (63% of list); dealer trade-in a further 14% below private -> NT$1,800,000. The 7,000 km reading is well under a normal 1-year car and is already reflected in the 72%. A ~37% first-year loss is still deliberately steep — this is a German luxury BEV in Taiwan, the weakest-retaining combination in this batch — but it is no longer propped up by the mis-derived 57% figure.

REAL EQE saloon listings on 8891 (auto.8891.com.tw/mercedes-benz/eqe), read 2026-08-12. CORRECTION TO PREVIOUS DRAFT — this is the material error in the record. It cited '2023 EQE 300, 32,000 km, DEALER ASKING NT$1,500,000' and then took a further 12.5% off it to reach private sale. That listing is 自售 (private), not 車商 — so the draft double-discounted an already-private price. It also omitted the genuine dealer anchor sitting on the same page: 2023 EQE 300, 75,000 km, 車商 asking NT$1,590,000. Together those two ARE the dealer-vs-private spread: the dealer asks NT$90,000 more on a car with more than double the mileage. Third anchor: 2022 EQE 300 (V295, 241 hp), 40,500 km, 車商 NT$1,556,000. Cross-check: the NT$1,500,000 private figure is independently corroborated by the real 自售 listing above, on a lower-trim car with 50% more mileage. Also removed from this checkpoint's reasoning: the previous draft's claim that the collapse is 'amplified by the official list-price cut from NT$3,580,000 to NT$3,310,000'. No such cut occurred (see purchase.notes). Excluded outlier: auto.8891.com.tw/usedauto-infos-3712829.html, a 2023 EQE at a Taipei dealer (桑尼車庫) asking NT$3,280,000 — verified real but wildly out of line with every other 2022-2023 EQE, and above even the 2023 AMG EQE 53 listings on the same page; treated as stale or mis-specified.

EXTRAPOLATED from the closest real Mercedes BEV in TW at this age — the EQC, since no EQE is 5 years old yet. 8891 (auto.8891.com.tw/mercedes-benz/eqc), read 2026-08-12: 2020 EQC 400 4Matic 運動版, 30,000 km and 36,000 km, both 車商 asking NT$1,080,000; plus a 129,000 km 自售 car at NT$990,000. RETENTION RATIO APPLIED TO THIS CAR: one year earlier on that curve, ~36% dealer retail = NT$1,250,000. ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: private sale 12% below dealer ask -> NT$1,100,000 (33% of list); dealer trade-in 15% below private -> NT$930,000. FULLY EXTRAPOLATED — there is no 10-year-old German BEV in Taiwan to observe, so this is a ratio transferred from a weaker proxy and should be read as such. Proxy: premium BEVs of that vintage on 8891 (auto.8891.com.tw/tesla/model-s), read 2026-08-12: 2018 Model S 75D, 66,000 km, dealer asking NT$998,000, and 2017 Model S 75D, 236,000 km, NT$958,000 — roughly 29% of a ~NT$3,450,000 original list as dealer retail at 8-9 years. Mercedes BEVs trade materially below Tesla in Taiwan (thinner used demand, no charging-network halo, and by 2036 the EQE will be two generations discontinued with a shrinking parts and specialist base), and the HV battery warranty expires exactly at year 10, which is the moment buyers start discounting for a NT$1m+ pack. Dealer retail set at ~19% of list = NT$640,000. ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: private sale 14% below dealer ask -> NT$550,000 (17% of list); dealer trade-in 20% below private -> NT$440,000. The tail keeps falling rather than flattening: -34% from year 7 over three years, a steeper three-year drop than the two-year drop before it. This is the German out-of-warranty pattern, not the Lexus one.

maintenance.plan_notes: WARRANTY FRAME (sourced): Mercedes-Benz Taiwan gives 3 years / unlimited mileage on the whole car, and for the EQE a high-voltage battery warranty of 10 years or 250,000 km with a guaranteed >=70% remaining capacity (cars.tvbs.com.tw/car-news/127611; mercedes-benz.com.tw/passengercars/services/warranty.html). So years 0-3 carry almost no repair exposure, and — unusually for this batch — the single most expensive failure mode, the pack, stays covered right through the 10-year window at this buyer's mileage. NO FREE SERVICING: unlike BMW Taiwan, Mercedes-Benz Taiwan does not bundle free scheduled maintenance as standard, so even in-warranty services are paid out of pocket. An extended warranty covering years 4-6 is sold in TW during the original warranty term; this estimate assumes it is NOT bought, so years 4 onward carry the full unsubsidised cost — if it were bought, roughly NT$60,000-100,000 of premium would move into the 3-5y window and reduce the 5-7y repair allowance. INTERVAL: the EQ schedule is 2 years or 25,000 km. At 7,000 km/year the clock always wins, so services land in years 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10 and are TIME-driven, not mileage-driven — which is why year 1 is nearly free and the even years carry the cost. COST BASIS: no official Mercedes-Benz Taiwan EQ service price table was retrievable and no Mobile01 thread with actual EQE receipts surfaced, so per-item costs are estimates anchored on faqs.tw/ev-maintenance-tw (verified live 2026-08-12). That page prices by brand, and the German column is the relevant one: coolant 5 yrs / 80,000 km at NT$8,000-15,000 for BMW (vs NT$5,000-8,000 Tesla); brake fluid every 2-3 yrs at NT$3,000-5,000 for BMW (vs NT$2,000-3,000 Tesla); brake pads 5+ yrs at NT$15,000-25,000 for BMW (vs NT$8,000-12,000 Tesla); tyres every 40,000-60,000 km, quoted there for a Tesla Model 3 at NT$30,000-50,000. The page states German EV servicing runs '比 Tesla 貴 20-30%'. Note the previous draft quoted these as cross-brand spans (e.g. 'brake fluid NT$1,500-5,000', 'tyres NT$25,000-80,000'); the low ends of those are the Luxgen column and the NT$80,000 tyre upper bound could not be verified on the page — the German column above is used instead. The EQE is heavier (2,415 kg), pricier and larger-wheeled than an i4 and gets no free-servicing offset, so it sits at and above the top of that band. WHY THIS IS NOT A CHEAP EV: BEV servicing really is lower than combustion — no oil, no plugs, no filters, and regen spares the pads — but nowhere near zero. The weight and torque chew 19-inch tyres, brake fluid and battery/drive-unit coolant still have fixed intervals, the 12V battery still dies every 4-5 years, and discs corrode from under-use in Taiwan's humidity precisely because regen means they are rarely used hard. AIR SUSPENSION CAVEAT (UNRESOLVED): I could not confirm whether the TW-spec EQE 350+ carries AIRMATIC. The Yahoo Autos trim page was fetched in full and lists 320 hp, 96 kWh, 2,415 kg, 3,120 mm wheelbase, 19-inch AMG Line wheels and rear-axle steering but is silent on suspension type, and two independent search passes failed to surface a TW spec sheet or owner thread confirming it. The 7-10y figure therefore carries a partial two-corner air-strut allowance rather than a full four-corner replacement; if the car turns out to be on steel springs, cut roughly NT$100,000 from that period.

assumptions.notes: Buyer drives 6,000-8,000 km/year; every checkpoint uses the 7,000 km/year midpoint (7,000 / 21,000 / 35,000 / 49,000 / 70,000 km), roughly half the Taiwan average of 12,000-15,000 km/yr. Consequences: (a) service intervals are TIME-driven, not mileage-driven — Mercedes ASSYST PLUS calls for service at 1 year or ~15,000-20,000 km whichever comes first, and at 7,000 km/yr the year always arrives first, so the owner pays for exactly one dealer visit per year; (b) tires age out rather than wear out, replaced roughly every 5-6 years on date code, not tread; (c) the used comparables quoted are LOW-MILEAGE listings, which sit above the mileage-blind market average, and the source strings say so per checkpoint. Powertrain: the 1.3L turbo (M282) carries a 48V belt-driven starter-generator adding 14 hp — verified via 自由時報. It CANNOT move the car on electricity alone, so it is classified 'gasoline', not 'hybrid'. Excluded by design: 牌照稅, 燃料稅, 強制險 and 任意險, fuel, parking and tolls. No home-charger cost applies (not a BEV). The GLA runs steel springs, not air suspension, so no air-spring replacement is provisioned.

selling_costs.notes: Private-sale scenario, consistent with private_sale_price at every checkpoint. The 過戶 regulatory fee itself is only a few hundred NT$; the rest is the 代辦 fee. Detailing is set at the upper end because a luxury German car with poor presentation gets hammered on price by private buyers. Total sits mid-band for the 6,000-15,000 range typical of this class. Reviewed and left unchanged — this was the soundest part of the original record. If sold to a dealer as a trade-in instead, most of these costs disappear, but so does 13-16% of the price (see dealer_tradein_price).

value_checkpoints.source: SOURCE CORRECTED BY THIS AUDIT. The previous record described the Mercedes-Benz Select anchor as 'a 2025 GLA 200, 4,728 km, asking NT$1,728,000'. I fetched that exact listing (mercedes-benz-select.com.tw detail id=3606) and it is materially different: a 2024/12-build GLA 200 AMG LINE registered 2025/04, 4,728 km, asking NT$1,780,000 — a richer trim, ~16 months old not 12, and NT$52,000 more expensive than reported. Re-derivation on the corrected figures: NT$1,780,000 is a factory-certified retail ASK, the top of the band; ordinary dealer retail is ~6% below at approx. NT$1,675,000. PRIVATE-SALE ADJUSTMENT: private = dealer retail less 13.5% -> approx. NT$1,450,000 (67.9% of real_cost). TRADE-IN ADJUSTMENT: dealer trade-in = private less 13% -> NT$1,260,000. Note the AMG Line comparable is roughly equipment-equivalent to the 摘星版 (pano roof, Burmester), so no further trim correction applied. A ~NT$685,000 loss in year one on a NT$2,135,000 outlay is the steep German year-one hit. Confidence medium: one certified listing, and certified asks are the least representative end of the market.

MODEL-YEAR MIS-AGEING CORRECTED. In August 2026 the 3-year point is the 2023 model year, not the 2024 cars the previous record interpolated from. I re-fetched auto.8891.com.tw and the genuine 2023 listings are: 2023 @ 17,000 km asking NT$1,598,000 and 2023 @ 28,000 km asking NT$1,658,000 — the buyer's 21,000 km sits between them, an unusually good mileage match. The previous record labelled the first as a 2024 car and discarded the second as trim-contaminated. Both asks are likely partly AMG-Line-contaminated (they exceed the ordinary-retail estimate for a 1-year-old car), so I did NOT take them at face value; I treat NT$1,600,000 as an upper bound on dealer retail and set clean-spec dealer retail at approx. NT$1,505,000. PRIVATE-SALE ADJUSTMENT: private = dealer retail less 13.5% -> NT$1,300,000 (60.9% of real_cost). TRADE-IN: private less 13% -> NT$1,130,000. Cross-checked against the clean 2022 @ 22,000 km listing at NT$1,438,000 (4 years old), which brackets this from below as it should. Confidence medium: real listings, but trim contamination forced a judgement call.

DEALER-RETAIL TRAP CORRECTED — this was the central error in the record. I independently re-fetched auto.8891.com.tw and confirmed the anchor listings are genuine: two 2021 H247 GLA 200s at 37,000 km asking NT$1,300,000 and NT$1,298,000. At 5 years that is 7,400 km/yr, essentially this buyer's exact profile, same generation and engine family — the strongest comparable in the record. BUT the previous version reported private_sale_price NT$1,250,000, which is only 3.8% below the observed DEALER ASKING price of NT$1,300,000 for the identical car. The brief requires 8-15%. The inflation entered through ratio laundering: retention was expressed against the 2021 car's lower NT$1,990,000 list, then multiplied by this car's higher real_cost, which silently undid the private-sale haircut. CORRECT CHAIN: dealer retail ask NT$1,300,000 -> private = less 11% -> NT$1,157,000, plus approx. NT$20,000 for the 摘星版's richer equipment (the used market repays only a fraction of a spec premium) -> NT$1,175,000 (55.0% of real_cost). TRADE-IN: private less 13.6% -> NT$1,015,000. Higher-mileage 2021 cars in the same listing set (68,000 km -> NT$1,238,000; 103,000 km -> NT$1,058,000) confirm the low-mileage premium is real and material.

EXTRAPOLATED — the current H247 generation only reached Taiwan in 2020, so no genuine 7-year H247 data exists. Per the brief's method: take the PREDECESSOR X156 at 7 years (2019 cars), express it as a retention ratio of ITS original list, then apply to this car's real_cost — but with the private-sale haircut applied to the OBSERVED price, not laundered through the ratio as the previous version did (it reported NT$1,055,000 where its own stated method yields ~NT$985,000). Real data: FindCar shows 2019 GLA 200 (1.6L, X156) used average NT$968,000 against a NT$2,010,000 new-car reference. I also cross-checked against verified 8891 H247 listings one year younger: 2020 @ 51,000 km -> NT$1,138,000 and 2020 @ 65,000 km -> NT$1,188,000 dealer ask, which low-mileage-adjusted give ~NT$1,090,000 private at 6 years — so ~NT$990,000 at 7 years follows consistently from two independent directions. CHAIN: low-mileage-adjusted dealer retail approx. NT$1,125,000 -> private less 12% -> NT$990,000 (46.4% of real_cost); trade-in = private less 14% -> NT$850,000. Confidence low: different generation, and the mileage correction is a judgement call, not an observed listing.

DEALER-RETAIL TRAP CORRECTED — the previous version reported a private_sale_price of NT$560,000 while the observed 8891 DEALER ASKING prices for 2016 X156 GLA 200s are NT$538,000 @ 54,100 km, NT$550,000 @ 66,000 km and NT$588,000 @ 93,000 km (FindCar average NT$568,000). A private seller cannot beat the dealer's shop-window price; that figure was structurally impossible. CORRECT CHAIN: this buyer's 70,000 km at 10 years sits inside the comparables' mileage band, so NO low-mileage markup is warranted — dealer retail approx. NT$550,000 -> private = less 12% -> NT$484,000, plus a small allowance for the richer original spec -> NT$500,000 (23.4% of real_cost). TRADE-IN: private less 16% -> NT$420,000 (dealer margin percentages widen on cheap old stock). The 7-to-10-year collapse is not modelling pessimism: the observed market really does ask ~NT$550,000 for a 2016 GLA while a 2019 fetches ~NT$970,000-1,040,000, because by then the car is long out of warranty and buyers price in the repair bill modelled below. Confidence low: predecessor generation, single age cohort.

maintenance.plan_notes: AT 7,000 KM/YEAR THE INTERVAL IS TIME-DRIVEN, NOT MILEAGE-DRIVEN. Mercedes ASSYST PLUS calls for service at 1 year or ~15,000-20,000 km, whichever comes first; this buyer never reaches the mileage trigger, so the plan is exactly one dealer visit per year, alternating Service A (minor) and Service B (major). COST ANCHOR VERIFIED BY THIS AUDIT: I fetched the PTT car-board thread directly and confirmed the GLA invoice line items — parts NT$8,164 + labour NT$3,714 = NT$11,878 at an official dealer. That same thread contains a useful corroborating data point for the later periods: a BMW G30 530i at 7.5 years / 110,000 km with a single NT$135,598 bill (labour alone NT$55,012), which is exactly the out-of-warranty German exposure the years 5-7 and 7-10 windows are provisioning for. WARRANTY: 3 years / unlimited mileage, but that is WARRANTY ONLY — scheduled servicing is paid from year one, evidenced by owner invoices paid inside the warranty window, so no early-period subsidy is applied. Mercedes-Benz Taiwan sells an optional 預付式保養套餐 and an optional 延長保固 covering years 4-6; neither is standard and no published pricing was found, so no premium is included and the years 3-5 and 5-7 periods carry the FULL unsubsidised cost. Later periods deliberately provision German-specific risk: the 48V belt starter-generator and its lithium pack, electric and mechanical water pumps, thermostat housing, M282 coil packs, and 7G-DCT clutch/mechatronic exposure. NO air-suspension provision — the GLA rides on steel springs. NO DPF — gasoline car. CHANGED BY THIS AUDIT: ten-year total NT$597,000 -> NT$540,000. Two corrections. (1) Tire sets were priced at NT$42,000 and NT$45,000; a set of four 19in tires for a COMPACT SUV in Taiwan is NT$30,000-36,000, so these drop to NT$34,000 and NT$36,000. (2) The 7-10 year window was NT$335,000, which exceeded the NT$210,000 booked for the same window on the larger, more complex GLC 200 4MATIC in this same dataset — the GLA is a smaller car with smaller brakes, smaller tires and a simpler 1.3L engine, so it cannot cost more; the risk stack was triple-counting low-probability events and is trimmed to NT$285,000. The result is still roughly 1.8x a RAV4 over ten years, which is the correct order of magnitude for an out-of-warranty German luxury compact SUV on Taiwan dealer labour rates.

assumptions.notes: Buyer drives 6,000-8,000 km/year, roughly half the Taiwan average of 12,000-15,000 km/year. All checkpoints use assumed_km = 7000 * years (7,000 / 21,000 / 35,000 / 49,000 / 70,000). Mercedes' service interval is 10,000 km OR 12 months, whichever comes first (confirmed on CW Group's Taiwan Mercedes service guide), so at 7,000 km/year every service in the 10-year window is TIME-triggered and never mileage-triggered: the owner pays for the same number of dealer visits as a 15,000 km/year driver. Low mileage therefore cuts resale loss substantially but saves very little maintenance. Resale figures quote low-mileage comparables where the comparable pool is genuinely higher-mileage than our car, and explicitly decline to apply a low-mileage uplift where it is not (see the 10-year checkpoint, whose GLA comparables average ~71,000 km, essentially identical to our car's 70,000 km). Licence tax (牌照稅), fuel tax (燃料費) and all insurance (強制險/任意險) are EXCLUDED by design and appear nowhere in purchase, maintenance or selling_costs. Fuel/energy cost is also out of scope. This is a steel-sprung compact SUV with no air suspension, so no air-strut replacement is budgeted.

purchase.source: PRICE INDEPENDENTLY RE-VERIFIED AND CONFIRMED — no correction. I read KingAutos article 369615 (2026-07-16) directly, which prints the pre-sale table verbatim: 燃油 GLB 200 (五座) 接單價 215 萬 / GLB 200 AMG Line (七座) 接單價 236 萬 / 純電 GLB 200 electric (五座) 接單價 198 萬 / GLB 250+ electric AMG Line (七座) 接單價 241 萬. I read the TVBS Cars price-and-spec table directly, which gives the same four figures. A third independent search pass confirmed 215萬 is a 預售/接單價 and surfaced no newer 建議售價 announcement. Note the trim requested — GLB 200 in 5-seat form — exists ONLY in this new generation: the outgoing X247 5-seat car was the GLB 180 摘星版 at NT$2,010,000, so the new-generation record is unambiguously the right one to price. Discount and on-road figures are estimates, not quoted numbers.
purchase.notes: POWERTRAIN: 1.5L four-cylinder turbo petrol, 163 hp / 25.5 kgm, 8-speed dual-clutch, plus a 48V mild-hybrid contributing about 30 hp of assist; 0-100 km/h 8.7 s, top speed 208 km/h, kerb weight 1,840 kg (all verified directly on the TVBS spec table). Classified as "gasoline", not "hybrid": this is a 48V mild hybrid (Mercedes' EQ Boost / integrated starter-generator lineage) that restarts, boosts and recuperates but cannot drive the car on battery alone. Caveat flagged rather than buried: on the new MMA architecture the electric machine sits inside the transmission and Mercedes claims limited low-speed electric creep, so this system is at the strong end of "mild" — but it is marketed and warranted as a mild hybrid, so "gasoline" is the correct bucket for this table. PRICE STATUS: NT$2,150,000 is the 預售價 announced 2026-07-16; the official 建議售價 is not yet published and deliveries are quoted from Q4 2026. Final list price could move roughly ±30,000 at launch. DISCOUNT: NT$60,000 is deliberately small. This is a just-announced, first-year-of-generation model still taking pre-orders — the weakest possible negotiating position in Taiwan. Real German discounts at this stage are accessory/領牌 allowances rather than cash off sticker; the deep cuts (the outgoing X247 GLB took NT$80,000-130,000 off in Sept 2025) only arrive once a model is a slow seller. ONROAD_FEES: NT$70,000 = 領牌 + 代辦 admin (~NT$8,000) plus the accessory pack a NT$2.15M SUV realistically leaves the showroom with (mats, window film, ceramic coating, dashcam) at ~NT$62,000. Scales with price; contains no tax and no insurance. real_cost = 2,150,000 - 60,000 + 70,000 = 2,160,000.

selling_costs.notes: Sized for a private sale (自售), which is the disposal route private_sale_price assumes. The statutory transfer fee itself is only a few hundred NT$; NT$2,500 reflects the usual 代辦 handling charge. Detailing sits at the upper end of normal because a luxury-badge SUV that photographs badly loses far more than NT$7,500 in asking price. Third-party inspection is zero because in Taiwan the buyer customarily pays for it. Total NT$12,000 sits mid-band for the 6,000-15,000 typical of this class and is consistent with the other German records in this table. If the owner trades in to a dealer instead, these costs mostly vanish — but so does roughly 14-17% of the price, which is why dealer_tradein_price is tracked separately.

value_checkpoints.source: EXTRAPOLATED — the new MMA-platform GLB has zero used examples anywhere (deliveries start Q4 2026), so every figure here transfers from the predecessor X247, whose 2020 Taiwan launch price of NT$2,160,000 for GLB 200 is within 0.5% of this car's NT$2,150,000, making the retention-ratio transfer unusually clean. Nearest real anchors, read directly off 8891 (2026-08) and all 車商售價 (dealer retail asking): a 2024 GLB 200 AMG facelift with 3,000 km asks NT$1,838,000 and a 2024 with 25,000 km asks NT$1,798,000, both against a facelift list near NT$2,380,000 — i.e. 75-77% dealer retail at TWO years. CORRECTION TO PRIOR PASS: the earlier researcher read 8891's "2.5万" as 2,500 km; it is 25,000 km. The genuine low-mileage 2-year car is the 3,000 km example at NT$1,838,000. Extrapolating one year up gives roughly 84-85% dealer retail at 1 year for a low-km car, then -12% to private sale gives ~74%. I hold at 73.5% (NT$1,580,000) rather than nudging higher because this is a first-model-year car facing an electric GLB sibling listed NT$170,000 BELOW it, which anchors the badge downward. A ~26.5% first-year loss is deliberately far steeper than the ~85% a RAV4 holds and sits inside the German band in this table (65-74%). Trade-in cut a further 14% from private.

Anchored on real 8891 X247 GLB 200 listings read directly (2026-08), all 車商售價: a 4-year-old 2022 GLB 200 AMG 7-seat with 69,000 km asks NT$1,388,000 against a facelift list near NT$2,380,000 (58.3% dealer retail). Interpolating back to 3 years gives roughly 64-66% dealer retail at a mileage-typical ~45,000 km. Our car carries 21,000 km, under half that, so I added ~6% for low mileage to reach ~69% dealer retail, then cut 12% to private sale (60.7%) and a further 14% to trade-in. Result NT$1,290,000 = 60.0% of list at 3 years — materially below the ~75% a Toyota RAV4 holds at the same age. Still inside the 3-year unlimited-mileage factory warranty at this point, which supports the private price.

REVISED UP from a prior pass's NT$1,090,000 — that figure was an openly-admitted 'judgement haircut' below the data rather than a reading of it, and a haircut is not evidence. Critically, these are AMG Line / 7-seat cars whose list was ~NT$2,290,000, NOT the NT$2,160,000 base — using the correct denominator gives 51.9-58.0% dealer retail, averaging ~55.3%, which is LOWER than the prior pass computed. Our car at 35,000 km carries roughly half these cars' mileage, so +7% for low mileage gives ~59% dealer retail; -12% to private sale gives 52.1% = NT$1,120,000; -14.7% again to trade-in. FindCar's reported NT$1,390,000 average for 2021 GLB 200 is noted but not used — it is above every individual listing I could actually see. At 52.1% of list this is consistent with the GLC 200 (51.1%) in this table and above the X3/Q5 (42-43%), which the GLB's real listings do support.

EXTRAPOLATED from the predecessor generation — the GLB nameplate only launched in Taiwan in 2020, so no 7-year-old GLB of any generation exists and none was invented. Proxy is the Mercedes GLA X156, the brand's previous Taiwan compact SUV, launched June 2014 at NT$1,850,000 for GLA 200. On 8891 today a 2019 GLA 200 with 70,000 km asks NT$650,000 = 35.1%. The prior pass described applying '-12% to private' but its stated arithmetic did not actually produce its stated number, so the narrative was wrong even where the figure was roughly serviceable. Correct treatment: 35.1% is a private-sale retention at 7 years and ~10,000 km/year; our car at 49,000 km is lower-mileage still, so +6% gives ~37.2%, and on NT$2,150,000 that is ~NT$800,000. I set NT$820,000, allowing a small upward nudge because the X156's list price had drifted below NT$1,850,000 by 2019, which makes 35.1% a mild understatement of true retention. Trade-in -15%. The step down from year 5 is intentionally the steepest in the curve: the 3-year factory warranty plus a maximum 3-year extension both expire by year 6, after which the Taiwan market prices out-of-warranty German repair risk rather than the car.

EXTRAPOLATED from the predecessor generation, same method as year 7. Real 8891 listings for the 10-year-old 2016 GLA 200 (X156, list NT$1,850,000), read directly 2026-08, all 車商售價: NT$538,000 at 54,100 km, NT$550,000 at 66,000 km, NT$588,000 at 93,000 km — averaging ~NT$558,000 = 30.2% dealer retail. Converting to private at -12% gives ~26.5% private retention. CORRECTION TO PRIOR PASS: it added '+12% for our car's very low 70,000 km' — but those GLA comparables average roughly 71,000 km, essentially IDENTICAL to our car's 70,000 km, so there is no low-mileage advantage to claim at this checkpoint and the uplift was unjustified. Removing it: 26.5% of NT$2,150,000 = NT$570,000, which I shade to NT$560,000 (26.0%) for first-model-year MMA electronics risk and the 48V lithium pack a GLA X156 never carried. Trade-in cut a wider 17% because dealers barely want a decade-old German; many will simply decline the car, so NT$465,000 is close to a floor rather than a market. At 26.0% the tail is still falling, not flattening — the observed German pattern and the opposite of a Lexus. Cross-check: a 2014 GLA 200 at 130,000 km still asks NT$478,000 at 12 years, confirming the decline continues past year 10.

maintenance.plan_notes: COST BASIS: Mercedes-Benz Taiwan dealer rates, grounded in Taiwan sources — A-Service (小保養) roughly NT$8,000-15,000 and B-Service (大保養) roughly NT$15,000-30,000, with one owner-reported Taiwan receipt near NT$55,000 for a comprehensive visit including brake pads and discs. INTERVAL IS TIME-DRIVEN, NOT MILEAGE-DRIVEN: the schedule is 10,000 km or 12 months whichever comes first (verified directly on the CW Group Taiwan Mercedes service guide), and at 7,000 km/year the car never reaches 10,000 km inside a year — so the owner pays for one dealer visit every single year regardless, 10 visits over 10 years, with Assyst Plus alternating A and B services. Low mileage protects resale value; it saves almost nothing on maintenance. WARRANTY: 3 years / unlimited mileage is standard from Mercedes-Benz Taiwan, which is why years 0-3 are cheap — only scheduled servicing and wear items are owner-paid. A paid extended warranty for years 4-6 is offered (typically NT$50,000-70,000); it is deliberately NOT included in any period_cost, because doing so would double-count against the repair allowances budgeted in years 5-7. If the buyer purchases it, treat it as substituting for part of that risk allowance, not adding to it. I found no evidence a free scheduled-maintenance package ships as standard with the new GLB — Mercedes-Benz Taiwan sells 預付式保養套餐 separately — so every period is costed at full retail. NO AIR SUSPENSION on this model, so none is budgeted. WHY THE LATER PERIODS ARE LARGE: years 7-10 carry the electric water pump and thermostat housing (both documented Mercedes four-cylinder failure items), ignition coils, an allowance for the 48V lithium battery and its DC/DC converter, and an age-driven suspension refresh. REVISION NOTE: a prior pass totalled NT$574,000 over ten years by summing every risk item at full value; risk allowances must be probability-weighted, not stacked. Corrected ten-year total is NT$507,000 — still roughly 2.1x the NT$244,000 a RAV4 costs over the same period, which is the intended gap and not an error, but no longer the highest figure in this table's German set despite the GLB being the smallest and cheapest Mercedes SUV in it.

checkpoints.source: Spark plugs at 40,000-50,000 km or on the time schedule (verified directly on the CW Group Taiwan service guide); at 35,000 km this is time-driven. Tires are the clearest low-mileage effect in reverse: 35,000 km would not wear a set out, but 5-year-old rubber must be replaced anyway, so this cost cannot be avoided by driving less. Brake pad cost scaled down from the ~NT$26,000 OEM front+rear figure since only fronts are due; a Taiwan owner receipt reporting ~NT$55,000 for a visit including pads and discs supports this order of magnitude. Warranty expiry per Mercedes-Benz Taiwan's 3-year term.

8-speed DCT transmission oil service ~NT$20,000 (due 40,000-60,000 km)

checkpoints.source: Transmission fluid interval 40,000-60,000 km, verified directly on the CW Group Taiwan Mercedes service guide — at 49,000 km this window is genuinely reached, and it is the one big item our low-mileage buyer hits on mileage rather than time. Dual-clutch fluid service is materially dearer than a torque-converter drain-and-fill, hence NT$20,000. AGM batteries in Taiwan's heat typically last 4-6 years. The NT$25,000 risk allowance is an explicit estimate, not a quote: from year 4 there is no warranty backstop and dealer labour rates apply to every fault. This is the first period where a German meaningfully separates from a Japanese equivalent — the RAV4's comparable window is NT$53,000.

major_items: Three annual services (Y8 A ~NT$13,000, Y9 B ~NT$30,000, Y10 A ~NT$14,000)
Second tire set ~NT$32,000 (age-driven again) and second spark plug set ~NT$10,000

Ignition coils / injectors ~NT$15,000; suspension refresh (shocks, bushings, arms) ~NT$25,000
General electrical, MBUX, A/C and sensor allowance ~NT$13,000
checkpoints.source: Risk-weighted extrapolated budget, not a quoted table — stated plainly. REVISED DOWN from a prior pass's NT$300,000, which summed every named failure item at its full replacement cost as if all of them fire in the same three-year window; an allowance across a probability of failure is the correct treatment, so the 48V pack, water pump/thermostat, suspension and electronics lines are all probability-weighted here. The certain items (three services, tires, plugs, discs, 12V battery) are unchanged and carry NT$133,000 of the total on their own. Item selection follows documented Mercedes four-cylinder weak points and the fact that a 48V mild hybrid carries a lithium pack and DC/DC converter a plain petrol car does not. Age, not mileage, drives almost everything: at 70,000 km the powertrain is barely run in, but rubber, coolant, batteries and electronics have all aged 10 years in a hot, humid climate. NT$240,000 over three years is NT$80,000/year for a decade-old out-of-warranty German SUV, consistent with the observed dealer per-visit baseline plus repairs, and still 2.2x the RAV4's NT$107,000 for the same window.
